- **`Permission denied (publickey)`**: Run `ssh -vT git@github.com` — if a work/corporate key appears before the personal key in the verbose output, `IdentitiesOnly yes` is missing or `~/.ssh/config` is not being read; fix is always in `~/.ssh/config`, not in the agent or IDE config
- **`Could not resolve hostname ssh.github.com`**: Port 53 DNS is blocked; use DoH: `curl "https://cloudflare-dns.com/dns-query?name=ssh.github.com&type=A" -H "accept: application/dns-json"` and add returned IPs to `/etc/hosts`
- **`Connection refused` or timeout on port 22**: Confirm `Port 443` is present in `~/.ssh/config`; test with `ssh -p 443 -T git@ssh.github.com`
- **Wrong GitHub account**: `ssh -T git@github.com` should return `Hi fwornle!`; if it returns a corporate username, add or verify `IdentitiesOnly yes` in the `Host github.com` block

topic: Tmux Proxy Badge Detection
summary:
## Purpose
Displays current proxy status (`P:ON` / `P:OFF`) in the tmux statusline, reflecting whether the local corporate proxy is active. Detection must correctly report `P:OFF` even when the proxy process is still running on its port. The faded/black badge appearance is a confirmed transient rendering state that self-resolves when the proxy recovers, without any code change or service restart.

## Architecture
- **Primary signal**: Presence/absence of proxy environment variables (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, etc.). If unset, proxy is reported as `P:OFF` regardless of port state.
- **Secondary signal (legacy)**: Raw TCP connect to `127.0.0.1:3128` via the health coordinator. Retained but subordinate to the env var check.
- **Why env vars are authoritative**: `px-toggle` unsets env vars but leaves the proxy process running on port 3128; port-only detection produces a false `P:ON` after the proxy is toggled off.
- **Rendering layer**: `combined-status-line.js` handles all badge color, opacity, and state rendering for the LLM proxy indicator.
- **Faded/black badge**: Transient rendering state occurring while the LLM proxy is recovering or temporarily unreachable. Confirmed to self-resolve once the proxy returns to green; the recovery is observable as a green badge without any intervention.

## Key Files
- `combined-status-line.js` — statusline renderer; controls color/opacity for proxy badge state; primary signal path reads env var presence

## Usage
Rendered on every tmux statusline refresh interval. Used by the developer to monitor corporate proxy state without leaving the terminal. `px-toggle` is the intended toggle mechanism; env var presence is the authoritative proxy-active signal consumed by the renderer.

## Troubleshooting
- **Faded/black badge**: Transient — proxy is recovering. No intervention required; badge self-resolves to green once the proxy is healthy.
- **Persistent `P:ON` after `px-toggle` off**: Renderer may be reading port state rather than env vars. Verify `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` are unset in the tmux session and that `combined-status-line.js` uses env var presence as the primary check.
- **Persistent `P:OFF` when proxy is confirmed running**: Check whether env vars are actually exported in the current session (`printenv HTTP_PROXY`); they may not have been propagated into the tmux environment.

topic: OntologyFilter Component — Unified Viewer
summary:
## Purpose
Provides the Ontology Class filter panel in the Unified Viewer, enabling show/hide of graph nodes by ontological classification in an expandable L0→L1→L2 hierarchy. All L1 classes are independently deselectable; toggling a class removes exactly its declared own-node count from the rendered graph.

## Architecture
**Data layer (backend is always authoritative):**
- API emits the complete hierarchy: 1 L0 root, 3 L1 nodes, 10 L2 nodes (14 total filter items)
- All filter defects are frontend-only; re-probing the API confirms hierarchy shape but cannot diagnose state or rendering bugs

**State model — `[]` sentinel:**
- Empty array `[]` is the sentinel for "all items visible" — never "none selected"
- Per-item checkbox handlers in `OntologyFilter.tsx` correctly expand `[]` to the full 14-item list before adding or removing a specific class — this is the **canonical correct materialization pattern** for all filter components

**Group-level operations (all/none buttons):**
- All/none toggle for the Ontology Class category is handled by `selectGroup`/`deselectGroup` in `FilterRail.tsx`, not in `OntologyFilter.tsx`
- Those handlers bypass `[]` materialization — the group-toggle bug lives in `FilterRail.tsx`; per-item logic in `OntologyFilter.tsx` is correct

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/OntologyFilter.tsx` — L0→L1→L2 hierarchy rendering; per-item checkbox state handlers; correct materialization pattern
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/FilterRail.tsx` — group-level all/none handlers (`selectGroup`, `deselectGroup`); contains the group-toggle sentinel-bypass bug
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/store/viewer-store.ts` — Zustand store backing all filter state

## Usage
- Rendered as a panel within the Unified Viewer sidebar
- State is read/written directly through `viewer-store.ts`; no local component state for filter visibility
- Per-item materialization in this file is the reference pattern to replicate when fixing `FilterRail.tsx`

## Troubleshooting
- **Per-item checkbox correct but all/none does not work**: bug is in `FilterRail.tsx` `selectGroup`/`deselectGroup`, not in `OntologyFilter.tsx` — do not modify this file to fix group-toggle behavior
- **Hierarchy item count mismatch**: re-probe the API to confirm 14 nodes (1 L0 + 3 L1 + 10 L2); if the API is correct, fault is in frontend rendering or state
- **L1 class not independently deselectable**: verify the class is represented as a distinct member of the 14-item materialized list; check that `[]` expansion in the per-item handler produces all 14 entries

topic: Online Learning System — Health Status and Monitoring
summary:
## Purpose
The `[📚]` online-learning badge reflects consolidation-layer freshness exclusively — not raw ETM capture activity. Capture writes and consolidation status are fully decoupled; the badge can display stale/cooling/black state for hours while observations flow normally. The confirmed root cause of persistent staleness is a stale-read or race-condition latch in `ObservationConsolidator.js`: `lastObservationAt` fails to advance despite new observations arriving and does not self-heal.

## Architecture
**Badge signal chain:**
- `knowledge.obsAgeMs` ← `lastObservationAt` ← `GET /api/consolidation/status` (`:12436`)
- No signal path exists from raw ETM write activity to `lastObservationAt`; writes to the capture store do not advance this timestamp

**Badge state computation in `combined-status-line.js`:**
- **Line 844**: `auto_heal_status` maps directly to `'cooling'` — drives the black/cold badge color
- **Lines 963–968**: user-activity threshold checks controlling active/cooling/broken state transitions
- `isUserActive()` in the badge renderer gates active/idle rendering; must use **transcript mtime** as its signal; a heartbeat-only check (`lastBeat`) produces false cooling because `lsl_heartbeat` fires unconditionally on every ETM poll regardless of user presence
- `isUserActive()` in the badge renderer is a **separate, independent check** from `userActiveNow()` in the health coordinator; both must be correctly calibrated

**Failure cascade:** Active observations arrive → obs-api receives them → `lastObservationAt` latch fails to advance → badge ages past threshold → `auto_heal_status` → `'cooling'` → badge turns black, while capture continues normally.

## Key Files
- `combined-status-line.js` — badge renderer; `isUserActive()` activity gate; line 844 (`auto_heal_status` → `'cooling'`); lines 963–968 (activity thresholds)
- `ObservationConsolidator.js` — consolidation service; `lastObservationAt` update logic; site of the stale-read/race-condition latch
- `/api/consolidation/status` (`:12436`) — sole upstream source of `lastObservationAt`; only input to badge color computation

## Usage
- Badge rendered in tmux `status-right` via `combined-status-line.js` on every status refresh cycle
- A black/cooling badge does **not** indicate broken capture; it means the consolidation service's timestamp is stale
- A fix to `combined-status-line.js` (`isUserActive` + badge rendering) is queued for commit alongside the coordinator fix, gated on live tmux render verification

## Troubleshooting
- **Badge stuck black while capture runs normally**: `lastObservationAt` latch in `ObservationConsolidator.js` is the root cause; restarting the consolidation service clears the latch as a temporary workaround
- **Badge doesn't recover after restart**: poll `/api/consolidation/status` directly and verify `lastObservationAt` advances with each new observation; static value means the latch is re-triggering
- **False cooling during active work**: confirm `isUserActive()` in `combined-status-line.js` uses transcript mtime, not `lastBeat`; `lastBeat` indicates daemon alive, not user present

topic: Truthfulness Verifier — Insight Claim Verification
summary:
## Purpose
The Coverage page in `system-health-dashboard` visualizes per-project claim verification status using a strict, unambiguous color-to-state mapping. Tiles deep-link to individual insight records using the native km-core UUID `id` as the canonical public identifier. All tile rendering, legend swatches, project-header badge, and deep-link href logic are co-located in a single file.

## Architecture
- **Single rendering file**: all Coverage page visual logic lives in `src/pages/coverage.tsx` within `integrations/system-health-dashboard/`
- **Canonical tile state → color mapping:**
  - `pending` → grey (verifier has not yet run; grey is **reserved exclusively** for this state)
  - `unverifiable` / `no claims` → beige/tan (`totalClaims = 0` or non-repo content); explicit high-contrast Tailwind text/background overrides applied; **intentionally distinct from grey** to prevent visual ambiguity with pending
  - `hallucinated` → distinct non-grey color (claims reference content not present in repo)
- **Legend**: present in page header with swatches for each claim state; legend text uses `text-muted-foreground` Tailwind class, which may produce insufficient contrast on light page backgrounds — a targeted style override is the known remediation
- **Deep-linking**: tile `href` uses the native km-core UUID `id` field as the canonical public identifier
- **Refresh semantics**: the "Refresh" button re-reads cached insight metadata only; it does NOT re-execute the verifier pass

## Key Files
- `src/pages/coverage.tsx` — all tile rendering, color mapping, legend, deep-link href logic, contrast overrides

## Usage
Accessed via the system-health-dashboard UI. Coverage states reflect the last explicit verifier pass, not live computation. The "Refresh" button reloads cached data only.

## Troubleshooting
- **Low-contrast `unverifiable`/`no claims` tiles**: verify the explicit Tailwind text and background class overrides are present in `coverage.tsx` for these tile states; the defaults produce near-illegible white-on-light-grey
- **Illegible legend text on light background**: `text-muted-foreground` provides insufficient contrast against the page's light gray background; apply an explicit foreground color override directly to the legend text elements — this is a known open issue
- **Grey tiles appearing for non-pending items**: grey must be reserved exclusively for `pending`; if `unverifiable`/`no claims` renders grey, the beige/tan override has been removed or overridden

topic: LslTimelineStrip — Timeline Selection and Bucket Matching
summary:
## Purpose
`LslTimelineStrip.tsx` displays LSL coding session ticks in the unified viewer, rendered per-bucket and colour-coded by source provenance. Phase 61 (LSLTIME-01..03) resolved three artificial limits: silent backend data truncation (LSLTIME-01), a 365-day ceiling on the "all" time window (LSLTIME-02), and absent bi-source tick colouring (LSLTIME-03). All three tracks are complete and merged to main.

## Architecture
- **Hook `useLslSessions.ts`**: issues requests to `/api/coding/lsl/sessions`; 365-day "all" window ceiling removed (LSLTIME-02 fix)
- **Hook `useNodeToBucketsIndex.ts`**: builds the node-to-buckets reverse index for tick-to-bucket assignment
- **Backend API post-Phase-61 response envelope**:
  - `source`: `'online'` | `'batch'` — per-session provenance
  - `total`: pre-slice session count (before any cap applied); drives the "showing N of M" badge
  - **D-09 derivation rule (backend-only, locked)**: manual km-core entities → `'batch'`; all others → `'online'`; must NOT be reimplemented in the frontend
- **Bi-source tick colours**: amber (online) and pink (batch) assigned from `source` field in `LslTimelineStrip.tsx`
- **Time ladder**: 24h / 7d / 30d / 1y selectable windows; "all" window no longer capped at 365 days
- **Live verification gate**: correct rendering of badge, ladder, and tick colours requires obs-api to be running with the post-Phase-61 envelope (`source` + `total` fields present)

## Key Files
- `LslTimelineStrip.tsx` — primary component; tick rendering, bi-source colour assignment, time-ladder UI; edited in phase 61 tasks 1–2
- `LslTimelineStrip.test.tsx` — component tests (47/47 Vitest pass after merge)
- `useLslSessions.ts` — data fetch hook; 365-day ceiling removed
- `useNodeToBucketsIndex.ts` — reverse index builder for tick-to-bucket assignment
- `visibility-predicate.ts` — visibility predicate logic for session filtering
- `graph-builder.ts` — graph structure builder
- `61-03-SUMMARY.md` — phase 61 merge summary and sign-off record

## Usage
Rendered in the unified viewer timeline panel. Triggered by node selection in the graph canvas. All 47/47 Vitest tests pass after the phase-61 merge; 3 pre-existing TypeScript errors in `OntologyFilter.test.tsx` are scoped out and are not regressions introduced by phase-61 changes. Live sign-off requires: obs-api running post-restart, "showing N of M" badge correct, all four ladder windows functional, and amber/pink tick colours visible.

## Troubleshooting
- **Amber/pink tick colours absent**: obs-api not returning `source` field — restart obs-api to pick up post-Phase-61 backend changes; verify response envelope includes `source`
- **"Showing N of M" badge missing or zero**: backend `total` field absent — restart obs-api
- **"All" time window still capped at 365 days**: verify 365-day ceiling removal is present in `useLslSessions.ts`; the hook should pass an unbounded window for the "all" selection
- **TypeScript errors in test suite**: errors in `OntologyFilter.test.tsx` are pre-existing and scoped out — do not treat as phase-61 regressions; `vitest` should still report 47/47 green

topic: VS Code SCM Workspace Configuration — Multi-Repo Visibility
summary:
## Purpose
Ensures the main `coding` repo, `.specstory/history` private repo, and all `integrations/` sub-repos are simultaneously visible in VS Code's Source Control panel without triggering enterprise auth failures or repo-list teardowns.

## Architecture
- **Root cause of disappearing parent repo**: The nested `.specstory/history/.git` repo (pointing at a GHE remote) triggers enterprise auth failures that cause VS Code's git extension to tear down the entire repo list when auto-discovery traverses into `.specstory/`
- **Fix**: Explicitly declare all repos as named `folders` entries in `coding.code-workspace` rather than relying on auto-discovery; disable auto-detection in workspace settings
- **Suppression settings** (retain as safety net): `git.repositoryScanIgnoredFolders: [".specstory"]`, `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders: "never"`, `git.repositoryScanMaxDepth: 0`
- **Secondary bug**: VSCode's submodule auto-detection cascade overrides explicit workspace folder registrations — disabled by workspace setting
- **Final state**: `coding.code-workspace` lists all 8 repos explicitly: `coding`, `.specstory/history`, and 6 `integrations/` sub-repos; SCM panel set to parallel display mode

## Key Files
- `coding.code-workspace` — workspace definition; must list all 8 repos as explicit folder entries with auto-discovery disabled

## Usage
Opened as a workspace (`code coding.code-workspace`) rather than a plain folder. All git operations across all 8 repos are accessible from the SCM panel simultaneously.

## Troubleshooting
- **Parent repo disappears from SCM**: Auto-discovery is traversing into `.specstory/` and hitting GHE auth failures — verify `repositoryScanIgnoredFolders` includes `.specstory` and all repos are listed explicitly in `folders`
- **Sub-repo missing from SCM panel**: Not listed in `coding.code-workspace` `folders` entries — add it explicitly
- **Submodule auto-detection overriding explicit folders**: Disable submodule auto-detection in workspace settings
- **SCM shows duplicate entries**: Both auto-discovery and explicit folder entries are active — confirm auto-discovery is fully disabled

topic: Unified Viewer — Filter Infrastructure
summary:
## Purpose
Manages user-controlled filter state for the Unified Viewer, narrowing the rendered graph and footer entity count across multiple categorical dimensions ("Ontology Class", "Project/System", "COMPONENT"). The Zustand store (`viewer-store.ts`) is the single source of truth; all filter components read and write state through it.

## Architecture
- **State store**: `viewer-store.ts` — Zustand store; single source of truth for all filter dimensions
- **Filter dimensions**: "Ontology Class", "Project/System", "COMPONENT" — each independently controlled
- **`[]` sentinel pattern (critical invariant)**: Empty array `[]` means "all items in this category are visible" — never "none selected"; any handler that modifies item-level visibility **must** expand `[]` to the full item list before adding or removing an entry; failure produces incorrect state transitions
- **Canonical reference implementation**: Per-item checkbox handlers in `OntologyFilter.tsx` correctly implement the `[]` materialization pattern — treat as the reference for all filter component implementations
- **Dev server**: Vite dev server runs on port 5173; use `lsof -i :5173` to confirm the active process and working directory before editing filter source files

## Key Files
- `viewer-store.ts` — Zustand filter state store; single source of truth
- `OntologyFilter.tsx` — canonical reference implementation of the `[]` sentinel expansion pattern for per-item checkbox handlers

## Usage
- Filter components in the Unified Viewer UI read active filter state from `viewer-store.ts` and dispatch updates through it
- Graph rendering and footer entity count both derive from the same filter state — changes propagate to both consumers automatically
- New filter dimensions must implement the `[]` sentinel expansion pattern as demonstrated in `OntologyFilter.tsx`

## Troubleshooting
- **Incorrect entity count in footer**: Usually caused by a filter handler that skips `[]` expansion before modifying item-level visibility; audit the handler against the `OntologyFilter.tsx` reference implementation
- **Filter appears to select nothing when toggling from "all visible"**: `[]` was not expanded to the full item list before removal — handler is missing the materialization step
- **Dev server not found at port 5173**: Run `lsof -i :5173` to find the active process; if missing, start Vite from the correct working directory before editing filter source files

topic: gsd-browser Operator Verification Tool
summary:
## Purpose
Browser automation tool backed by a persistent background Chromium daemon, used to smoke-test web UIs — primarily the Unified Viewer and Coverage dashboard — and produce screenshot evidence for operator verification runbooks at phase acceptance gates. The primary mechanism for executing scenario-card checks and generating `{phase}-VERIFICATION.md` artifacts required to formally close a phase.

## Architecture
- **Background Chromium daemon**: long-running process handling all `navigate` and screenshot operations; liveness tracked via a PID file in the gsd-browser state directory.
- **Daemon lifetime independence**: the daemon can terminate independently of the target service or network connection; when down, all subsequent `gsd-browser` calls fail with a **process-state error** — not a network or service error.
- **Service isolation**: target service HTTP reachability and daemon liveness are fully independent failure domains; a service being up does not imply the daemon is up, and vice versa.

## Key Files
- PID file in gsd-browser state directory — daemon liveness tracking; location is gsd-browser state directory (exact path environment-specific)
- `{phase}-VERIFICATION.md` — output artifact; required for formal phase closure

## Usage
- Invoked during phase acceptance gates to execute scenario-card checks against live UI targets.
- Produces screenshot evidence and `{phase}-VERIFICATION.md` for operator review.
- Operator reviews screenshots as part of the verification runbook before approving phase close.

## Troubleshooting
- `gsd-browser` process-state errors mean the Chromium daemon is down — restart the daemon independently; do not troubleshoot the target service first.
- Always check daemon PID file before assuming a service failure: the two failure domains are independent.
- Blank or incorrect screenshots with no error: verify target service is separately reachable (HTTP check), then verify daemon is serving the correct URL.

topic: Cross-Agent Runner — Phase 78 Architecture
summary:
## Purpose
Delivers the autonomous runner engine that spawns each agent binary headlessly, drives experiment matrix execution across variants and repeats, and persists structured Run records for normal, skip, and terminal-state outcomes. Covers requirements RUN-02 (variant encoding), RUN-03 (skip handling), and RUN-04 (terminal-state machine). Provides both a programmatic API and an operator-facing CLI.

## Architecture
**Headless agent layer (`agent-headless.mjs`, ~153 lines):**
- `argvForAgent(variant, task)` — constructs correct argv per agent type
- `resolveAgentBinary(variant)` — maps variant names to on-PATH binaries
- `probeCopilotHeadless(opts)` — requires `-p --allow-all-tools` flags; must be verified before any Copilot headless run
- All four agents (`claude`, `copilot`, `opencode`, `mastra`) confirmed viable for headless invocation

**Runner engine (`experiment-runner.mjs`, ~427 lines):**
- `runMatrix(matrixSpec)` — drives full variant × repeat matrix
- Three-branch cell dispatch for normal, skip, and terminal-state outcomes (RUN-02/03/04)
- Persists structured Run records per matrix cell

## Key Files
- `agent-headless.mjs` (~153 lines) — headless agent spawn layer; binary resolution and argv construction
- `experiment-runner.mjs` (~427 lines) — matrix runner engine; three-branch cell dispatch; Run record persistence

## Usage
- Invoked via CLI or programmatic `runMatrix(matrixSpec)` call
- Drives cross-agent experiment matrices for benchmarking and comparison across agent implementations
- Run records persisted per cell enable post-hoc analysis of variant × repeat results

## Troubleshooting
- **Copilot headless failure**: requires `-p --allow-all-tools` flags — verify via `probeCopilotHeadless()` before any matrix run that includes the Copilot variant
- **Binary not found**: check `resolveAgentBinary()` mapping and confirm target binary is on `PATH`
- **Skip/terminal misclassification**: RUN-03 and RUN-04 logic lives in the three-branch cell dispatch of `experiment-runner.mjs`

topic: Tmux/Worktree Maintenance — Stale Session and Metadata Cleanup
summary:
## Purpose
Provides a safe, repeatable procedure for identifying and cleaning up stale/idle tmux coding sessions and pruning git worktree metadata without disrupting active work or losing in-progress state.

## Architecture
- **Current-session identification**: before killing any tmux session, inspect `TMUX`/`TMUX_PANE` env vars of the invoking shell to identify the "current" session; also check for active peer sessions belonging to other in-progress work — both must be preserved.
- **Session inventory**: enumerate `coding-<agent>-<PID>` sessions (`coding-claude-*`, `coding-opencode-*`, `coding-pi-*`); distinguish idle/stale from current/active peer sessions before killing. A tmux server process itself has been misidentified as a target session in the past — always verify process identity before terminating, and correct any misidentification immediately.
- **Worktree metadata**: `git worktree list` is used to inspect worktrees under `.data/run-restores` before acting. `git worktree prune` only removes metadata for already-deleted directories — it does not delete actual worktree trees, so it is safe to run speculatively but does not accomplish full cleanup on its own.
- Fact-gathering (listing sessions/worktrees, checking env vars) is prioritized before any destructive action; destructive pruning is deferred until state is fully understood.

## Key Files
- No dedicated script identified; cleanup performed via `tmux` CLI (`list-sessions`, `kill-session`) and `git worktree list`/`prune` commands directly.

## Usage
Run periodically or when disk/process clutter is suspected, especially after multiple agent relaunches or crashes. Always performed manually/interactively rather than via automation, given the risk of killing active work.

## Troubleshooting
- If unsure whether a session is active, check `TMUX`/`TMUX_PANE` from within it and confirm recent pane activity before killing.
- If a worktree directory was deleted outside git, `git worktree prune` will clear its stale metadata — but only after directory deletion, not before.
- Always confirm work is preserved on disk (e.g. via `git status`, file timestamps) after killing sessions, not just before.

topic: Staff Feedback Template System
summary:
## Purpose
Defines the full operational workflow for capturing a meeting, producing a transcript, and filing the result into the second-brain vault using the `rapidscribe-meeting` CLI.

## Architecture
- **Stage 1 — Capture**: `rapidscribe-meeting start` invoked via Bash tool call; records audio via ScreenCaptureKit (system-and-mic mode) to a session directory; must verify `RECORDING_IN_PROGRESS` state before ending turn.
- **Stage 2 — Stop & finalize**: `rapidscribe-meeting stop` finalizes the WAV file; may report a stream-stop error/"failed" status even when the underlying `recording.wav` (tens of MB) is intact — transcription can be recovered directly from the audio file in this case.
- **Stage 3 — Transcription & diarization**: run on the session WAV; includes automatic language detection and speaker diarization; if initial pass misclassifies speaker count (e.g. single-speaker when actually two), re-run with forced two-speaker diarization.
- **Stage 4 — Vault filing**: transcript handed to `ef-412-feedback` skill, which files content per EF-412 Feedback File Schema rules into `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/<surname-firstname>/`.

## Key Files
- `~/.rapidscribe/meetings/<session-id>/recording.wav` — captured audio
- `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/<surname-firstname>/timeline.md`, `log.md` — filed output

## Usage
End-to-end pipeline used whenever a feedback/development meeting is recorded for filing against a team member's EF-412 record.

## Troubleshooting
- Stop failures: verify WAV integrity before re-recording (see Audio Capture Failure Recovery)
- Diarization errors: re-run transcription forcing correct speaker count
- Filing errors: cross-check folder name against roster before creating a new EF-412 feedback folder

topic: A2A LLM Provider Configuration — Custom Endpoints
summary:
## Purpose
Defines custom LLM provider endpoints in `opencode.json` for the `a2a` project, controlling which model each agent/job routes to (local clusters, cloud/proxy providers, or external third-party APIs). Routing is manual/explicit per provider entry — no automatic cost- or complexity-aware routing exists.

## Architecture
- Providers declared under a top-level `providers` section in `opencode.json`; each entry is an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint with `baseURL` and `apiKey` fields, following the pattern of the `qwen-local` entry.
- `apiKey` values always reference environment variables (e.g. `OPENCODE_API_KEY`), never hardcoded; `.env` is user-managed, gitignored, and loaded at runtime to inject credentials securely.
- Active session config is locked at startup via `PI_MODEL`/`PI_PROVIDER` env vars (e.g. `PI_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5`, `PI_PROVIDER=rapid-proxy-pi`).
- External third-party API providers are added identically to internal cluster providers — only the `baseURL`/`apiKey` values differ, not the entry structure.
- Adding a new provider requires documenting the associated `.env` variable so users can manually populate their local key.

## Key Files
- `opencode.json` — central provider registry, `providers` section
- `.env` (user-managed, gitignored) — holds actual API keys referenced by provider entries

## Usage
Used by all coding agents in the system to resolve which model endpoint to call. New providers (internal cluster or external API) are added by appending an entry to `providers` and documenting the required env var; no code changes needed elsewhere.

## Troubleshooting
- If an agent fails to authenticate, check that the referenced env var is set in `.env` and loaded at runtime.
- If routing goes to the wrong model, verify `PI_MODEL`/`PI_PROVIDER` env vars at session startup — these lock config for the session.
- Never commit real API keys; confirm `.env` remains gitignored.

topic: A2A API Server — SSE Streaming & Reconnect Behavior
summary:
## Purpose
Serves real-time SSE event streams to browser clients for the a2a dashboard, enabling live session logs, observations, and health metric updates without polling.

## Architecture
- API server serves SSE streams on port **3031**.
- Dashboard/proxy server runs on port **3033**, proxying `/api/token-usage/*` to the LLM proxy on port 12435 and serving the main dashboard UI; repeatedly reverified healthy with SSE streaming functioning correctly.
- An unrelated `llm-proxy.mjs` file defaults to port 8089 — not part of the SSE serving path, and has been repeatedly mistaken for the API server port during health checks; disregard this file when checking API server health.
- `ERR_NETWORK_IO_SUSPENDED` errors in browser clients are caused by client-side OS-level socket throttling, not server failures.
- SSE reconnect logic is implemented client-side and is self-healing by design; these errors are cosmetic noise rather than actionable failures.

## Key Files
- `llm-proxy.mjs` — unrelated proxy defaulting to port 8089; not part of the SSE path, do not confuse with the API server.

## Usage
Consumed by the dashboard frontend for live log/observation/health streaming; any health check of "the API server" should target port 3031 (SSE) and port 3033 (proxy/dashboard), not 8089.

## Troubleshooting
- If health checks report the API server on the wrong port, verify against ports 3031/3033 rather than trusting `llm-proxy.mjs`'s default of 8089.
- `ERR_NETWORK_IO_SUSPENDED` in browser console logs is expected noise from OS socket throttling — do not treat as a server outage; reconnect logic will self-heal.
- Open follow-up directions if revisiting this area: investigate token-usage cost accounting, or implement suppression of the reconnect warning noise in client logs.

topic: Measurement Harness — Agent Band Seams and Spawn Utilities
summary:
## Purpose
Provides a structured harness for spawning coding agents headlessly with explicit complexity-band control, enabling reproducible measurement of token usage and routing behavior across `claude`, `copilot`, `opencode`, and `pi`.

## Architecture
- **Four-phase plan**:

topic: Token Accounting — Dashboard Bugs and Planned UI Enhancements
summary:
## Purpose
Tracks confirmed aggregation bugs in the proxy dashboard's token accounting views and scopes planned UI enhancements for cost visibility, foreground/background filtering, and GitHub Copilot budget tracking.

## Architecture
- **Confirmed aggregation bug**: `SUM` operations in the SQL aggregation layer are incorrectly scoped to fresh/recent data only — the token-filtering predicate governing display filtering is incorrectly also constraining the `SUM` scope.
  - Confirmed affected locations: **Routing tab account totals** and **Subscription card**
- **Planned enhancements (not yet implemented)**:
  - Foreground/background process filter checkboxes (default: both on) on Evolution and Cost views
  - Per-category fg/bg cost breakdown
  - Editable monthly GitHub Copilot budget input
  - Offload savings calculation benchmarked against GitHub's standard pricing model
- **Deployment blocker**: Corporate `rapid-llm-proxy` repo enforces branch protection on `main`; direct pushes are rejected. Requires PR workflow via `gh pr create` and valid GitHub authentication for the corporate GHE instance.

## Key Files
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy` dashboard SQL layer — contains confirmed buggy `SUM` scoping
- `.data/llm-proxy/token-usage.db` — SQLite backing store queried by all dashboard views

## Usage
Dashboard views query the SQL aggregation layer directly. The Routing tab and Subscription card are the confirmed broken surfaces. Planned filter controls will affect Evolution and Cost views.

## Troubleshooting
- **Understated totals in Routing tab / Subscription card**: caused by `SUM` predicates scoped to fresh data only; fix requires correcting the SQL aggregation scope in the dashboard layer.
- **Cannot push fix directly**: branch protection on `rapid-llm-proxy` `main` requires a feature branch + PR; ensure GHE authentication (`gh auth login` against corporate GHE) is configured before attempting `gh pr create`.
- **Prioritization**: UI enhancements are explicitly deferred pending branch protection resolution and user sign-off on priority order.

topic: Budapest Flat Balance Project
summary:
## Purpose
Tracks and reconciles financial transactions for a Budapest flat using an Excel workbook as the canonical ledger and a Python script for automated parsing and data transfer from bank statement PDFs.

## Architecture
- Bank statement PDFs are the source of transaction data, parsed via Python (`pdfplumber` or similar) and written to the workbook via `openpyxl`.
- `reconcile.py` is the primary automation script; supports a `--dry-run` flag for safe inspection before writing.
- No "balance skill" component is currently implemented in `reconcile.py`.
- Workbook filenames follow a date-prefix convention (e.g. `260124-1104_Balance.xlsx`).
- Git-managed project on `main` branch; feature branches used for script fixes (fast-forward merge pattern); `origin/main` may lag local `main` if pushes are deferred.

## Key Files
- `Balance.xlsx` — main ledger workbook; updated with parsed transaction data
- `reconcile.py` — reconciliation/parsing script; primary entry point for automation
- Bank statement PDFs — source input; stored alongside the workbook in the project directory

## Usage
Run `reconcile.py --dry-run` against a target workbook to inspect parsed transactions before committing changes. Full run writes parsed PDF transactions into `Balance.xlsx`. Feature branches are used for script changes and fast-forward merged into `main`.

## Troubleshooting
- If a session ends before data transfer completes, the workbook remains unmodified — always verify with `--dry-run` before assuming data was written.
- Unmapped entries surface during dry-run; investigate `reconcile.py` mapping logic to handle new transaction formats.
- If `origin/main` lags local `main`, an explicit `git push` is needed; feature branches should be deleted after merge to avoid stale refs.

topic: Other Activity UI — Pagination and Split-Pane Layout
summary:
## Purpose
Replaces endless scroll in the "Other activity" section with discrete pagination and restructures the view into a horizontal split-pane so the selection panel and turns detail pane are simultaneously visible.

## Architecture
- **Pagination**: the "Other activity" list uses page-based navigation instead of infinite scroll; implemented in the `runs-table` component.
- **Split-pane layout**: left pane holds experiments list + paginated "Other activity"; right pane shows turns detail for the selected item; both panes remain visible simultaneously. (Tracked as a future implementation task — not yet implemented.)
- **Layout constraint**: narrower table width required for pagination controls is verified not to clip right-hand columns (confirmed via DOM inspection; all 5/5 layout specification tests pass).

## Key Files
- `runs-table.tsx` — primary component; pagination controls implemented here; layout specification tests live alongside this component.

## Usage
Consumed by the experiments/runs view. Pagination controls appear below the "Other activity" list. Split-pane layout will place this panel on the left with the turns detail pane on the right.

## Troubleshooting
- If right-hand columns appear clipped after pagination changes, re-run layout specification tests (`runs-table` test suite, expect 5/5 pass) and inspect table width via DOM.
- Split-pane layout is not yet implemented; any rendering of a side-by-side detail pane is pending the tracked task.

topic: Playwright E2E Performance Tests — Context Block Legibility
summary:
## Purpose
Validates that context block category detail items render correctly and that interactive elements in the KB drill-down UI (working memory, insights, entities) remain accessible after code changes to helpers or the `cat-samples` renderer.

## Architecture
- Single spec file executed directly via Playwright CLI
- **tool_use card scoping**: `details` element queries must be scoped to a testid-anchored parent on the `tool_use` card. Without scoping, the selector matches the first `details` in the DOM — which belongs to a `thinking` block — causing node mismatch assertion failures. A testid was added to the card to enable correct parent scoping.
- **KB drill-down regression coverage**: working memory, insights, and entities elements in the KB drill-down UI can lose clickability after edits to helpers or the `cat-samples` renderer. The spec navigates into retrieval capture data to isolate which code change breaks interactive element accessibility.
- Root cause of KB clickability loss is under active investigation; `cat-samples` renderer and helper changes have been partially ruled out via targeted spec runs.

## Key Files
- `context-block-legibility.spec.ts` — primary spec covering tool_use card detail rendering and KB drill-down interactive element accessibility

## Usage
Run via Playwright CLI against the system health dashboard or context-block UI. Triggered when changes touch helpers, the `cat-samples` renderer, or any component in the KB drill-down view.

## Troubleshooting
- **`details` selector matches wrong element**: ensure the query is scoped to the tool_use card's testid parent, not the document root — the `thinking` block's `details` appears first in DOM order.
- **KB elements lose clickability**: run the KB drill-down regression spec in isolation; navigate into retrieval capture data to identify the precise interactive element accessibility failure. If `cat-samples` renderer and helper changes are ruled out, inspect the drill-down component's event binding or overlay z-index changes.

topic: Opencode Splice Config — agent_pre_launch Test Suite
summary:
## Purpose
Validates that `agent_pre_launch` renders the correct splice configuration shape for opencode, covering the canonical default blob and all provider-naming paths.

## Architecture
- **Canonical default**: `{}` is the authoritative empty-object default blob for splice config
- **Primary config path**: `_oc_splice_config` is the primary rendering path through `agent_pre_launch`
- **Invariant guards**: two invariants enforced — `INSIDE_CN` identity guard and trailing-comma guard defending the empty-object branch
- **Negative controls**: each invariant must fail independently when source is broken; negative controls confirm isolation
- All rendering paths through `agent_pre_launch` must be covered; provider-naming assertions validate modern rendering shapes

## Key Files
- `tests/agents/` — splice test suite (18 tests); contains provider-naming assertions and invariant tests

## Usage
Run as part of the standard agent test suite. All 18/18 tests must pass. Triggered on any change to `agent_pre_launch` or splice config rendering logic.

## Troubleshooting
- If provider-naming assertions fail, verify assertions match modern rendering shapes (not legacy names)
- If invariant tests fail, check that `INSIDE_CN` identity and trailing-comma guards are independently broken by source corruption — each must fail in isolation
- Suite target: 18/18 passing; fewer indicates stale assertions or a rendering regression in `agent_pre_launch`

topic: LLM Proxy Health — Statusline vs Dashboard Desynchronization
summary:
## Purpose
The statusline and dashboard consume LLM proxy health state through independent mechanisms, causing observable desynchronization during recovery transitions where the dashboard shows healed while the statusline still shows degraded.

## Architecture
- **Dashboard path**: reads LLM proxy health through its own polling/reporting mechanism — transitions reflect live state promptly
- **Statusline path**: reads LLM proxy health through a separate mechanism that applies anti-oscillation/damping logic
- **Damping logic location**: `scripts/` file, approximately lines 530–600 — intentionally delays statusline state transitions to suppress flapping
- The damping delay prevents rapid toggling but produces visible desynchronization during genuine recovery events

## Key Files
- `scripts/` (lines ~530–600) — anti-oscillation logic governing statusline LLM proxy state transitions
- `kb-ab-discrimination-report.mjs` — diagnostic script used to capture the state gap during proxy recovery

## Usage
Observed whenever the LLM proxy at `localhost:12435` recovers from a degraded state. Dashboard consumers will show healthy before the statusline clears. This is expected behavior, not a bug.

## Troubleshooting
- If statusline shows degraded but `curl localhost:12435/health` returns 200, the damping window has not yet elapsed — wait for the transition delay in `scripts/` lines ~530–600 to expire
- If desynchronization persists beyond expected damping window, inspect the damping logic directly for stuck state or misconfigured thresholds

topic: Local Qwen Provider — opencode Integration via llama.cpp
summary:
## Purpose
Provisions a local Qwen3-27B inference server via llama.cpp and registers it as a named provider (`qwen-local`) in opencode, enabling fully local model use without Docker or remote HGA dependencies.

## Architecture
- **Port**: 8081 — chosen to avoid Docker's default 8080 and the existing remote HGA provider
- **Launcher**: `~/opt/llama.cpp/start-qwen.sh` with three variants: `default` (32K context, Q8_0 KV cache), `fast`, and `think`
- **Provider registration**: model visible in opencode as `qwen-local/qwen3.8-27b-local`
- **Process management**: server launched under `nohup` for persistence across terminal sessions
- **Reasoning mode**: `-rea off` / `-no-cnv` flags are essential for coding tasks; omitting them degrades output quality
- **HGA provider**: unnecessary on unified-memory Macs — the 16 GB VRAM constraint HGA was designed to address does not apply to unified memory hardware

## Key Files
- `~/opt/llama.cpp/start-qwen.sh` — launcher script with `default`, `fast`, and `think` variants

## Usage
Start the server via `start-qwen.sh` (default variant recommended for coding). Invoke via `opencode run --model qwen-local/qwen3.8-27b-local`. Health check: server returns `PROVIDER OK` (exit code 0) when ready.

## Troubleshooting
- **`--flash-attn` flag**: requires careful quoting/placement in the launcher script; shell flag parsing issues were encountered during initial provisioning — verify flag syntax if server fails to start
- **Port conflict**: confirm ports 8080 (Docker) and existing remote HGA provider port are not 8081 before launching
- **Reasoning mode**: always pass `-rea off` / `-no-cnv` for coding tasks; default server variant includes this

topic: LSL Markdown Parser and Pi Session Writer — Backfill Pipeline
summary:
## Purpose
The ETM daemon applies redaction patterns to transcript content before writing observation records. A pre-flight validation gate confirms pattern correctness and quarantine behavior before any write operation proceeds.

## Architecture
- **Three sync points**: redaction patterns exist in three places that must be kept in sync — a Python implementation, a Node.js implementation, and `redaction-patterns.json`
- **Catastrophic backtracking hazard**: unbounded character class repetition (e.g. `[a-zA-Z0-9+/]{8,}`) combined with adjacent quantifiers causes superlinear/exponential backtracking on large inputs (~246 ms per 200 KB; >300 s on 400 KB)
- **Confirmed fix pattern**: bound all character class repetitions with an explicit upper limit (e.g. `[a-zA-Z0-9/]{8,64}`); also remove `+` from leading character classes in patterns like `aws_secret_standalone`
- **SHA redaction precision**: the SHA/git commit ID pattern uses a **negative lookahead/lookbehind** to preserve lowercase-only hex sequences (e.g., `refs/heads/main`) while still catching mixed-case tokens and keys containing `+`/`/`; fix applied to both `redaction-patterns.json` and the `ConfigurableRedactor` fallback table
- **Backfill behavior**: configured to preserve existing redacted placeholders and apply new patterns forward only; does not retroactively alter previously redacted content

## Key Files
- `redaction-patterns.json` — primary pattern list; must be kept in sync with both language implementations
- `~/Agentic/coding/.specstory/config/redaction-patterns.json` — specstory-specific pattern config
- `ConfigurableRedactor` class — Node.js implementation; owns fallback table; must match JSON config

## Usage
Invoked by the ETM daemon on every observation record before DB write. Backfill operations across multi-repo corpora (~22k files) use the same patterns. Pre-flight dry-run validates pattern behavior before any `--write --commit` phase.

## Troubleshooting
- **Regex performance regression**: benchmark patterns against 200 KB and 400 KB inputs; superlinear timing indicates unbounded quantifier — add upper bound
- **False preservation of git refs**: if `refs/heads/main` is being redacted, the negative lookahead/lookbehind on the SHA pattern is missing or misconfigured
- **Test suite**: must hold at 5 pass / 0 todo with all assertions substantive; a `todo` placeholder indicates an unverified redaction case
- **Sync drift**: if behavior differs between Python and Node.js implementations, diff both against `redaction-patterns.json` as the source of truth

metadata.summary:
## Purpose
The ETM daemon applies redaction patterns to transcript content before writing observation records. A pre-flight validation gate confirms pattern correctness and quarantine behavior before any write operation proceeds.

## Architecture
- **Three sync points**: redaction patterns exist in three places that must be kept in sync — a Python implementation, a Node.js implementation, and `redaction-patterns.json`
- **Catastrophic backtracking hazard**: unbounded character class repetition (e.g. `[a-zA-Z0-9+/]{8,}`) combined with adjacent quantifiers causes superlinear/exponential backtracking on large inputs (~246 ms per 200 KB; >300 s on 400 KB)
- **Confirmed fix pattern**: bound all character class repetitions with an explicit upper limit (e.g. `[a-zA-Z0-9/]{8,64}`); also remove `+` from leading character classes in patterns like `aws_secret_standalone`
- **SHA redaction precision**: the SHA/git commit ID pattern uses a **negative lookahead/lookbehind** to preserve lowercase-only hex sequences (e.g., `refs/heads/main`) while still catching mixed-case tokens and keys containing `+`/`/`; fix applied to both `redaction-patterns.json` and the `ConfigurableRedactor` fallback table
- **Backfill behavior**: configured to preserve existing redacted placeholders and apply new patterns forward only; does not retroactively alter previously redacted content

## Key Files
- `redaction-patterns.json` — primary pattern list; must be kept in sync with both language implementations
- `~/Agentic/coding/.specstory/config/redaction-patterns.json` — specstory-specific pattern config
- `ConfigurableRedactor` class — Node.js implementation; owns fallback table; must match JSON config

## Usage
Invoked by the ETM daemon on every observation record before DB write. Backfill operations across multi-repo corpora (~22k files) use the same patterns. Pre-flight dry-run validates pattern behavior before any `--write --commit` phase.

## Troubleshooting
- **Regex performance regression**: benchmark patterns against 200 KB and 400 KB inputs; superlinear timing indicates unbounded quantifier — add upper bound
- **False preservation of git refs**: if `refs/heads/main` is being redacted, the negative lookahead/lookbehind on the SHA pattern is missing or misconfigured
- **Test suite**: must hold at 5 pass / 0 todo with all assertions substantive; a `todo` placeholder indicates an unverified redaction case
- **Sync drift**: if behavior differs between Python and Node.js implementations, diff both against `redaction-patterns.json` as the source of truth

topic: ETM Log Archival — Size Management and Post-Archival Review
summary:
## Purpose
Periodic log archival compresses accumulated ETM daemon logs to manageable size. Post-archival git review across all tracked project repositories confirms staged state is clean before committing.

## Architecture
- **Archival effect**: log files accumulate to ~130 MB between archival runs; archival reduces to ~8 MB
- **Trigger**: a task notification confirms the respawned ETM instance has written its log before archival begins
- **Post-archival check**: `git status` and diff review run across all four active project repositories after archival to confirm changes are staged correctly before commit
- **Health signal**: all four repositories reporting clean staged state is the expected post-archival condition; the review pass is observational and preparatory — no files are modified during it

## Key Files
- ETM daemon log (accumulated JSONL output from `enhanced-transcript-monitor.js`)

## Usage
Triggered by a task notification confirming the respawned ETM instance has written its log. The post-archival git review is a standard pre-commit gate, not an autonomous operation.

## Troubleshooting
- If the task notification does not fire, the ETM instance may not have respawned cleanly — check process state before archiving
- If any repository reports unexpected unstaged changes post-archival, investigate whether the archival operation itself touched tracked files

topic: VS Code SCM Panel — Nested Repo Detection
summary:
## Purpose
Explains why a nested git repository (such as a project's private `.specstory/history/.git` history repo) fails to appear in VS Code's Source Control panel even though it is correctly configured and listed in the workspace file, and how to fix it.

## Architecture
- VS Code's automatic repository detection is controlled by the `git.autoRepositoryDetection` setting; when set to `false`, VS Code does not dynamically re-scan the workspace for newly created git repos after the window opens.
- If a nested repo is created **after** the workspace was already opened — as happens when a history repo is freshly initialized during a migration — VS Code never binds it as a tracked SCM repository, regardless of correct `.code-workspace` configuration.
- This is a timing/detection issue, not a configuration or repository-integrity problem; the nested repo is fully functional via CLI even while invisible in SCM.

## Key Files
- `.code-workspace` — must list the nested repo path under `folders`
- VS Code `settings.json` — `git.autoRepositoryDetection` controls dynamic scanning

## Usage
Affects any workflow where a nested `.git` repo is initialized mid-session inside an already-open VS Code workspace.

## Troubleshooting
- **Repo not visible in SCM**: reload the VS Code window (`Developer: Reload Window`) after the nested repo is initialized; this forces a fresh repo scan.
- **Persistent invisibility**: set `git.autoRepositoryDetection` to `true` or `subFolders` and reload.

topic: OpenCode Configuration
summary:
## Purpose
Configures a local Qwen HGA endpoint (`http://10.143.241.223:8080/v1`) as an OpenCode provider, enabling both the native `opencode` CLI and the `coding --opencode` wrapper to use self-hosted models.

## Architecture
- Single config file registers the HGA provider with base URL and auth token
- Four model variants (base, fast, normal, deep) control reasoning depth and token budgets: 512–4096 thinking tokens, 384–4608 output tokens
- API key loaded from `~/.secrets/hga-api-key` (mode 600); path is user-specific — never hardcode another user's home directory
- Model selection and proxy bypass overridable via environment variables: `CODING_OPENCODE_MODEL=hga/qwen3.8-27b-hga coding --opencode`
- Endpoint connectivity depends on VPN access; verify reachability before assuming models are available

## Key Files
- `config/agents/opencode.sh` — primary config; defines HGA provider registration and all model variants
- `~/.secrets/hga-api-key` — developer-specific API key; gitignored, mode 600

## Usage
Invoke via `coding --opencode` or the native `opencode` CLI. Override the active model with `CODING_OPENCODE_MODEL=hga/<variant>`. The four variants trade off speed vs. reasoning depth; use `deep` for complex tasks (4096 thinking tokens, 4608 output tokens) and `fast` for quick iterations (512 thinking tokens, 384 output tokens).

## Troubleshooting
- **Connection refused / timeout**: endpoint requires VPN; confirm tunnel is active and `http://10.143.241.223:8080/v1` is reachable before debugging model config
- **Auth failures**: confirm `~/.secrets/hga-api-key` exists, is mode 600, and contains the correct key — do not use a colleague's key path
- **Wrong model loading**: check `CODING_OPENCODE_MODEL` env var; unset it to fall back to the configured default

topic: Vault Memory System
summary:
## Purpose
Maintains cross-session continuity for the vault and coding projects via LSL memory files indexed by `MEMORY.md`, allowing full project state to be restored at the start of each session.

## Architecture
- `MEMORY.md` acts as a flat index listing active memory files with one reference line each
- Individual `.md` memory files cover specific tasks or workstreams; stored in a memory/continuity directory
- Spans multiple projects (vault, coding); all listed files are loaded at session start
- Stale or completed task memories are deleted outright and their reference line removed from `MEMORY.md`
- Currently one active entry: the HGA opencode endpoint note

## Key Files
- `MEMORY.md` — top-level index of active memory files; edit to add/remove entries
- Individual task `.md` files — created per workstream; deleted when the task is complete

## Usage
At session start, read `MEMORY.md` to identify which memory files to load, then read each listed file to restore project state. To retire a memory, delete the `.md` file and remove its line from `MEMORY.md`. To add a new workstream, create a `.md` file and add a reference line to `MEMORY.md`.

## Troubleshooting
- **Stale entries**: if a listed file no longer exists or its task is complete, delete the file and remove the reference line from `MEMORY.md` to avoid confusion at next session load
- **Missing context at session start**: ensure all files listed in `MEMORY.md` are actually read — partial loads leave project state incomplete
- **Orphaned files**: memory files not listed in `MEMORY.md` will not be loaded; always add the reference line when creating a new memory file

topic: Submodule Rename — mcp-server-* to semantic-analysis / constraint-monitor
summary:
## Purpose
Migrates both MCP submodules from their legacy `mcp-server-semantic-analysis` / `mcp-server-constraint-monitor` identities to the canonical short names `semantic-analysis` and `constraint-monitor`, and removes all CN mirror infrastructure to consolidate on a single public GitHub remote.

## Architecture
**Rename scope — files requiring update:**
- **Runtime-breaking**: `.gitmodules`, `.git/config`, `Dockerfile`, TypeScript import at `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/components/workflow/constants.ts:27`
- **Silent failures**: `test-coding.sh` existence guards that check old directory names
- **Hook paths**: `~/.claude/settings.json` — hook paths reference old submodule directory names and must be migrated
- **Known bug**: `start-services.sh` lines 102 and 110 contain a wrong repo-name reference requiring correction alongside the rename
- **Prose/docs**: `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh`, submodule-internal `package.json`, `README.md`, and docs

**CN mirror removal scope:**
- Environment variables, shell conditionals, and alternate URLs in `install.sh` — all consolidated onto the single public GitHub remote under the `fwornle` organization

## Key Files
- `.gitmodules` — declares submodule paths and remote URLs; must be updated first
- `.git/config` — local remote registrations for each submodule
- `Dockerfile` — references old submodule directory names
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/src/components/workflow/constants.ts:27` — TS import using legacy path
- `start-services.sh:102,110` — contains wrong repo-name bug to fix alongside rename
- `install.sh` / `uninstall.sh` / `test-coding.sh` — CN mirror conditionals and old directory existence guards
- `~/.claude/settings.json` — hook paths referencing old submodule directory names
- `~/.claude/plans/lively-swinging-eich.md` — task tracking file for this operation

## Usage
This is a one-time migration operation. After completing all file updates, submodule remotes must be re-pointed to the renamed GitHub repositories under `fwornle` org. The GitHub repository rename for `semantic-analysis` was initiated; `constraint-monitor` rename follows the same pattern.

## Troubleshooting
- **`test-coding.sh` silently passes/fails**: existence guards use old directory names — update to new names or tests will silently skip
- **TypeScript build errors**: check `constants.ts:27` import path first; it is the only TS import site flagged as runtime-breaking
- **Hook not firing after rename**: confirm `~/.claude/settings.json` hook paths reflect new directory names; old paths silently do nothing
- **`start-services.sh` service launch failures**: lines 102 and 110 contain a pre-existing wrong repo-name bug — fix these alongside the rename to avoid confusing the two issues

topic: A/B Experiment Cell — Knowledge Injection and Sandbox Neutralization
summary:
## Purpose
The `auto-measure-foreground` and `measurement-reconciler` launchd services write measurement data in the background and must be stopped during active kb-ab experiment task sequences to prevent interference with controlled cell execution.

## Architecture
- Both services are managed via `launchd` and can be queried for state at any time.
- Services are intentionally stopped while any task in the kb-ab sequence is active — this is expected, not a failure condition.
- An EXIT trap handler in the kb-ab sequence script automatically restores both services upon completion of the full task sequence (confirmed to fire on clean code-0 exits), requiring no manual intervention.
- **Completion triggers (dual)**: a direct monitor on the `RE4 COMPLETE` signal plus a fallback process-death detector on the runner PID — whichever fires first delivers the completion ping with smoke-spec verdict and final metrics.
- A process-death backstop runs alongside a `RE4 COMPLETE` log watcher to prevent false "still running" states from blocking the completion ping under hard-kill scenarios.
- The 4-task `kb-ab` pipeline (`kb-ab-etm-crashloop` × 6 cells, `retrieval-service`, `smoke-spec-snapshot-restore-km-core-blockers`, plus report generation) runs sequentially under the EXIT-trap wrapper.

## Key Files
- kb-ab sequence script — contains EXIT trap that restores both launchd services on exit
- launchd plists for `auto-measure-foreground` and `measurement-reconciler`

## Usage
Triggered whenever the kb-ab experiment pipeline executes. The dual completion trigger setup (RE4 signal + process-death fallback) is configured once per run session; no additional setup is required.

## Troubleshooting
- If services appear stopped outside of an active kb-ab run, check whether a prior run exited uncleanly (EXIT trap may not fire on SIGKILL).
- If no completion ping arrives, verify both triggers are active: check the RE4 log watcher and confirm the runner PID is still registered with the process-death detector.
- Services can be manually restarted via `launchctl` if the EXIT trap failed to restore them.

topic: deploy-docs CI/CD Workflow — MkDocs Publication Pipeline
summary:
## Purpose
Publishes documentation changes from the `coding` repository to the MkDocs-based GitHub Pages site at `fwornle.github.io/coding`. Triggered selectively to avoid unnecessary rebuilds on code-only changes.

## Architecture
- **Trigger gate**: workflow path filter watches both `docs/` and `docs-content/`; watching only `docs-content/` silently skips builds when symlink targets in `docs/` change — gate must cover both paths.
- **Job structure**: `gate` → `build` → `deploy` sequence; a `freshness` job runs only when the build is skipped (no redundant execution when build succeeds).
- **Freshness guard**: independent CI job detects stale deployments that slip past gate-pattern failures by inverting trust from path patterns to content invariants.
  - Computes a content manifest via `docs-manifest.sh` (shared between build and verification sides).
  - Compares `.docs-manifest` against tracked hashes; passes cleanly on non-docs pushes.
  - Manifest hashing must not include the manifest file itself (self-referential hash invalidation).
- **Deployment verification**: live manifest hash on GitHub Pages is compared against local state; all deep-page images must render correctly post-deploy.

## Key Files
- `.github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml` — workflow definition
- `docs-manifest.sh` — shared manifest computation script
- `.docs-manifest` — tracked manifest hash file

## Usage
Triggered automatically on push to `main` when files under `docs/` or `docs-content/` change. Manual verification: compare live manifest hash at the published URL against local `.docs-manifest`.

## Troubleshooting
- **Build silently skipped**: check that the path filter includes both `docs/` and `docs-content/`.
- **Stale deployment**: freshness job will flag mismatch between `.docs-manifest` and live site hash — re-trigger the build job manually.
- **Deep-page images missing**: confirm PNGs are in `docs-content/images/` and committed before the deploy run.
- **Manifest hash drift**: ensure `docs-manifest.sh` excludes `.docs-manifest` itself from the hash input.

topic: Graphify MCP Endpoint (supervisord Service)
summary:
## Purpose
Graphify exposes a code-graph MCP endpoint consumed by agents and the code-graph registry. It runs as a long-lived service managed by supervisord.

## Architecture
- The supervisord program name is `graphify`.
- The service is launched via `/usr/local/bin/graphify-serve.sh`.
- The listening port is controlled by `GRAPHIFY_MCP_PORT`, defaulting to **3851**.
- Registered in `config/code-graph.json` with transport type `http`.

## Key Files
- `/usr/local/bin/graphify-serve.sh` — startup script executed by supervisord
- `config/code-graph.json` — registers Graphify as an `http` transport backend at `localhost:$GRAPHIFY_MCP_PORT`

## Usage
Supervisord starts and monitors the `graphify` program automatically. The MCP endpoint is available at `http://localhost:$GRAPHIFY_MCP_PORT` (default `http://localhost:3851`) and is referenced by the code-graph registry for tool registration.

## Troubleshooting
- Check status: `supervisorctl status graphify`
- Restart: `supervisorctl restart graphify`
- Confirm port is bound: `ss -tlnp | grep 3851`
- Review logs via supervisord's configured log path for the `graphify` program.

topic: Code-Graph Registry and MCP Backend Configuration
summary:
## Purpose
The code-graph registry manages multiple code-graph backends and controls how MCP servers are registered and exposed to agents.

## Architecture
- Backend definitions live in `config/code-graph.json`, declaring each backend's name, transport type, and MCP tool list (`mcp.tools`).
- Two known backends:
  - **Graphify** — `http` transport (connects to `localhost:$GRAPHIFY_MCP_PORT`)
  - **CodeGraph** — `stdio` transport
- The registry reads `mcp.tools` from each backend's config entry to determine which tools to register with each MCP server.
- Registry logic is implemented in `lib/code-graph/registry.mjs`.

## Key Files
- `config/code-graph.json` — declares backends, transports, and `mcp.tools` lists
- `lib/code-graph/registry.mjs` — consumes `mcp.tools` to drive MCP server registration

## Usage
Agents and MCP consumers reference the registry to discover available code-graph tools. Adding or removing entries from `mcp.tools` in `config/code-graph.json` directly controls which tools are registered with each MCP server.

## Troubleshooting
- If a tool is missing from an MCP server, verify it is listed under the correct backend's `mcp.tools` in `config/code-graph.json`.
- If registry changes don't take effect, restart the affected MCP server process so it re-reads the config.

topic: .codegraph/ Directory and Docker Volume Tracking
summary:
## Purpose
The `.codegraph/` directory is tracked by Git as an empty placeholder to ensure Docker can mount it as a volume. Its presence in the repository is a structural requirement for container builds and volume mounts.

## Architecture
- `.codegraph/` is committed to the repository (tracked but empty, typically via a `.gitkeep`-style file).
- Docker uses this directory as a mount point or named volume target; it must pre-exist in the image layer.
- Docker cannot create a tracked Git directory at runtime if it is absent — the build or mount will fail silently or with an error.
- `git clean -fdx` or manual deletion will remove it and it will **not** be recreated automatically by Docker.

## Key Files
- `.codegraph/` — tracked empty directory; must not be deleted from the repository

## Usage
The directory is automatically present in any clean `git clone`. Docker Compose or Dockerfile configurations reference it for volume mounts related to code-graph data persistence.

## Troubleshooting
- If Docker volume mounts fail or code-graph data is not persisted, verify `.codegraph/` exists in the working tree.
- Recreate if accidentally deleted: `mkdir .codegraph && touch .codegraph/.gitkeep && git add .codegraph/.gitkeep`
- Do not add `.codegraph/` to `.gitignore`.

topic: MkDocs Documentation — Directory Layout and Screenshot Placement
summary:
## Purpose
Defines where all documentation source files, images, and diagram PNGs must live to build correctly under MkDocs `--strict` mode, and how to systematically verify and fix broken or placeholder image references.

## Architecture
- **Root configuration**: `mkdocs.yml` sets `docs_dir: docs-content` — all Markdown sources and embedded assets for the published site must live under `docs-content/`; edits under `docs/` have zero effect on the built site.
- **Two separate trees**: `docs-content/` (MkDocs-served) vs `docs/` (constraint-monitored project artifacts) — misplacing files between them is the primary cause of missing images and broken builds.
- **Architecture diagram**: lives inside `docs-content/` under the **Architecture** section header; exact location confirmed via `grep` of section headers and surrounding context lines.
- **Screenshot capture workflow**: screenshots intended for documentation must match the established image format (question + tool calls + answer).

## Key Files
- `mkdocs.yml` — sets `docs_dir: docs-content`; controls which tree is built and served
- `docs-content/` — canonical root for all MkDocs source Markdown and embedded images
- `docs/` — project artifact tree; changes here do not affect the built site

## Usage
Consulted when adding new diagrams, screenshots, or documentation sections. Any new image asset must be placed under `docs-content/` and referenced with a path relative to that root.

## Troubleshooting
- Missing images in built site: confirm the asset is under `docs-content/`, not `docs/`.
- To locate the Architecture section and its diagram: `grep -n "Architecture" docs-content/**/*.md -A 5`
- MkDocs `--strict` mode fails on broken image references — run a local build (`mkdocs build --strict`) to surface all broken refs before pushing.

topic: Concurrent Agent Session Management — Phantom Commits and Inter-Session Communication
summary:
## Purpose
Defines how to undo published changes on `main`, covering both the preferred forward-revert approach and the exceptional hard-reset path used when revert leaves the repo in an inconsistent state.

## Architecture
- **Forward-revert (default)**: changes already pushed to `main` are undone via `git revert` (a new commit), never via force-push. After revert, working tree is compared byte-for-byte against the target baseline to confirm full revert.
- **Hard reset (exceptional)**: when `git revert --no-commit` leaves an inconsistent state (e.g. broken submodule pointers), switch to `git reset --mixed <target>` to preserve live service files in `.data/` while removing unwanted commits from history. Force-push with `--force-with-lease`. Rebuild `dist/` after reset.
- **No-PR workflow**: all changes — including reverts and resets — are committed and pushed directly to `main` without pull requests.
- **Recovery artifact**: before any hard reset, save removed commit SHAs to `scratchpad/removed-commits.txt` for potential recovery.
- **Submodule alignment**: after any reset, verify submodule pointers are correct and re-trigger docs deploy if documentation is affected.

## Key Files
- `.git/` — standard git metadata
- `scratchpad/removed-commits.txt` — removed commit SHAs saved before hard resets
- `memory/` — stale memory files (e.g. `memory/feedback_mkdocs_two_image_dirs.md`) may need updating after large reverts

## Usage
Apply forward-revert for routine published-commit rollbacks. Use hard reset only when revert produces an inconsistent tree (broken submodule pointers, unresolvable conflicts). Always verify tree state post-operation and retrigger CI/docs deploy as needed.

## Troubleshooting
- **Inconsistent state after `git revert --no-commit`**: abort with `git revert --abort`, then use `git reset --mixed <baseline-commit>` instead.
- **Submodule pointers broken after reset**: run `git submodule update --init --recursive` and commit corrected pointers.
- **Docs not reflecting reset**: manually retrigger the `deploy-docs` workflow; confirm `dist/` is rebuilt before push.
- **Need to recover removed commits**: consult `scratchpad/removed-commits.txt` for SHAs, then use `git cherry-pick` or `git show` to recover content.

topic: Rec Project — Turnkey Onboarding Plan
summary:
## Purpose
Provides a unified onboarding experience for the "rec" second-brain project so colleagues can clone and run `./install.sh` to fully configure their environment — dependencies, Obsidian configuration, public/private data partitioning — without manual steps.

## Architecture
- `install.sh` is **idempotent** (safe to re-run) and supports flags:
  - `--dry-run` — preview actions without changes
  - `--check` — validate current environment state
  - `--private` — provision the confidential vault
  - `--no-obsidian` — skip Obsidian-specific configuration
- Full flow: `git clone` + `./install.sh` handles dependency installation, Obsidian vault setup, pre-commit leak-guard hook installation, and routine configuration
- `braincli` and skills ecosystem enforce data-placement policy at the tooling level

## Key Files
- `install.sh` — main onboarding script; idempotent, flag-driven
- `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` — leak-guard hook installed during onboarding
- `install.md` — documents onboarding steps including Step 6 (agent smoke test)

## Usage
Run once after cloning: `./install.sh`. Re-run safely at any time with `--check` to validate environment state. Use `--private` on machines that should also provision the confidential vault.

## Troubleshooting
- If onboarding fails partway through, re-run `./install.sh` — idempotency ensures no double-application of completed steps.
- Use `--dry-run` to diagnose what the script would change before applying.
- If the pre-commit hook is missing, re-run install; it is placed at `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`.
- After install, run the pi agent smoke test (Step 6 in `install.md`) to confirm full agent functionality.

topic: CJS/ESM Module Compatibility — Adapter Files
summary:
## Purpose
Resolves CommonJS/ESM incompatibility for specific adapter and registry files that must remain CJS consumers in a package declared `"type": "module"`, without breaking ESM callers that import their exports.

## Architecture
- The root `package.json` uses `"type": "module"`, making all `.js` files ESM by default
- Files requiring CJS semantics are renamed to `.cjs`; Node.js treats `.cjs` as CommonJS regardless of the `"type"` field
- **ESM default-export unwrapping**: when a `.cjs` file `require()`s an ESM module, Node returns a namespace object — the actual class/value is at `.default`; callers must use `.default` access explicitly; `require(esm)` does NOT return the class directly
- **`package.json` main entry**: updated to reference the renamed `.cjs` file when the primary entry point is CJS
- **ESLint**: `eslint.config.js` must explicitly apply `no-unused-vars` to `.cjs` glob patterns; flat-config does not inherit `.js` rules for `.cjs` files automatically

## Key Files
- `lib/agent-registry.cjs` — renamed from `.js`; CJS registry file
- `lib/adapters/claude-mcp.cjs` — renamed from `.js`; CJS adapter file
- `lib/adapters/semantic-analysis-bridge.js` — has deleted-module imports; currently broken (open blocking issue)
- `package.json` — `main` entry updated to reference `.cjs` renamed file
- `eslint.config.js` — must include `.cjs` glob in `no-unused-vars` rule

## Usage
Used by any code path that `require()`s the agent registry or claude-mcp adapter from within a CommonJS context. ESM callers importing these files receive the namespace object and must access `.default` to get the exported class.

## Troubleshooting
- **Wrong export type**: if a caller receives a namespace object instead of a class, add `.default` access after `require()`.
- **`npm install` pruning `km-core` symlink**: re-link manually after any `npm install` run; this is a known hazard.
- **`ugrep` alias masking grep failures**: `ugrep` aliased to `grep` may suppress expected grep errors; use explicit `grep` binary if diagnosing missing matches.
- **Open blocking issues**: deleted-module imports remain in `semantic-analysis-bridge.js`, `GraphMigrationService.js`, and 7 operator scripts; `Validator.ts` is untested; 14 CI test suites are skipped — these must be resolved before those paths are considered stable.

topic: .codegraph/ Directory and Docker Bind Mount Contract
summary:
## Purpose
`.codegraph/` is a tracked project directory that serves as a required host-side source for a Docker bind mount. It must exist on the host before any container starts; Docker will not create missing bind-mount source paths automatically.

## Architecture
- The directory is kept in version control via a `.gitkeep` file (or equivalent), ensuring it exists after a fresh clone.
- Docker bind mounts reference `.codegraph/` as the host source; if the directory is absent at container startup, the mount silently fails or the container errors out.
- No automatic recovery mechanism exists — Docker does not recreate missing bind-mount sources.
- Deleting the directory (and its `.gitkeep`) breaks the volume mapping silently; git does not restore it automatically unless the sentinel file is also restored and committed.

## Key Files
- `.codegraph/` — tracked empty directory; must remain present on host
- `.codegraph/.gitkeep` — (or equivalent) sentinel file keeping the directory in git history
- `docker-compose.yml` — defines the bind mount referencing `.codegraph/` as host source

## Usage
The directory is mounted into one or more containers via Docker bind mounts defined in `docker-compose.yml`. Any process inside those containers that reads or writes to the mounted path depends on this directory existing on the host.

## Troubleshooting
- If a container fails to start or a volume mapping is missing, verify `.codegraph/` exists on the host.
- If deleted, restore by running `mkdir -p .codegraph && touch .codegraph/.gitkeep` and committing the result.
- Docker will not recreate the directory automatically — manual restoration is always required.
- Confirm the bind mount is active inside the container with `docker inspect <container>` and checking the `Mounts` section.

topic: coding-v1 Benchmark — Design and Scoring
summary:
## Purpose
Documents known threats to benchmark measurement validity in the kgbench coding performance project: system-load noise, ambiguous `"no_result"` cell classifications, baseline isolation constraints, concurrent session corruption, and tally discrepancies that affect report integrity.

## Architecture
- **Result buckets**: `report.mjs` (lines 125–131, 155–160) computes all metrics exclusively over the `"ok"` bucket; `"no_result"` cells are excluded from aggregate scores but still affect token median figures when they represent a large fraction of the underlying sample.
- **Token median skew**: ambiguous `"no_result"` cells can dominate the token sample for a given arm, making the token median unreliable until those cells are resolved.
- **Concurrent session corruption (confirmed)**: two concurrent opencode session sets corrupt attribution bidirectionally. Opencode combos must be scheduled **sequentially** to prevent overlapping time windows from cross-contaminating token count columns.
- **Progress monitoring race condition**: `tail -f` invoked on a log file before that file exists will fail silently or error. Pre-create the log file with `touch <scratchpad-log-path>` before starting the tail operation to ensure reliable progress tracking.
