topic: EF-412 Feedback File Schema
summary:
## Purpose
Defines the standardized structure and compliance bar for filing EF-412 team member feedback transcripts, including handling of transcripts lacking substantive development content, misattributed speakers, and third-party performance data violations.

## Architecture
- Each team member has a folder `surname-firstname` under `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/`, containing `timeline.md` and `log.md`.
- Folder names must match `EF-412.md` reference links and be cross-checked against the roster — ASR/transcript name errors are common; always confirm against the private vault roster before creating a folder.
- Sessions only qualify as "development content" if they cover actual performance/growth feedback for the named subject; tool-test calls, process/mechanics discussions, or org-context chat do NOT qualify.
- **Third-party performance data rule**: if a transcript contains performance/development discussion about someone OTHER than the record's subject, it must NOT be filed as-is into that subject's record — this is a recurring real-world scenario (e.g. a manager's feedback session referencing a peer's performance) and requires pausing before filing to seek clarification on how to handle/redact the third-party content.

## Key Files
- `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/<surname-firstname>/timeline.md`
- `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/<surname-firstname>/log.md`
- `second-brain-private/EF-412.md` — roster/reference links

## Usage
Invoked by the ef-412-feedback skill after a meeting-recording session produces a transcript; the agent classifies transcript content and either files it into the appropriate person's folder or halts pending clarification.

## Troubleshooting
- If a transcript discusses a third party's performance, do NOT file automatically — pause and ask for guidance on redaction/exclusion before writing to any record.
- If transcript lacks substantive development content (e.g. it's just tool testing), do not create/update a feedback entry.
- Always verify folder name against the roster before creating a new person folder — ASR mis-transcription of names is common.

- Each team member has a folder `surname-firstname` under `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/`, containing `timeline.md` and `log.md`.
- Folder names must match `EF-412.md` reference links and be cross-checked against the roster — ASR/transcript name errors are common; always confirm against the private vault roster before creating a folder.
- Sessions only qualify as "development content" if they cover actual performance/growth feedback for the named subject; tool-test calls, process/mechanics discussions, or org-context chat do NOT qualify.
- **Third-party performance data rule**: if a transcript contains performance/development discussion about someone OTHER than the record's subject, it must NOT be filed as-is into that subject's record — this is a recurring real-world scenario (e.g. a manager's feedback session referencing a peer's performance) and requires pausing before filing to seek clarification on how to handle/redact the third-party content.

## Key Files
- `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/<surname-firstname>/timeline.md`
- `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/<surname-firstname>/log.md`
- `second-brain-private/EF-412.md` — roster/reference links

## Usage
Invoked by the ef-412-feedback skill after a meeting-recording session produces a transcript; the agent classifies transcript content and either files it into the appropriate person's folder or halts pending clarification.

## Troubleshooting
- If a transcript discusses a third party's performance, do NOT file automatically — pause and ask for guidance on redaction/exclusion before writing to any record.
- If transcript lacks substantive development content (e.g. it's just tool testing), do not create/update a feedback entry.
- Always verify folder name against the roster before creating a new person folder — ASR mis-transcription of names is common.

topic: Playwright CLI Browser Automation Skill Guide (a2a-xpr)
summary:
## Purpose
Restructures a2a-xpr's MkDocs documentation into a code-along tutorial (8 chapters, Quick/Deep Dive tiers) that walks a reader from an empty directory to a working a2a/AgentStack deployment, while also serving as a dogfooding exercise that surfaces real defects in the platform's own tooling.

## Architecture
- Tutorial is organized as 8 sequential chapters (~2,000 lines across 16 new doc files) added to `mkdocs.yml` nav, with chapter-discovery and `.gitignore` guards added so chapter artifacts aren't accidentally excluded from the docs build.
- Each chapter is dogfooded end-to-end: every command in the tutorial is actually run against a real checkout, verifying all four A2A paradigms (sync, async+input-required, streaming, push) work as documented.
- Defects found via dogfooding are fixed in the underlying codebase (not just documented), each with a regression test, since the tutorial is treated as an executable spec of the platform's UX.
- Builds on the general Quick/Standard/Deep tab pattern established for other pages (shell page + `pymdownx.snippets` include of moved-verbatim original content), extended here to a full tutorial rather than a per-page split.

## Key Files
- `mkdocs.yml` — nav restructured for the 8-chapter tutorial flow.
- `serve.py` — had a missing "push" wiring bug, now fixed.
- `adp-internal-a2a.md` — had stale claims corrected to match current behavior.
- New chapter doc files (16 total, one plan file e.g. `eager-munching-cake.md`) — the tutorial content itself.
- Test suite additions — regression tests for each of the 5 defects found (gitignore masking docs, push not wired, `make demo` entry point, proxy blocking compose names, NL path type mismatch).

## Usage
Consumed by new developers/readers following the "Build it" tutorial from scratch; also used internally as a validation harness — running through the tutorial is now an effective way to catch regressions in the a2a/AgentStack developer experience (69 tests must pass, `mkdocs build --strict` must be clean).

## Troubleshooting
- If `mkdocs build --strict` fails, check for broken snippet includes or nav entries referencing renamed/moved chapter files.
- If a chapter's commands fail against a fresh checkout, suspect drift between documented behavior and actual code — treat as a defect to fix + regression-test, not just a doc typo.
- Mermaid diagrams (e.g. in chapter 5) should be visually spot-checked on the deployed site after merge, since `--strict` build success doesn't guarantee correct rendering.
- PR merge blockers seen previously: branch already merged into main (check `gh pr view`/`git log` before re-attempting), and GitHub CLI auth mismatches between github.com and internal GHE remotes (verify `gh auth status` against the correct host).

topic: Health Coordinator launchd Service Management
summary:
## Purpose
The `health-coordinator` runs as a macOS launchd-managed service. Its runtime configuration (env vars, flags, tracing) is controlled via a launchd plist, requiring specific reload procedures when changed.

## Architecture
- Service is defined by a launchd plist (typically under `~/Library/LaunchAgents/`) specifying the executable, environment variables, and startup behavior for `health-coordinator`.
- launchd caches the loaded plist definition in memory; a simple `kickstart` restart only restarts the running process without re-reading plist changes.
- To apply plist edits (e.g. enabling tracing flags/env vars), the service must be fully unloaded and reloaded via `bootout` then `bootstrap`, not just kickstarted.

## Key Files
- launchd plist for `health-coordinator` (e.g. `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.*.health-coordinator.plist`) — defines service env, args, and lifecycle.
- `health-coordinator.js` — the coordinator's main implementation, invoked by launchd per plist config.

## Usage
Used whenever tracing, debug env vars (e.g. `HEALTH_DEBUG_ETM`), or other launch-time configuration for the health-coordinator needs to change and take effect.

## Troubleshooting
- If tracing/config changes appear not to take effect after a restart, check whether only `kickstart` was used — perform a full `launchctl bootout` followed by `launchctl bootstrap` of the plist instead.
- Confirm the plist was reloaded by checking coordinator logs for the new config/tracing output immediately after bootstrap.

topic: Live-Logging Test Suite — Flaky Test Race Conditions
summary:
## Purpose
Establishes a diagnostic discipline for CI and compiler failures: verify runtime/daemon health first, run the full test suite locally, then trace TypeScript config/import chains before assuming a code regression or architectural type-debt.

## Architecture
- Triage sequence: (1) confirm daemon/service health, (2) run tests locally in CI mode, (3) if local passes but CI fails, pivot to CI-specific compile/environment issues, (4) trace `tsconfig` settings and import paths, comparing file trees between repo and submodule, before assuming deeper architectural debt.
- Common tsconfig root cause: `lib`/`target` pinned to an older ES version (e.g. `ES2020`) missing features used by newer code — e.g. the `Error` constructor's `cause` parameter requires `ES2022`. Fix by bumping `lib`/`target` in `tsconfig.json` to at least `ES2022`.
- Broken-import root cause pattern: code duplicated from a submodule (e.g. `integrations/semantic-analysis`) into the main repo without copying a sibling module (e.g. `src/agents/`) — violates the project's no-parallel-versions rule and manifests as "cannot find module" errors pointing at directories that only exist in the submodule.
- When investigating reported compiler errors (e.g. from a screenshot), confirm each error individually against `tsconfig` settings and import path resolution rather than assuming a single shared cause — errors can have distinct root causes (3 config-related + 1 structural duplication, in one observed case).

## Key Files
- `tsconfig.json` — must exclude submodule/symlinked directories and set `lib`/`target` to at least `ES2022`.
- `OntologyClassifier.ts` — example of a file broken by incomplete submodule-to-repo duplication (references nonexistent `src/agents/`).
- `integrations/semantic-analysis` — submodule source of truth; duplicated code elsewhere must mirror its full sibling module set.

## Usage
Applied whenever a batch of TypeScript compiler errors appears (e.g. from CI or IDE) to distinguish quick config fixes from deeper architectural debt before committing to a fix approach.

## Troubleshooting
- `Error` constructor `cause` param errors → check `tsconfig.json` `lib`/`target`; bump to `ES2022`.
- "Cannot find module" errors pointing at submodule-only paths → check whether the file was duplicated from a submodule without its sibling modules; either copy the missing module or re-point the import at the submodule per the no-parallel-versions rule.
- Always compare repo vs. submodule file trees directly rather than guessing from error text alone.

topic: Rapid-LLM-Proxy — PR-Based Push Workflow (Enterprise GHE)
summary:
## Purpose
Documents the workflow and troubleshooting steps for pushing local commits/branches and opening PRs, distinguishing the direct-push `coding` repo from the PR-required `rapid-llm-proxy` enterprise repo. Feature branch pushes can fail transiently and require retry plus config verification against a known-working baseline.

## Architecture
- `coding` repo: direct push to `origin main` over SSH works routinely; no PR needed.
- `rapid-llm-proxy` repo: hosted on enterprise GHE (`<company>.ghe.com`) over HTTPS; branch protection blocks direct push to `main`; all changes require `gh pr create`.
- `gh` CLI shorthand repo references 404 against enterprise hosts — must set `GH_HOST=<company>.ghe.com` and use fully-qualified repo paths for all `gh` commands.
- Local branches lacking a remote counterpart (e.g. `local/live`) are a known separate issue distinct from feature-branch push failures.
- Feature branch push failures for PR prerequisites are sometimes transient — retry before deeper diagnosis.

## Key Files
- Claude/CLI configuration/settings files (compared against known-working `rapid-llm-proxy` PR workflow) — exact paths not enumerated in digests.

## Usage
Used whenever finalizing feature work (e.g. `feat/network-aware-judge-bands`) that needs to be pushed and turned into a PR on the enterprise repo, or when syncing the `coding` repo directly.

## Troubleshooting
- If `gh` commands 404, verify `GH_HOST` env var and fully-qualified repo path are set.
- If a branch push fails, retry once before investigating config; compare current settings against a previously successful PR workflow.
- Check for stray local-only branches (no remote tracking) as a separate root cause of confusion during push troubleshooting.

topic: Documentation Style Guide (a2a-xpr)
summary:
## Purpose
Covers the `gsd-browser` tool's installation, path resolution, and the fresh-install/merge verification workflow used to confirm fixes work for both new and existing users.

## Architecture
- `gsd-browser` resolves its binary/profile by checking both legacy (`${TMPDIR}/chromiumoxide-runner`) and current (`~/.gsd-browser/browser-profile`) locations, falling back gracefully if one is absent.
- `GSD_BROWSER_BIN` env var provides an explicit override/fallback for locating the binary, used when `install.sh` cannot auto-provision it.
- `install.sh` performs fresh-install provisioning but currently has no `.gsd-browser`-specific references for missing-binary cases; this is a known gap deferred as a product decision rather than a bug.
- `verify_installation` includes warning-level coverage for cases where the binary/profile isn't found in either expected location.
- Test suite (Jest + node:test) validates regex-based guard conditions across bounded windows (e.g. 300-char scan windows) rather than unbounded matches, avoiding false negatives/positives in pattern checks.

## Key Files
- `install.sh` — fresh-install provisioning script, missing `.gsd-browser` binary handling (deferred item)
- Jest test files — verify guard-condition regex patterns across bounded windows
- Path-resolution logic (binary lookup) — checks legacy `${TMPDIR}/chromiumoxide-runner` then `~/.gsd-browser/browser-profile`

## Usage
Invoked during binary upgrades, fresh installs (`./install.sh`), and background daemon startup (`gsd-browser daemon start --debug`). Verification runs the full Jest + node:test suite (expect ~1132+ passing, zero failures) plus coordinator sweep monitoring to confirm session integrity after merges.

## Troubleshooting
- If binary not found, check both legacy and current profile paths; set `GSD_BROWSER_BIN` explicitly to bypass auto-detection issues.
- `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` in worktrees is unrelated to gsd-browser logic — see Git Worktree Setup insight for symlink requirements.
- Missing-binary provisioning failures in `install.sh` are a known, deferred gap — do not treat as a regression.

topic: LLM Proxy — rapid-llm-proxy Operational Characteristics
summary:
## Purpose
`rapid-llm-proxy` is a local HTTP proxy bridge between AI agents and upstream LLM APIs (e.g. Anthropic). It handles credential forwarding, parameter translation, and routing for agents like Claude, pi, and opencode.

## Architecture
- **Entry point**: `rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — the running Node.js server process
- **Bind address**: `127.0.0.1:12435`
- **Upstream**: Anthropic API; proxy maintains established TCP connections to upstream when healthy
- **Agent integration**: agents route through the proxy via `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` environment variables; per-agent credential wiring is separate from proxy health
- **Not the only proxy in the chain**: a separate system-level proxy agent (`proxydetox`, managed via `launchctl`) sits between agents and `rapid-llm-proxy` for some launchers — the two layers must be diagnosed independently (see CN Environment insight)

## Key Files
- `rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — main proxy server process

## Usage
All LLM-calling agents (Claude, pi, opencode) route requests through this proxy when configured via proxy environment variables. It is the shared dependency point for diagnosing "LLM unavailable" reports.

## Troubleshooting
- Diagnose via: HTTP health probe to `127.0.0.1:12435`, process listing (confirm `server.mjs` running with healthy resource usage), and checking for active established upstream connections
- A healthy proxy does NOT rule out failure — check `proxydetox` (system-level layer) and non-proxy causes (e.g. unsupported model input types like images) separately
- No log directory issues observed in past investigations; env var inspection is part of standard diagnostic routine

topic: Rec Project — Repository Architecture and Purpose
summary:
## Purpose
The `rec` repository is a macOS meeting-recording and note-management pipeline that captures audio, produces transcripts, and ingests structured notes into an Obsidian "second brain" vault. It acts as a workspace container for related sub-tools, vault content, and configuration.

## Architecture
- **Workspace container**: outer `rec/` directory organizes sub-tools, vault content, and configuration but has no git commit history of its own
- **Versioned sub-project**: `rapidscribe-meeting/` (Swift/Rust CLI) is nested within `rec/` and is the correct target for code commits related to recording, transcription, installer scripts, and skill logic
- **Pipeline flow**: audio capture (macOS ScreenCaptureKit) → `rapidscribe-meeting` CLI → transcript → Obsidian vault ingestion (`second-brain/EF-412/`)
- **Related repos**: `second-brain` (public vault), `second-brain-private` (confidential vault on GHE)
- **Multi-repo context**: `rec`, `second-brain`, and `second-brain-private` are separate repos referenced together for the full feedback workflow

## Key Files
- `rapidscribe-meeting/` — versioned CLI project
- `second-brain/EF-412/` — public vault structure
- `second-brain-private/EF-412/feedback/` — confidential feedback records

## Usage
Developers working on recording/transcription code should `cd rapidscribe-meeting/`; vault content changes go through the appropriate second-brain repo.

## Troubleshooting
- Confirm correct repo before committing (see rapidscribe-meeting Repository Structure insight)
- If vault changes aren't tracked, verify which second-brain repo (public vs private) the target directory belongs to

summary:
## Purpose
Clarifies which directory is the actual versioned git project for code changes (installer fixes, skill logic, state-machine hardening) within the broader "rec" workspace, preventing commits to the wrong location.

## Architecture
- The outer `rec/` directory is a **workspace container only** — no git commit history; organizes sub-tools, vault content, and the second-brain vault
- `rapidscribe-meeting/` is the actual versioned sub-project nested within the rec workspace, carrying real commit history
- All code commits related to the recording/transcription CLI (installer scripts, skill logic, session state machine) must target `rapidscribe-meeting/`, not `rec/`

## Key Files
- `rapidscribe-meeting/` — versioned project root; contains `.git/`
- `rec/` — workspace container; no `.git/` at root level

## Usage
Before committing any code change, confirm target by checking for `.git/` presence: `ls rapidscribe-meeting/.git`.

## Troubleshooting
- If a commit seems to vanish or `git log` shows unexpected history, verify current working directory is `rapidscribe-meeting/`, not `rec/`
- Use `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` to confirm repo root before committing

topic: Token Usage Dashboard — Routing Trail Persistence and Observability
summary:
## Purpose
Visualizes LLM routing decisions as a decision ladder backed by the existing SQLite token-usage database and provides an inline offload policy editor. Enables developers to inspect per-call gate evaluation, fallback chains, and complexity-band dispatch without new instrumentation.

## Architecture
- **Data source**: existing `token_usage` SQLite database — records job, agent, complexity band, attempt trails with errors and timings; no new instrumentation required.
- **Decision ladder**: mirrors the gate evaluation order in `routing-config.mjs` (~lines 726–771) exactly; seven rungs with collapsed zero-count rows to prevent silent diagram/implementation disagreement.
- **Dual-mode display**: Configuration mode (policy as configured) vs Recorded mode (observed routing from DB); call-scrubber filmstrip for per-call replay (see Recorded Call Scrubber insight — now implemented).
- **Edge encoding**: outcome-based 3-colour CVD-safe palette (blue=as-routed, aqua=offloaded, red=failed) with solid/dotted line styles distinguishing edge types.

## Key Files
- `routing-config.mjs` — source of truth for gate evaluation order (~lines 726–771)
- `token-usage.db` — SQLite data source
- `decision-ladder.tsx` — ladder rendering component

## Usage
Used by developers to inspect routing behaviour without new instrumentation; toggled between Configuration and Recorded modes to compare intended vs. actual routing.

## Troubleshooting
- If the ladder disagrees with `routing-config.mjs` gate order, check that rung ordering hasn't drifted from the config file's evaluation sequence.
- Zero-count rungs are collapsed by design — do not mistake this for missing data.

topic: Letter-Counting Query Handling
summary:
## Purpose
Documents the reliable method used by the `pi` agent to answer letter-occurrence-counting queries in words or short phrases (a known weak point for LLMs due to tokenization), ensuring accurate character-level counting rather than relying on tokenization-based guesses.

## Architecture
- Approach: manually spell out the word/phrase character-by-character before counting occurrences of the target letter, avoiding token-level miscounting errors common in LLMs.
- Applies equally to single words and multi-word phrases, including spaces (e.g. "strawberry" → 3 occurrences of "r"; "cheese cake" → 1 occurrence of "r").
- Purely an in-context reasoning technique — no code or persistent artifacts involved.

## Key Files
N/A — no files produced or modified.

## Usage
Applied whenever a user asks the agent to count specific letter occurrences in a word or phrase; the agent should explicitly spell out the text character-by-character (including spaces) before counting to ensure correctness.

## Troubleshooting
If letter-counting answers are wrong, check whether the agent skipped the explicit character-by-character spelling step and instead estimated from token boundaries — this is the most common failure mode. Re-run with explicit spelling to correct.

## Purpose
Defines the architectural boundary between the general-purpose `rapidscribe-meeting` skill (community tool) and EF-412-specific recording preferences and conventions, preventing project-specific customizations from being imposed on broader users.

## Architecture
- **General skill**: `rapidscribe-meeting` skill lives in the `rapidscribe-meeting` versioned sub-project; must remain unmodified by project-specific conventions
- **Project-specific skill**: EF-412 meeting recording skill is to be created within the `rec` private repo, encapsulating EF-412-specific style, preferences, and vault ingestion targets
- **Separation principle**: general community tools and project-specific tools evolve independently; a project's conventions must never be merged back into the shared skill

## Key Files
- `rapidscribe-meeting/` — general-purpose skill; must stay unmodified for community use
- `rec/` (private) — target location for the EF-412-dedicated meeting recording skill (creation pending)

## Usage
Consulted when deciding where to implement a new recording behavior or convention — general fixes go to `rapidscribe-meeting/`, EF-412-specific behavior goes to `rec/`.

## Troubleshooting
- If a proposed change is EF-412-specific (naming, filing conventions, style preferences), do not add it to `rapidscribe-meeting/` — create/extend the EF-412 skill in `rec/` instead

topic: LLM Routing Dashboard — Decision Ladder and Flow Diagram Integration
summary:
## Purpose
Governs how routing complexity bands are evaluated against ladder "rungs" (e.g. `target-band`, `scope`) to decide offload/scope behavior per request, avoiding redundant transitions between rungs.

## Architecture
- Ladder retains separate rungs for `target-band` and `scope`; these are evaluated independently rather than collapsed.
- Per-band scope change evaluation now happens at the existing `scope` rung instead of re-triggering `RUNG_OFFLOADED` transitions — this avoids redundant rung movement while still assessing scope changes for each band.
- This sits alongside the broader decision-ladder visualization (see Token Usage Dashboard — Routing Trail Persistence insight) which mirrors gate evaluation order in `routing-config.mjs` (~lines 726–771), seven rungs, dual-mode (Configuration vs Recorded) display.

## Key Files
- `routing-config.mjs` — canonical gate/rung evaluation order (lines ~726–771)
- Ladder/flow diagram components (`DecisionLadder`, flow diagram) — consume rung geometry

## Usage
Used by the proxy's routing engine when deciding whether a request should be offloaded or kept on-path per complexity band; visualized in the token-usage dashboard's decision ladder.

## Troubleshooting
If rungs appear to re-transition unnecessarily (e.g. `RUNG_OFFLOADED` firing repeatedly for scope changes within the same band), verify scope evaluation is happening at the `scope` rung and not triggering a full rung re-move.

topic: opencode Daemon — Crash Recovery and Cold-Start Replay
summary:
## Purpose
The opencode daemon is one of three sub-agents (claude, opencode, copilot) maintaining 30s heartbeat cycles for health monitoring. After a host crash (e.g. VSCode crash), the daemon must cold-start and replay unprocessed sessions to restore healthy heartbeats across all three sub-agents.

## Architecture
- **Cold-start replay**: on restart, the daemon replays all sessions since the last known cursor position. A full cold start (no persisted cursor) can take over 10 minutes for ~80 sessions, since `lastPollTime` is not persisted across restarts, forcing a full re-scan instead of resuming from a checkpoint.
- **Heartbeat model**: all three sub-agents (claude, opencode, copilot) converge on a 30s heartbeat cycle once healthy; successful cold-start replay is confirmed when all three return to this cadence.
- **Latent defect #1**: launchd plist config sets `SuccessfulExit: false`, which can mask real outages instead of surfacing them clearly.
- **Latent defect #2**: `lastPollTime` is not persisted, causing long replay cycles on every restart rather than only after a true cold start.
- `trackError` function (error/telemetry tracking) exists in `scripts/sub-agent-live-opencode.mjs` at HEAD; cursor persistence logic is present but not yet validated end-to-end across a real restart.

## Key Files
- `scripts/sub-agent-live-opencode.mjs` — daemon implementation, includes `trackError` and cursor persistence logic
- launchd plist for the daemon — controls restart behavior; `SuccessfulExit: false` setting needs review

## Usage
Consulted when diagnosing slow daemon recovery after a crash, or when heartbeat status for claude/opencode/copilot sub-agents fails to stabilize post-restart.

## Troubleshooting
- If replay takes many minutes after restart, check whether `lastPollTime` was persisted — if not, expect a full re-scan of all sessions.
- If outages aren't surfaced despite real failures, check the `SuccessfulExit: false` plist setting as a possible masking cause.
- Confirm recovery success by watching for all three sub-agents (claude, opencode, copilot) reaching a stable 30s heartbeat cadence; end-to-end restart validation with cursor persistence is still pending confirmation.

topic: A2A Coding Integration — MCP Server Submodules & CI Contract
summary:
## Purpose
Defines the submodule structure and naming conventions for the coding-assistant integration layer in the a2a project, and enforces server declarations via a CI contract test so all expected servers are always registered.

## Architecture
- Two submodules — `semantic-analysis` and `constraint-monitor` — are not MCP server implementations; the `mcp-server-` prefix has been dropped from both directory names and upstream repository names.
- A systematic rename of the upstream repositories (affecting `integrations` config, `install.sh`, `test-coding.sh`, `uninstall.sh`, and docs) has been **scoped but not yet executed** — tool execution was aborted before any changes were made.
- `claude-code-mcp.json` declares all required servers; it must list all three: `constraint-monitor`, `graphify`, and `semantic-analysis`.
- `.gitmodules` and git config reference the renamed repository URLs and submodule paths.
- `agent-startup-contract.test.js` enforces that all three servers are present in `claude-code-mcp.json`; missing declarations cause CI failure.

## Key Files
- `claude-code-mcp.json` — server declarations; must list `constraint-monitor`, `graphify`, `semantic-analysis`
- `.gitmodules` — submodule remote URLs; must reference correct (non-`mcp-server-` prefixed) repository names post-rename
- `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh`, `test-coding.sh` — scripts requiring repo-name updates when rename is executed
- `agent-startup-contract.test.js` — CI test enforcing all three server declarations are present

## Usage
The integration layer is consumed by the coding assistant agent at startup. CI runs `agent-startup-contract.test.js` on every change to catch missing server registrations.

## Troubleshooting
- **CI failure on server declaration**: verify all three servers (`constraint-monitor`, `graphify`, `semantic-analysis`) appear in `claude-code-mcp.json`.
- **Submodule path mismatch after rename**: ensure `.gitmodules`, `integrations` config, and all shell scripts consistently reference the new non-`mcp-server-` prefixed names. The rename has not yet been applied — any reference to `mcp-server-semantic-analysis` or `mcp-server-constraint-monitor` is a stale name.
- **Partial rename state**: if rename is partially applied, cross-check `install.sh`, `uninstall.sh`, `test-coding.sh`, and `README.md` for lingering old names.

topic: KB Injection A/B Experiment — Task Design and Discrimination Validity
summary:
## Purpose
Defines validity criteria for task specs used in the KB injection A/B experiment and the methodology for analyzing and reporting results. A spec is only valid if its graded strings are structurally absent from the sandbox AND retrievable from the knowledge base.

## Architecture
**Validity rule (dual requirement):**
- Graded string must be **absent from the sandbox** — confirmed via post-strip audit using `experiment-audit-recoverability.mjs`
- Graded string must be **retrievable from the knowledge base**
- If either condition fails, the task measurement is invalid and cannot be recovered post-hoc

**Known discrimination failure mode — repo-solvable tasks:**
- If tasks are solvable from repository content alone, both kb-on and kb-off arms converge to similar scores (~0.70 observed), making KB injection invisible
- Task selection is the primary lever; judge scoring fixes are prerequisite but not sufficient

**Report structure:**
- Experiment specification definitions live in KB-AB specification files (not reconstructed from memory)
- Report is assembled by separating discovery from synthesis; research objectives, methodology, and measurement approach are treated as distinct sections
- Feasibility of expanding scope to programming tasks is an open investigation item

## Key Files
- `experiment-audit-recoverability.mjs` — post-strip audit tool confirming graded strings are absent from sandbox
- `context-block-legibility.spec.ts` — referenced artifact in experiment sessions (role may be incidental)

## Usage
Used when designing new task specs for the A/B experiment or when evaluating whether existing results are valid. Audit must be run after any sandbox strip operation before recording scores.

## Troubleshooting
- **Both arms score similarly (~0.70)**: repo-solvable task — task spec must be replaced; scoring fixes alone will not reveal KB effect
- **Invalid measurement**: if audit shows graded string present in sandbox or absent from KB, the data point must be discarded — no post-hoc recovery is possible

- Graded string must be **retrievable from the knowledge base**
- If either condition fails, the task measurement is invalid and cannot be recovered post-hoc

**Known discrimination failure mode — repo-solvable tasks:**
- If tasks are solvable from repository content alone, both kb-on and kb-off arms converge to similar scores (~0.70 observed), making KB injection invisible
- Task selection is the primary lever; judge scoring fixes are prerequisite but not sufficient

**Report structure:**
- Experiment specification definitions live in KB-AB specification files (not reconstructed from memory)
- Report is assembled by separating discovery from synthesis; research objectives, methodology, and measurement approach are treated as distinct sections
- Feasibility of expanding scope to programming tasks is an open investigation item

## Key Files
- `experiment-audit-recoverability.mjs` — post-strip audit tool confirming graded strings are absent from sandbox
- `context-block-legibility.spec.ts` — referenced artifact in experiment sessions (role may be incidental)

## Usage
Used when designing new task specs for the A/B experiment or when evaluating whether existing results are valid. Audit must be run after any sandbox strip operation before recording scores.

## Troubleshooting
- **Both arms score similarly (~0.70)**: repo-solvable task — task spec must be replaced; scoring fixes alone will not reveal KB effect
- **Invalid measurement**: if audit shows graded string present in sandbox or absent from KB, the data point must be discarded — no post-hoc recovery is possible

topic: Network Override Replay Strategy — Recorded Mode
summary:
## Purpose
Enables historical traffic to be replayed under alternate network configurations without persisting network state in history records. Supports counterfactual analysis of how recorded sessions would behave under different network parameters.

## Architecture
- **Derivation principle**: network behavior is never stored as an observed fact in history records; it is *derived* by replaying captured traffic through the ladder mechanism with different network parameters supplied at replay time
- **Consistency validation**: contract testing against the proxy validates that replayed results are consistent with live results under equivalent parameters
- **Semantic labeling**: results produced via this path are explicitly labeled as **derived** (as opposed to observed facts) to prevent derived values from being treated as ground truth in downstream analysis or storage

## Key Files
- No specific implementation files identified; this is a pure architectural constraint on the history record schema and replay pipeline

## Usage
Applied whenever recorded-mode traffic is replayed with non-original network parameters. The ladder mechanism accepts network parameters at replay time rather than reading them from stored history. Downstream consumers must check the `derived` label before treating results as observed facts.

## Troubleshooting
- If derived results are being stored or treated as observed facts, verify that the semantic label is propagated through the full replay pipeline to all consumers
- If replayed and live results diverge under equivalent parameters, the contract test against the proxy will fail — investigate parameter equivalence between the replay invocation and the live baseline

topic: KB Injection A/B Experiment — Sampling Pipeline and Mining Automation
summary:
## Purpose
Manages iterative sampling rounds for the KB injection A/B experiment, generating specs from the knowledge base and automatically triggering mining passes once sampling completes. Ensures sampled tasks are genuinely unsolvable from repository content alone — a prerequisite for valid KB injection signal.

## Architecture
- **Sampler script**: `kb-ab-sampler.mjs` — drives derivation runs; reference filter must be absent to avoid tainting batch results; must be killed and relaunched cleanly if configuration changes mid-run
- **Spec generation**: `kb-ab-make-mine-specs.mjs` — dedicated reusable script (extracted from inline heredoc); auto-triggers a mining pass once the pilot log reaches final state (~50 min completion window), removing manual intervention between sampling rounds
- **Discrimination report**: `kb-ab-discrimination-report.mjs` — generates and audits discrimination rate signal; validates facts from ledger data via sandbox-based iterative grep
- **Draw verification**: pilot log grep on `DERIVED` and `EXCLUDED` counts is the primary progress signal; confirmed population/draw ratios (e.g. 36 derived from 50 drawn out of 162) validate pipeline integrity before downstream continuation
- **Mining pass scale**: 24-cell pass (3 repeats × 8 tasks)

## Key Files
- `kb-ab-sampler.mjs` — core sampler; configuration-sensitive; kill and relaunch if config changes mid-run
- `kb-ab-make-mine-specs.mjs` — reusable spec generation + auto-mine trigger
- `kb-ab-discrimination-report.mjs` — discrimination rate audit and report generation
- `kb-ab-sample-pilot2.log` / `kb-ab-sample-pilot3.log` — pilot run logs; grep target for draw/derivation verification

## Usage
Run `kb-ab-sampler.mjs` to start a sampling round. Monitor progress via `grep DERIVED` and `grep EXCLUDED` on the active pilot log. Once the log reaches final state, `kb-ab-make-mine-specs.mjs` fires automatically to generate specs and trigger the next mining pass. Draw counts (e.g. 36/50) should be verified before proceeding to cell execution.

## Troubleshooting
- **Tainted batch**: if reference filter was active during sampling, kill the process immediately (even at 2/50), remove the filter from `kb-ab-sampler.mjs`, and relaunch — partial tainted results are not recoverable
- **Stalled progress**: grep the pilot log for `DERIVED`/`EXCLUDED` counts to confirm forward movement; a flat count indicates the sampler is wedged
- **Session limit invalidation**: prior draw result interpretations are invalidated if the session hit Claude's context limit; re-verify counts from the log directly via `bash grep` before treating results as confirmed
- **Mining not auto-triggered**: confirm the pilot log has reached its final line count and that `kb-ab-make-mine-specs.mjs` has execute permissions and is referenced correctly from the sampler's completion hook

topic: KB Injection A/B Experiment — Cell Injection Pipeline and Pilot Exclusion
summary:
## Purpose
Implements per-cell injection logic for the KB A/B experiment, controlling how and whether KB content is injected into each agent cell. Pilot exclusion logic filters cells that fail cost or budget criteria before the matrix runs.

## Architecture
- **`cell-injection.mjs`**: central module; contains API retrieval logic and budget threshold parameters governing whether injection proceeds for a given cell.
- **Request body divergence**: differences between injection implementations are not visible from surface-level parameter inspection — full request body comparison is required to locate divergence points. Parameters may appear identical at the top level while diverging in nested fields. Identifying the injection gap requires deep inspection of full request bodies, not just top-level parameter comparison.
- **Pilot exclusion reasons**: cells can be excluded based on cost scaling factors and budget thresholds; exclusion logic and cost scaling factors are inspectable via bash tooling. Sampling pilot exclusion reasons is a diagnostic step when injection gaps appear unexpectedly.
- **Injection gap diagnosis workflow**: (1) grep `cell-injection.mjs` for API retrieval and budget threshold patterns; (2) compare request parameters between implementations at surface level; (3) if parameters appear identical, inspect full request bodies to find the divergence point; (4) sample pilot exclusion reasons and cost determinants to re-derive the injection gap analysis before moving to solution design.

## Key Files
- `cell-injection.mjs` — core injection module; API retrieval logic and budget threshold parameters

## Usage
Invoked per cell during matrix execution. Exclusion decisions made here determine which cells receive KB content and which are filtered from the pilot set.

## Troubleshooting
- **Injection gap of unknown origin**: surface-level parameter inspection is insufficient — always compare full request bodies.
- **Unexplained exclusions**: sample exclusion reasons and cost scaling factors via bash to identify whether budget thresholds or cost normalization factors are the cause.
- **Parameters appear identical across implementations**: escalate to full request body diff; divergence is typically in nested fields not visible at the top level.

topic: MCP Server Configuration
summary:
## Purpose
Defines which MCP servers are available to coding agents, scoped to the minimal set needed for semantic analysis, code graph querying, and constraint monitoring. Configuration spans multiple JSON config variants, a global marketplace plugin registry, and a Docker-mode config generator script — stale entries in any layer cause session-start reconnect errors.

## Architecture
**Three active MCP servers:** `semantic-analysis`, `code-graph-rag`, `constraint-monitor`

**Six servers fully removed:** `browser-access`, `browserbase`, `serena`, `shadcn`, `context7`, `spec-workflow`

**Multi-scope configuration layers (all must be kept in sync):**
- **Project-level**: `.mcp.json` — scoped to a single project session
- **Global**: `~/.claude/settings.json` `enabledPlugins` — marketplace plugins active across all sessions; updated independently of `.mcp.json`; root cause of `-32000` session-start reconnect errors when stale
- **Docker**: `supervisord` configs and a Docker-mode config generator script
- **Launcher scripts**: may reference or inject MCP server lists at session creation time

**Unwanted servers appearing at runtime** (`constraint-monitor`, `semantic-analysis` showing up unexpectedly in `coding/bin/coding`) indicate a configuration layer has not been fully audited — the specific layer (local, Docker, or project-level) must be identified by diffing all four layers above.

## Key Files
- `.mcp.json` — project-scoped MCP server list
- `~/.claude/settings.json` — global `enabledPlugins` registry; most common source of ghost registrations
- Docker `supervisord` configs — controls which MCP servers start inside the container
- Launcher scripts — may inject MCP config at session creation

## Usage
Consulted at session start by the Claude Code agent runtime. All four layers are merged; a server present in any layer will appear in the session even if removed from others.

## Troubleshooting
- **Ghost servers appearing**: diff all four config layers to find the stale registration; `~/.claude/settings.json` is the most frequent culprit
- **`-32000` reconnect errors at session start**: a server listed in `enabledPlugins` no longer exists or has moved — remove the stale entry from `~/.claude/settings.json`
- **Server present in Docker but not local**: check `supervisord` config and the Docker-mode config generator independently of `.mcp.json`
- **Verification**: after editing any layer, relaunch the session and confirm only the three expected servers (`semantic-analysis`, `code-graph-rag`, `constraint-monitor`) appear

topic: VirtioFS Stale Cache — Docker Bind Mount Invalidation
summary:
## Purpose
Documents a macOS VirtioFS bug where Docker bind-mounts serve stale or truncated cached file content to containers even after the host file has been correctly updated. Affects any configuration file mounted into a container, with confirmed impact on `.constraint-monitor.yaml`.

## Architecture
- **Root cause**: VirtioFS caches bind-mount content; after host-side edits the container may receive a truncated or outdated copy without any error signal
- **Symptom pattern**: parsing failures or unexpected behaviour inside the container while host-side inspection shows a valid file — easily misattributed to syntax errors (e.g. YAML parser incompatibility between PyYAML and JS parsers) before the cache is ruled out
- **Detection**: compare file size/line count between host and container — `wc -l <file>` and `wc -c <file>` on both sides; any mismatch confirms stale cache
- **Recovery**: `docker-compose restart` (full restart, not just container stop/start) forces cache invalidation
- **Validation rule**: always verify configuration at the point of consumption (inside the container); host-side checks cannot catch runtime bind-mount cache issues

## Key Files
- `.constraint-monitor.yaml` — confirmed affected file (443 lines / 17676 bytes when healthy)
- `pattern-test.js` — used to verify parsing succeeds inside container post-restart
- `verify-rule.sh` — used to confirm constraint enforcement post-recovery

## Usage
Applies to any service consuming bind-mounted config files on macOS with Docker Desktop using VirtioFS. Relevant whenever a container reports parse errors or unexpected config state that cannot be reproduced on the host.

## Troubleshooting
1. Run `wc -l <file>` and `wc -c <file>` on both host and inside container — mismatch = stale cache
2. Run `docker-compose restart` (not stop/start) to force cache invalidation
3. Re-verify inside container: check file size, confirm parsing succeeds, confirm health API reports healthy
4. Do not spend time on YAML syntax investigations until bind-mount freshness is ruled out

topic: ETM — Redaction Pattern Performance
summary:
## Purpose
The ETM daemon applies redaction patterns to transcript content before writing observation records. A pre-flight validation gate confirms pattern correctness and quarantine behavior before any write operation proceeds.

## Architecture
- **Three sync points**: redaction patterns exist in three places that must be kept in sync — a Python implementation, a Node.js implementation, and `redaction-patterns.json`
- **Catastrophic backtracking hazard**: unbounded character class repetition (e.g. `[a-zA-Z0-9+/]{8,}`) combined with adjacent quantifiers causes superlinear/exponential backtracking on large inputs (~246 ms per 200 KB; >300 s on 400 KB)
- **Confirmed fix pattern**: bound all character class repetitions with an explicit upper limit (e.g. `[a-zA-Z0-9/]{8,64}`); also remove `+` from leading character classes in patterns like `aws_secret_standalone`
- **SHA redaction precision**: the SHA/git commit ID pattern uses a **negative lookahead/lookbehind** to preserve lowercase-only hex sequences (e.g., `refs/heads/main`) while still catching mixed-case tokens and keys containing `+`/`/`; this fix is applied to both `redaction-patterns.json` and the `ConfigurableRedactor` class fallback table
- **Test suite state**: 5 pass / 0 todo; all assertions are substantive (no placeholder `todo` entries remain)

## Key Files
- `redaction-patterns.json` — primary pattern list consumed by `ConfigurableRedactor`
- `~/Agentic/coding/.specstory/config/redaction-patterns.json` — specstory-specific copy; must be kept in sync
- `ConfigurableRedactor` class — Node.js implementation with fallback pattern table; owns the SHA negative lookahead fix independently of the JSON config

## Usage
Applied by the ETM daemon before every observation record write. Patterns must be validated in dry-run mode before any backfill `--write --commit` operation proceeds across the tracked repositories (`agentic-ai-nano`, `balance`, `coding`, `curriculum-alignment`, `km-core`, `timeline`, `ui-template`).

## Troubleshooting
- **False redaction of git refs**: if `refs/heads/main` or similar lowercase-only hex sequences are being redacted, the SHA negative lookahead is missing or incorrectly applied — verify both `redaction-patterns.json` and the `ConfigurableRedactor` fallback table carry the fix
- **Catastrophic backtracking**: if redaction takes >1 s on moderate inputs, check for unbounded `{8,}` quantifiers without an upper bound; add `{8,64}` cap
- **Pattern drift**: run the test suite (`5 pass / 0 todo` is the expected baseline) after any pattern change to confirm all three sync points are consistent

topic: SDK Surface Verification Workflow
summary:
## Purpose
Analyzes the exposed API/interfaces of the pinned `a2a-sdk` version to inform a pros/cons comparison and supporting diagram, published in the project's MkDocs documentation, and to surface real defects in both SDK usage and the verification tooling.

## Architecture
- `scripts/verify-sdk-surface.py` runs against the pinned SDK version to enumerate exposed interfaces.
- **Known SDK issues surfaced**: `TaskStore` ABC signature mismatch in the DynamoDB implementation; missing `sse-starlette` dependency.
- **Known script issues**: two bugs identified in `scripts/verify-sdk-surface.py` itself — script correctness is not yet fully solid.
- Downstream deliverable: `docs/sdk-and-runtime-options.md` with a Mermaid diagram separating SDK-choice concerns from deployment/hosting concerns.

## Key Files
- `scripts/verify-sdk-surface.py` — SDK surface analysis script (contains known bugs)
- `docs/sdk-and-runtime-options.md` — documentation output with Mermaid diagram

## Usage
Run manually when the pinned SDK version changes or when updating SDK comparison documentation.

## Troubleshooting
- **Script false positives/negatives**: two known bugs exist in the script; verify results manually against SDK source before acting on output.
- **`sse-starlette` import error**: add `sse-starlette` to the project's dependencies.
- **DynamoDB `TaskStore` error**: fix the ABC signature mismatch in the DynamoDB implementation to match the base class contract.

topic: Course Transcript Scraping Workflow
summary:
## Purpose
Automates extraction of lesson transcripts from the DeepLearning.AI course platform for local reference/archival, avoiding manual copy-paste from the video player UI.

## Architecture
- `cdp-scrape.mjs` drives a Chrome DevTools Protocol (CDP) session to scrape transcript content from DeepLearning.AI lesson pages.
- Requires the user to be signed in to the DeepLearning.AI platform first — authentication state is a precondition; sessions are resumed once sign-in is confirmed.
- Output path is a configurable scratchpad location updated per-course/per-session before each run.
- Workflow is resumable: interrupted sessions restart by re-confirming authentication, re-pointing the scratchpad path, and re-invoking the script.

## Key Files
- `cdp-scrape.mjs` — CDP-driven scraping script, sole entry point for transcript extraction

## Usage
Run manually per course/session. Output files are stored at the configured scratchpad path for local reference.

## Troubleshooting
- **Empty output / auth error**: confirm browser session is signed in to DeepLearning.AI before running.
- **Interrupted scrape**: re-point scratchpad path variable and re-invoke `cdp-scrape.mjs`; prior output is not lost.

topic: A2A PoC GitHub Enterprise Migration
summary:
## Purpose
Migrates the a2a proof-of-concept project to GitHub Enterprise, establishing correct remote configurations, submodule wiring, and history repo separation.

## Architecture
- The main a2a repo and its submodules are hosted on `<COMPANY_NAME_REDACTED>.ghe.com`; remotes must be configured to point at GHE URLs.
- The `.specstory/history/` directory is an **independent git repo** — it must be migrated separately and its remote set independently of the parent repo.
- VS Code SCM panel timing issues apply during migration (see VS Code SCM Panel insight); reload window after initializing the history repo.
- Submodule push ordering applies: push submodule changes before updating parent repo pointer.

## Key Files
- `.gitmodules` — submodule remote URLs; must reference GHE endpoints post-migration
- `.specstory/history/.git/config` — independent repo config; set its own GHE remote

## Usage
One-time migration procedure; ongoing GHE commit attribution rules (see GitHub Enterprise Commit Attribution Configuration insight) apply after migration is complete.

## Troubleshooting
- **History repo not visible in SCM after migration**: reload VS Code window to force repo re-scan.
- **Submodule 404 on clone**: verify `.gitmodules` URLs point to GHE and submodule has been pushed before parent.

topic: System Health Dashboard — Sessions Tab (LSL Viewer)
summary:
## Purpose
Provides an in-browser viewer for LSL session transcripts (both `.lsl.md` and `.lsl` chain formats) inside the system-health-dashboard, using a vendored copy of pi's HTML export template for server-side rendering without requiring the `pi` binary in the container.

## Architecture
- **Session discovery**: `lsl-sessions.mjs` walks `/workspace` siblings to discover all projects (9 found); parses both `.lsl.md` and `.lsl` chain formats in-memory using `LslMarkdownParser` backfill logic
- **Multi-part chain aggregation**: `peekMeta` aggregates metadata across all parts of a chain (e.g. a 12-part chain correctly reports 48 sets, not just the first part's 12); 200 chains list in ~520ms; default selection skips empty mid-flush sessions
- **Rendering**: pi's export-html template (~266 KB, 5 files, v0.84.2) vendored under `assets/`; tool name aliasing applied at render time only (`Bash` → `bash`) so pi's renderer receives expected argument shapes (e.g. `$ command` display instead of raw JSON); both `.md` and `.pi` formats display with format badges
- **API routes**: `GET /api/lsl-sessions` (list), `GET /api/lsl-sessions/:id(*)` (render individual chain); server-side markdown-to-pi conversion performed in-memory
- **Chain grouping**: server-side chain grouping logic consolidates multi-part chains before listing
- **Scale verified**: 200+ LSL transcript chains render correctly, including 12-part/2.6 MB chains with 48 prompt sets and 991 tool calls
- **Docker**: bind mounts added for `lsl-sessions.mjs` and related modules; pi vendor assets baked into image

## Key Files
- `lsl-sessions.mjs` — session discovery, chain grouping, `peekMeta` aggregation, in-memory markdown-to-pi conversion
- `assets/` — vendored pi export-html template (v0.84.2, ~266 KB, 5 files)
- Dashboard server route handlers — `GET /api/lsl-sessions` and `GET /api/lsl-sessions/:id(*)`
- Frontend React Sessions tab — lazy-loaded transcript rendering at `/sessions`

## Usage
Navigate to `/sessions` in the system-health-dashboard. Select a project from the sidebar; chains are listed with metadata (sets, tool calls, format badge). Click a chain to render the full transcript using pi's HTML template. No `pi` binary required in the container.

## Troubleshooting
- **Empty chain list**: verify Docker bind mounts include `lsl-sessions.mjs` and sibling workspace paths are accessible from the container
- **Wrong metadata on multi-part chains**: `peekMeta` must aggregate across all parts — if counts appear to reflect only the first part, the aggregation fix has not been applied
- **Rendering errors on large chains**: confirmed working up to 12-part/2.6 MB; tool name aliasing (`Bash` → `bash`) must be applied before passing to pi renderer or argument shapes will be wrong
- **E2E tests**: 6 Playwright E2E tests cover the sessions tab; run these after any change to discovery or rendering logic

topic: Deliberately Omitted Capabilities in code-graph Registry
summary:
## Purpose
Documents two capabilities intentionally excluded from the code-graph registry, preserving the rationale so future maintainers do not inadvertently re-add them.

## Architecture
- `config/code-graph.json` contains a `_comment` block that records which capabilities are omitted and why.
- For at least one omission, responsibility is explicitly delegated to another named component rather than handled by the registry itself.

## Key Files
- `config/code-graph.json` — source of registry configuration; `_comment` block documents excluded capabilities and delegation rationale

## Usage
Consult the `_comment` block in `config/code-graph.json` before adding new capabilities to the registry to confirm they are not intentionally excluded.

## Troubleshooting
If a capability appears missing from the registry, check the `_comment` block in `config/code-graph.json` first. If the omission is intentional, locate the delegated component noted there instead of adding the capability directly.

topic: Playwright Test Scoping — tool_use Card and KB Drill-Down
summary:
## Purpose
Ensures Playwright assertions in `context-block-legibility.spec.ts` correctly scope DOM queries to their intended parent elements, and verifies interactive element accessibility in KB drill-down views (working memory, insights, entities).

## Architecture
- **tool_use card scoping**: `details` element queries must be scoped to a testid-anchored parent on the `tool_use` card. Without scoping, the selector matches the first `details` in the DOM — which belongs to a `thinking` block — causing node mismatch assertion failures.
- **KB drill-down regression**: working memory, insights, and entities elements in the system health/knowledge base drill-down UI can lose clickability after edits to helpers or the `cat-samples` renderer. The regression spec navigates into retrieval capture data to isolate which code change breaks interactive element accessibility.
- Root cause of KB clickability loss is under active investigation; `cat-samples` renderer and helper changes have been partially ruled out via dedicated spec runs, but the precise mechanism has not yet been confirmed.

## Key Files
- `context-block-legibility.spec.ts` — primary spec; covers both tool_use card scoping and KB drill-down clickability regression

## Usage
Run as part of the Playwright regression suite against the system health dashboard UI. Triggered manually when changes touch helpers or the `cat-samples` renderer.

## Troubleshooting
- If `details` selector assertions fail with node mismatch, verify queries are scoped to the correct testid-anchored parent, not document root.
- If KB drill-down elements (working memory, insights, entities) lose clickability, run the KB drill-down regression spec and inspect retrieval capture data navigation to isolate the breaking change.
- Helper and `cat-samples` renderer changes are lower-probability culprits; investigate other recent edits to the drill-down rendering path first.

topic: KGBench Token Measurement (Content vs. Total Tokens)
summary:
## Purpose
KGBench distinguishes "content tokens" from total tokens to provide an efficiency metric reflecting only meaningful payload consumed during benchmark execution, excluding overhead such as system prompts and scaffolding.

## Architecture
- **Total tokens**: all tokens consumed in LLM calls during a run (input + output, including system/scaffolding prompts).
- **Content tokens**: tokens attributable to actual task content — the portion meaningful for measuring benchmark difficulty and agent efficiency, excluding fixed scaffolding overhead.
- The `summaryStats` function is the canonical implementation of this distinction for retrieval benchmark runs and is imported by at least one other module in the kgbench codebase.

## Key Files
- File containing `summaryStats` — implements content-token calculation for the retrieval benchmark (exact path unconfirmed; locate with `grep -r "summaryStats" .`)

## Usage
Benchmark result reports surface both content and total token counts. Content tokens are the primary metric for comparing agent efficiency across runs with differing scaffolding configurations.

## Troubleshooting
- If token counts appear inflated, verify whether scaffolding/system prompt tokens are being excluded in `summaryStats`.
- Locate the importer of `summaryStats` to trace how aggregated stats flow into reports: `grep -r "summaryStats" .`

topic: LLM Proxy Dependency for Agent Launch (Port 12435)
summary:
## Purpose
The LLM proxy on port 12435 is a required intermediary between agents/benchmark runners and upstream LLM APIs. All agent LLM calls are routed through it.

## Architecture
- Agents and benchmark execution pipelines direct LLM API requests to `localhost:12435`.
- The proxy handles authentication, routing, and potentially caching or rate-limiting before forwarding to the actual LLM backend.
- Both agent launch and any benchmark run involving LLM inference depend on this proxy being reachable.
- Failure modes: agent launch fails immediately if the proxy is down; benchmark runs fail at the first LLM call.

## Key Files
- Proxy service startup path unconfirmed; locate via: `grep -r "12435" supervisord.conf /etc/supervisor*`

## Usage
The proxy must be running before agents are started or benchmarks are executed. Any LLM-dependent operation will fail immediately or stall at the first LLM call if the proxy is unreachable.

## Troubleshooting
- Verify the proxy is listening: `ss -tlnp | grep 12435`
- If not running, locate and restart the proxy service via supervisord or its init mechanism.
- Check proxy logs for authentication errors or upstream LLM API failures if requests are being rejected.

topic: System-Health Dashboard Code-Graph Re-Index HTTP Route
summary:
## Purpose
The system-health dashboard exposes an HTTP route that allows operators or automated processes to trigger a full code-graph re-index on demand without restarting any service.

## Architecture
- The re-index route is served by the system-health dashboard server.
- Hitting the route initiates a re-index of the code graph against the active backend (Graphify or CodeGraph).
- Exact route path should be confirmed directly from the server source file.

## Key Files
- `integrations/system-health-dashboard/server.js` — hosts the re-index route handler

## Usage
Send an HTTP request to the re-index route after large code changes or when the index is suspected stale. No service restart is required; the dashboard server must be running on its configured port.

## Troubleshooting
- Find the exact route: `grep -n "reindex\|re-index\|index" integrations/system-health-dashboard/server.js`
- If re-index does not complete, check dashboard server logs for errors from the active code-graph backend.
- Ensure the dashboard server is running before attempting to trigger the route.

topic: KGBench Content Tokens Metric
summary:
## Purpose
Isolates the marginal token cost attributable to a retrieval strategy by subtracting fixed overhead from total observed tokens, enabling fair cost comparisons across retrieval arms, agents, and models.

## Architecture
- **Raw formula**: `content_tokens = in_tokens + out_tokens` — cache tokens (`cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`) are explicitly excluded to prevent inflation from longer sessions or differing caching strategies. Implemented in `lib/kgbench/tokens.mjs` via `fromTotals()`.
- **Baseline subtraction**: `content_tokens = total_tokens − baseline`, where baseline captures system prompt + tool schema overhead per `(arm, agent, model)` tuple. Measured once via a real probe session — median `in_tokens` across a trivial "reply OK, no tools" prompt — using `measureBaseline`. Resumed runs reuse prior baselines rather than remeasuring.
- **Token source consistency**: the accounting method (`stream-json` vs. `proxy-db-*`) is recorded alongside each baseline; a mismatch between a cell's token source and its baseline's source is a correctness error — baselines must be subtracted only from totals using the same source.
- Cache tokens are retained on individual rows for diagnostics but excluded from all summary aggregations.

## Key Files
- `lib/kgbench/tokens.mjs` — `fromTotals()` implements the raw exclusion formula; `measureBaseline` probes overhead per `(arm, agent, model)` tuple

## Usage
Called during kgbench run aggregation and reporting. `fromTotals()` is invoked per cell; baseline measurement runs once at the start of a fresh benchmark (or is reloaded for resumed runs). Output feeds `summaryStats` in `lib/kgbench/report.mjs`.

## Troubleshooting
- **Inflated content_tokens**: verify cache tokens are not being included — check `fromTotals()` call site.
- **Baseline mismatch warnings**: ensure the token source (`stream-json` vs. `proxy-db-*`) recorded with the baseline matches the source for the cells being aggregated.
- **Resumed runs**: baselines are not remeasured on resume — if the system prompt or tool schemas changed, delete the cached baseline to force a fresh measurement.

topic: semantic-analysis-bridge.js — Removal
summary:
## Purpose
`semantic-analysis-bridge.js` was a bridge to the `semantic-analysis-system/` MCP server tree. Both have been intentionally deleted with no replacement. This insight documents the removal state for future reference.

## Architecture
- `semantic-analysis-system/` MCP server tree was deleted; `semantic-analysis-bridge.js` imported from it and had no viable repoint target.

topic: Operational Knowledge Management (OKM) Export Snapshots
summary:
## Purpose
OKM export snapshots provide serialized knowledge-management data consumed by downstream workflows. The expected export location is persistently absent from the working tree, blocking all workflows that depend on this data.

## Architecture
- OKM exports are expected at `integrations/operational-knowledge-management/.data/exports/`, with `raas.json` as the primary expected file.
- Multiple independent checks have confirmed this directory does not exist in the current working tree.
- The gap surfaces incidentally during unrelated work rather than being pursued as a dedicated investigation, indicating a known blocker that keeps being rediscovered but not actioned.

## Key Files
- `integrations/operational-knowledge-management/.data/exports/raas.json` — expected export snapshot; confirmed absent

## Usage
Consumed by any workflow that reads OKM export data. Currently blocks all such workflows until the export is re-run or the correct path is identified.

## Troubleshooting
- Verify whether the export process has ever been run in the current environment; the directory may need to be created by running the OKM export pipeline.
- If the path is wrong, locate the actual export output directory by inspecting the OKM integration's configuration or run scripts.
- Until resolved, any workflow depending on `raas.json` will fail at the data-read step.

topic: kgbench Contamination Prevention
summary:
## Purpose
Prevents the kgbench benchmark harness from producing invalid results due to contamination — either by harness source leaking trap phrases into grep-searchable space, or by question/answer sets being physically located inside the repo tree that agents search.

## Architecture
**Contamination vector 1 — trap phrase leakage in harness source:**
- The grep arm searches the codebase; trap phrases quoted verbatim in comments inside `sandbox.mjs` or `graders.mjs` become matchable targets, producing self-inflicted false positives.
- Authoring rule: harness source must **never** quote trap phrases verbatim in comments or strings. A WARNING block documenting this rule is embedded at previously-offending locations.
- `graders.mjs` and `sandbox.mjs` must be **excluded from the run tree entirely** via `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES`.

**Contamination vector 2 — question/answer sets inside repo tree:**
- `queries.json` (question/answer sets) must be excluded from benchmark runs via `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` in `sandbox.mjs`.
- `leak_terms` declaration: a per-question mechanism that explicitly declares decisive must-not-appear strings; the harness validates that none appear in agent-visible files.

**DEFAULT_EXCLUDES** in `sandbox.mjs` is the single authoritative list of files excluded from every benchmark run tree. Current known required entries: `graders.mjs`, `sandbox.mjs`, `queries.json`.

## Key Files
- `lib/kgbench/sandbox.mjs` — contains `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES`; spawns per-cell benchmark runs; binary file encoding issues (NUL bytes) have been encountered here — use a hex-safe editor or strip NULs before editing
- `lib/kgbench/graders.mjs` — must itself be excluded from run trees to prevent trap phrase leakage

## Usage
`DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` is applied at harness startup when constructing the agent-visible worktree. Any file whose content could match benchmark queries or expose answers must be added here. Review this list whenever new harness source files reference question content.

## Troubleshooting
- **False positives on grep arm**: check whether a harness source file quoting a trap phrase is missing from `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES`; add it and re-run.
- **NUL bytes in sandbox.mjs**: the file has previously contained binary/NUL byte corruption; if edits fail or produce garbled output, inspect with `xxd | grep 00` and strip NUL bytes before modifying.
- **queries.json visible to agent**: confirm `queries.json` is present in `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES`; absence allows agents to read answers directly.

topic: GSD Discuss-Phase Menu Rendering — Skill Description Truncation
summary:
## Purpose
Tracks an unresolved defect where the `gsd-discuss-phase` skill's description renders visibly truncated or corrupted in the slash-command menu, despite the underlying source data being verified intact. This is distinct from the separately-resolved general slash-command menu corruption (stale binary build).

## Architecture
- **Symptom**: the `gsd-discuss-phase` skill description appears cut off/garbled in the rendered menu.
- **Confirmed non-causes**: raw source files inspected with control-character visibility enabled; exact truncation point measured; no invisible/non-printing characters found — storage-level corruption ruled out.
- **Root cause**: narrowed to a render-time fault in the menu display logic, not the underlying data. Specific code path not yet identified.

## Key Files
- `gsd-discuss-phase` skill definition source (exact path not confirmed) — verified clean at storage level
- Menu display/render logic (exact path not confirmed) — suspected fault location

## Usage
Affects any developer invoking the `gsd-discuss-phase` skill via the slash-command menu. The truncated description may cause confusion about available skill options.

## Troubleshooting
- Re-inspect the menu render logic for length caps, buffer limits, or truncation applied at render time rather than at data load.
- Confirm the stale-binary fix (rebuild/restart) is applied first to rule out that class of issue before diving into render logic.
- Diff rendered output length against raw source description length to identify the exact truncation boundary in the render path.

topic: Pi Interactive Launcher — Verification and Terminal Diagnostics
summary:
## Purpose
Documents the verification procedure for confirming that the pi-agent's routing path is correctly established after ETM registration or session recovery, and the diagnostic approach for identifying which provider is serving inference requests.

## Architecture
- **Session baseline**: active tmux sessions and VS Code windows must be audited before assuming the `pi` session needs restarting; an existing clean session may not require relaunch. Sessions are named `coding-pi-<PID>` (e.g. `coding-pi-35390`).
- **VS Code workspace reload risk**: a VS Code workspace reload kills any associated tmux session; mitigated by configuring a `folderOpen` task in `.vscode/tasks.json` to auto-relaunch pi in an integrated terminal, eliminating the need for manual restarts.
- **Routing verification**: post-ETM-registration routing is confirmed via a test inference query (e.g. "There are 3 r's in 'strawberry'") — successful tool response confirms connectivity is restored.
- **Provider identification**: determined via log inspection after the routing test; provider identity is not directly visible from the inference response alone. Confirmed providers include `gh-copilot` backed by `claude-sonnet-5` (~3.4s response times after quota window rollover).
- **Health endpoint**: `localhost:3034/health/state` — use to confirm pi has recovered and is serving.

## Key Files
- `.vscode/tasks.json` — `folderOpen` task that auto-relaunches pi in the integrated terminal; prevents session loss on workspace reload

## Usage
Run after any ETM registration event, VS Code workspace reload, or session restart to confirm the pi-agent's routing and provider are correctly established.

## Troubleshooting
- If pi is unresponsive after a VS Code reload, check whether the tmux session still exists before relaunching; the `folderOpen` task should handle recovery automatically if configured.
- Verify health via `curl localhost:3034/health/state`; a successful response confirms pi is serving.
- If quota is exhausted, pi will recover on the next quota window rollover — monitor response times (~3.4s is normal post-recovery).
- Provider identity is not visible from the inference response; inspect logs to confirm which backend is active.

topic: EF-412 Team Knowledge Base
summary:
## Purpose
Enables sharing a sanitized version of the second-brain repository with department colleagues while fully protecting confidential staff records, meeting recordings, staff discussions, and feedback entries (e.g., EF-412 feedback) — both in current files and in git history.

## Architecture
- **Classification-first prerequisite**: before any split is executed, the full repository structure, git history, and config files must be mapped to classify every file/directory as either confidential or shareable. This classification pass is a standalone task distinct from the actual split implementation.
- **Confidential content**: staff roster, feedback records, personal recordings, named assignments, meeting transcripts, EF-412 feedback entries.
- **Shareable content**: generic function matrices, department setup docs, schema/template files.
- **Tooling enforcement**: `install.sh --private` provisions the confidential vault; `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` (leak-guard) prevents accidental confidential commits to the public repo.

## Key Files
- `second-brain/EF-412/` — confidential; contains all staff feedback folders
- `second-brain/EF-412/staff-roster.md` — confidential HR grading data
- `funktionsmatrix-software-engineering.md` — candidate shareable content
- `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` — leak-guard hook
- `install.sh` — supports `--private` flag for dual-vault provisioning

## Usage
Triggered when preparing a department-facing fork or sanitized clone. Requires a completed classification map before any git history rewriting or repo forking is performed.

## Troubleshooting
- **Classification map missing**: the split effort has been re-initiated from scratch across multiple sessions with no persistent classification artifact — produce and commit a classification map file (e.g., `docs/content-classification.md`) before proceeding to avoid repeated rework.
- **History exposure risk**: current file removal alone is insufficient; git history must also be rewritten (e.g., `git filter-repo`) to remove confidential content from all past commits.

topic: coding-v1 Benchmark — Cross-Agent Matrix Runs (cont2/cont2b)
summary:
## Purpose
Extends `coding-v1-r8` with continuation budget 2 (`cont2`/`cont2b`) to measure whether additional agent turns improve retrieval quality. `cont2b` is a re-run used to validate/compare against the `cont2` baseline. Per-row integrity checks allow analysis to begin before the run fully completes, while full aggregate comparison is gated on the `matrix` test phase passing and all rows reaching completion.

## Architecture
- **Run state tracking**: progress tracked via `.data/kgbench/runs/coding-v1-r8-cont2b/supervise.status`. The `matrix` test phase passing is a distinct, earlier milestone than full row completion (48/48 rows) — at one checkpoint only 12/48 rows were complete, making aggregate stats premature; per-row integrity validation is the valid analysis mode on partial data.
- **Confirmed milestone**: the `matrix` test phase has now passed and completed successfully for `cont2b` (confirmed via `supervise.status`); this unblocked a full comparison of `cont2b` results against the `cont2` baseline.
- **Toolchain maintenance wave**: alongside the run, a broad set of core kgbench scripts and docs were updated in the same working session — indicates the run and its toolchain are actively co-evolving, so run outputs should be re-validated against the current script versions rather than assumed stable across sessions.

## Key Files
- `.data/kgbench/runs/coding-v1-r8-cont2b/supervise.status` — run state/progress file, source of truth for matrix-test vs full-completion status
- `runner.mjs`, `tokens.mjs`, `report.mjs` — core kgbench execution/reporting pipeline
- `kgbench-backfill-tokens.mjs`, `kgbench-repair-attempt-windows.mjs`, `kgbench-verify-report-claims.mjs` — post-hoc repair/verification scripts
- `kgbench-continuation.test.js`, `kgbench-tokens.test.js`, `kgbench-publish-guard.test.js`, `kgbench-report-provenance.test.js` — test coverage for continuation logic, token accounting, publish guards, and report provenance
- `README.md`, `kgbench.md`, `measurement-lessons.md`, `reference_kgbench_attempt_window_attribution.md`, `MEMORY.md`, `compressed-baking-cray.md` — documentation kept in sync with toolchain changes

## Usage
Consulted when assessing whether continuation-budget experiments (cont2/cont2b) are ready for authoritative comparison. Check `supervise.status` first to distinguish "matrix test passed" from "all rows complete" before drawing conclusions from aggregate stats.

## Troubleshooting
- If aggregate comparison numbers look suspicious, verify row completion count in `supervise.status` — partial runs (e.g., 12/48) should only be analyzed via per-row integrity checks, not aggregates.
- If `cont2b` results diverge unexpectedly from `cont2`, re-check whether the run used the current versions of `runner.mjs`/`tokens.mjs`/`report.mjs`, since these are frequently updated in parallel with runs.
- Cross-reference `kgbench-verify-report-claims.mjs` output before publishing any comparison derived from `cont2b`.
