`PROJECT.md` and `ROADMAP.md` serve as the canonical source of truth for the GSD project's current position, completed work, and upcoming phases. They are the first documents to consult when orienting to the project state.

## Architecture
The project organises work into numbered **Plans** (granular implementation units) and **Milestones/Phases** (larger feature or subsystem deliverables). A `km-core` Git submodule exists as a dependency that must be updated in lockstep with host-repo changes. The current known backlog contains three major remaining areas:

- **Phase 33** — Health Monitoring Consolidation
- **Milestone 37** — km-core-foundation
- **Milestone 38** — ontology-registry

## Key Files
- `PROJECT.md` — top-level project description and status overview
- `ROADMAP.md` — milestone/phase tracking; authoritative list of completed and pending work
- `km-core/` — Git submodule; changes here require coordinated commits in both the submodule and the parent repo

## Usage
Consult `ROADMAP.md` at the start of any work session to confirm the current phase and identify the next actionable item. When completing a Plan or Milestone, update both `ROADMAP.md` and any relevant submodule references before merging to `main`.

## Troubleshooting
- If the repo appears out of sync after a merge, run `git submodule update --init --recursive` to realign `km-core`.
- If `ROADMAP.md` and commit history disagree on what has landed, treat the commit history on `main` as ground truth and update `ROADMAP.md` accordingly.
- Unresolved phase ordering questions should be reconciled in `ROADMAP.md` before starting implementation, not during.

topic: Nav Bar Layout — Token Usage Tab Clipping
summary:
## Purpose
Tracks a known UI regression where the navigation bar shifts upward by a few pixels on the Token Usage tab, causing the "Health" nav label to be clipped at the top viewport edge.

## Architecture
- Affects the nav bar component (`nav-bar.tsx`) and its layout container in `App.tsx`
- The clipping is tab-specific — other tabs render the nav bar at the correct position
- The purple hatching visible in browser screenshots is Chrome DevTools gap visualization, not a real background artifact in the app

## Key Files
- `App.tsx` — top-level layout; compare Token Usage tab structure against other tabs
- `nav-bar.tsx` — nav bar component; inspect for conditional styles or margin/padding differences triggered by the Token Usage tab

## Usage
- Bug is visible when the Token Usage tab is active; switching to any other tab restores correct nav bar position
- No fix has been applied; investigation was read-only

## Troubleshooting
- **Nav bar clipped only on Token Usage tab**: Compare the DOM structure and CSS applied to the Token Usage page wrapper vs other tab wrappers in `App.tsx`; look for a missing wrapper div, extra margin, or flex/grid layout difference
- **Purple hatching in screenshot**: This is Chrome DevTools gap highlighting — not a real rendering artifact; disable DevTools overlay to get a clean view

topic: Startup Script and Container Health Check
summary:
## Purpose
Provides a robust container launch sequence for the `coding` CLI and related agents, handling Docker port conflicts, stale container recovery, and health-check waiting.

## Architecture
- `_container_has_unbound_ports()` — detects stale containers with ports occupied by host processes (e.g., a local Next.js dev server on :3030 blocking Docker port publishing)
- `_recover_stale_container()` — force-recreates the container when unbound ports are detected, before entering the health-wait loop
- `_diagnose_unhealthy_services` — returns exit codes (not `exit 0`) for proper error propagation
- **`free-coding-ports.sh`**: host-side utility that identifies and kills processes holding ports needed by the container (e.g., :3030); must be invoked on the host **before** `docker-compose up` — `entrypoint.sh` runs inside the container and cannot intercept host-side port-binding failures
- Health-wait timeout: **30s** (reduced from 60s)
- Host-side health check endpoint: `localhost:8080`

## Key Files
- `scripts/launch-agent-common.sh` — container launch, port conflict detection, stale container recovery, health wait loop
- `free-coding-ports.sh` — host-side port liberation script; kills processes on ports Docker needs

## Usage
`launch-agent-common.sh` is sourced by agent-specific launch scripts and runs automatically when the `coding` CLI starts a session. `free-coding-ports.sh` is invoked by the coordinator or manually when a port conflict is suspected.

## Troubleshooting
- **`coding-services` container stays in `Created` state (never starts)**: A host process is holding port 3030 — run `free-coding-ports.sh` to kill it, then start the container; use `lsof -i :3030` to identify the process manually
- **Health check timeout after Docker crash**: Stale container with unbound ports — the script auto-detects and force-recreates; if still failing, run `free-coding-ports.sh` explicitly
- **`_diagnose_unhealthy_services` not reporting correctly**: Ensure it returns exit codes and does not call `exit 0` directly

topic: Observation Pipeline — ObservationWriter and Deduplication
summary:
## Purpose
Provides a three-layer entity deduplication pipeline (`JaccardNameMatcher → CosineEmbeddingMatcher → LLMSemanticMatcher`) and an `IngestPipeline` orchestrator that chains extract → synthesize → dedup → store stages within the `km-core` library. Satisfies requirements PIPE-01 and DEDUP-01.

## Architecture

**Type contracts:**
- `src/dedup/types.ts` — layer contracts (`Deduplicator`, `DedupResult`, etc.)
- `src/pipeline/types.ts` — pipeline interfaces; imports from `dedup/types.ts`
- `tests/unit/_helpers/fakes.ts` — shared test helpers using direct subpath imports (types not yet re-exported via `index.ts` at time of creation)

**Three dedup layers** (all in `src/dedup/`):
- `JaccardNameMatcher.ts` — Jaccard name similarity; configurable threshold, defaults to 0.85
- `CosineEmbeddingMatcher.ts` — cosine embedding similarity; configurable threshold, defaults to 0.90
- `LLMSemanticMatcher.ts` — LLM-based semantic matching; exports `LLMDedupParseError`; `parseDedupResponse` returns discriminated union `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false }` to distinguish parse failures from canonical empty responses without emitting false stderr warnings
- All three layers: dead self-id guard conditions removed (CR-02); self-match now returns `matched: true, confidence: 1.0`

**`LayeredDeduplicator`** (`src/dedup/LayeredDeduplicator.ts`):
- Chains the three layers in order with configurable `shortCircuit` behavior (Decision D-44)
- Short-circuits downstream layers when an earlier layer produces a definitive match

**`IngestPipeline`** (`src/pipeline/IngestPipeline.ts`):
- `runStage('extract' | 'synthesize' | 'dedup' | 'store', opts)` with 4-overload signatures (collapsed to single lines for grep-acceptance compliance)
- `opts.domain` propagated through all `runStage` calls (CR-04 fix)
- Emits `stderr` warn when entity lacks `ontologyClass` (CR-01 fix); does not silently write
- Documented deviation: `deduplicator.dedup` call returns 2 matches (not spec's expected 1) due to `runStage('dedup')` delegation architecture; noted in `40-SUMMARY.md`

**Gap closures** (Plans 40-08 through 40-11):
- CR-01: `ontologyClass` guard in `IngestPipeline.ts`
- CR-02: self-id guard removal across all 3 matchers
- CR-03: typed `LLMDedupParseError` + discriminated-union `parseDedupResponse` in `LLMSemanticMatcher.ts`
- CR-04: `opts.domain` propagation through `runStage`
- SC#1: `examples/custom-adapter.ts` — downstream reference adapter implementing all 4 stage interfaces with thresholds (0.85, 0.90, 0.70); imports only from `@fwornle/km-core`; resolved locally via `node_modules` symlink (gitignored)

**Test suite:** 153 tests passing across 17 test files after gap closure; `tsc --noEmit` clean.

## Key Files
- `src/dedup/types.ts` — layer type contracts
- `src/pipeline/types.ts` — pipeline interfaces
- `src/dedup/JaccardNameMatcher.ts` — Jaccard layer; threshold 0.85
- `src/dedup/CosineEmbeddingMatcher.ts` — cosine embedding layer; threshold 0.90
- `src/dedup/LLMSemanticMatcher.ts` — LLM semantic layer; `LLMDedupParseError`; discriminated-union parse
- `src/dedup/LayeredDeduplicator.ts` — chain orchestrator; `shortCircuit` option
- `src/pipeline/IngestPipeline.ts` — pipeline; `runStage` 4-overload; CR-01 and CR-04 fixes
- `tests/unit/_helpers/fakes.ts` — shared test helpers
- `examples/custom-adapter.ts` — SC#1 reference adapter
- `.planning/phases/40-ingest-pipeline-layered-dedup/` — 11 plan files (40-01 through 40-11), `40-REVIEW.md`, `40-VERIFICATION.md`

## Usage
Construct `IngestPipeline` with extractor, synthesizer, embedding client, LLM client, and optional dedup thresholds. Call `ingest(entities)` for the full pipeline or `runStage(stageName, opts)` for explicit stage control. SC#4 (co-exist mode second half) is deferred to Phase 42 per Decision D-45. Phase 42 imports this pipeline via the km-core root barrel.

## Troubleshooting
- **Self-match returns `matched: false`**: Dead self-id guard still present — CR-02 removes it; self-match must return `matched: true, confidence: 1.0` for all three matchers
- **LLM parse error spam in stderr for empty responses**: `parseDedupResponse` using old `canonicalEmptyResponse` pattern — verify discriminated-union return type is in place in `LLMSemanticMatcher.ts`
- **`opts.domain` silently dropped**: CR-04 not applied — verify every `runStage` call in `IngestPipeline.ts` forwards `opts.domain`
- **Entity silently skipped with no warning**: CR-01 guard missing — `IngestPipeline.ts` must emit `stderr` warn when `ontologyClass` is absent
- **Custom adapter `@fwornle/km-core` import fails**: `node_modules/@fwornle/km-core` symlink absent — create it pointing to the km-core source directory (equivalent to `npm link`; must be gitignored)
- **`deduplicator.dedup` count unexpected**: Documented deviation — `runStage('dedup')` delegation returns 2, not 1; behavior is correct and documented in `40-SUMMARY.md`
- **grep fails on `runStage` overload signatures**: Multi-line overloads not accepted — collapse each overload signature to a single line

topic: Kgbench Grep vs CodeGraph A/B Experiment — SPA Report Artifact
summary:
## Purpose
The `grep-vs-codegraph.html` SPA is a self-contained report artifact summarizing the grep-vs-graph A/B investigation findings. It must stay in sync with the canonical benchmark report as findings are updated.

## Architecture
- The SPA is generated from a Claude.ai chat thread (not from a local build script); corrections require crafting prompting instructions targeted at that originating thread.
- The canonical source of truth for findings is the published benchmark report/URL; the SPA is a derived artifact.
- Drift between SPA and report is detected by direct comparison of SPA content against the published benchmark URL.
- When drift is confirmed, the remediation path is to translate discrepancies into corrective prompting instructions for the originating Claude.ai thread, then regenerate.

## Key Files
- `grep-vs-codegraph.html` — SPA report artifact; may lag behind the investigation report if findings were updated after SPA generation

## Usage
Consulted as a shareable, standalone summary of the grep-vs-graph experiment. Used when the full benchmark report URL is not convenient to share directly.

## Troubleshooting
- **SPA out of sync**: compare SPA content directly against the published benchmark URL to surface specific discrepancies; do not assume the SPA is current after any report update
- **Correction workflow**: identify the delta, craft targeted prompting instructions for the originating Claude.ai chat thread, and regenerate the SPA; there is no local build script to re-run

topic: Install Test Script — Single-Slot Result Cache
summary:
## Purpose
Avoids redundant container rebuilds across the 18 test shapes by reusing the result of a previous shape when consecutive shapes share identical build inputs, reducing overall test harness runtime.

## Architecture
- **Single-slot strategy**: tracks the last build's output and arguments; if the next shape's inputs match, the harness reuses the cached result instead of rebuilding.
- **Order-dependency flaw**: the default shape execution order (direct → proxy-only → no-egress → arch) causes intermediate shapes to evict the direct result before the arch shape can reuse it, making the last-only cache strategy ineffective for non-adjacent matching shapes. Reordering shapes (or widening the cache beyond a single slot) is required to make reuse effective.
- **Subshell isolation bug (confirmed root cause)**: variable-based caching via `LAST_OUT`/`LAST_ARGS` is non-functional because command substitution runs in subshells that cannot propagate variable assignments back to the parent shell — assignments are silently discarded, so the cache never persists across shape iterations. A file-keyed caching approach (writing cache state to disk rather than shell variables) was staged as the fix, consistent with the "Cache assignment escape failure" pattern documented in the Shell Strict Mode Robustness insight.
- **Missing "reusing" log message**: even when all 18 tests pass (1 build + 7 direct + 3 proxy + 4 no-egress + 3 arch), the expected cache-hit log message does not reliably surface to terminal output. Suspected cause is the message being swallowed by log capture/redirection rather than printed to a live-visible stream — this makes it hard to visually confirm the cache is actually being exercised, independent of whether the underlying caching logic itself is correct.

## Key Files
- Install test harness script (the shape-iteration driver containing the single-slot cache logic and `LAST_OUT`/`LAST_ARGS` variables)

## Usage
Consulted when investigating why the install-test harness takes longer than expected, or when trying to confirm cache hits are actually occurring across shape runs.

## Troubleshooting
- If test runtime doesn't improve despite the cache logic being present, check the shape execution order — the direct→proxy→no-egress→arch default order evicts cacheable results before reuse is possible.
- If cache state appears to reset between shapes despite matching inputs, verify the caching mechanism isn't using shell variables set inside command substitution subshells — switch to file-keyed cache state instead.
- If no "reusing" log message appears even when caching is suspected to be working, don't treat its absence as proof the cache is broken — check whether output is being captured/redirected rather than printed live before debugging the cache logic itself.

topic: coding-v1 Benchmark — Baseline Token Floor Measurement
summary:
## Purpose
Each benchmark arm requires a baseline token floor — the token count consumed by the agent before any task content is added — for token normalization. When a run completes before its floor is measured, a post-hoc measurement and patch workflow is applied via dedicated scripts.

## Architecture
- **Measurement method**: run the agent under the target sandbox commit with no task content; take the median of 3 samples to reduce noise
- **Patch metadata**: affected rows receive a `baseline_post_hoc` metadata block; manifest source is updated to `proxy-db-session (post-hoc)` for auditability
- **Execution ordering constraint**: post-hoc patch must be staged after supervisor exit and before the token backfill runs, to preserve `content_tokens` consistency
- **Floor drift**: grep/copilot floor drift across samples is ~0.6%; grep/claude is ~3.2%; tool grant has no effect on baseline context size
- **Token attribution window bug**: a known bug exists in the window calculation or session-token mapping logic; investigation targets `measure-floor.mjs` and `patch-floor.mjs` as the fix location; root cause is incorrect window calculation or session-token mapping

## Key Files
- `measure-floor.mjs` — executes baseline token floor measurement runs; primary target of the attribution window bug fix
- `patch-floor.mjs` — applies post-hoc floor values to existing result rows; secondary target of the attribution window bug fix

## Usage
Run post-hoc after a benchmark arm completes without a prior floor measurement. Stage the patch before the token backfill step. Results feed into per-cell token normalization in the benchmark report pipeline.

## Troubleshooting
- **Attribution window bug**: if floor values appear incorrect or session-token mapping produces anomalous results, inspect window calculation logic in `measure-floor.mjs` and session inheritance patterns; the bug is under active investigation
- **Floor consistency**: if `content_tokens` values look wrong after backfill, verify that `patch-floor.mjs` was run before the backfill script, not after
- **High drift**: drift >1% across 3 samples suggests environment instability; re-sample before patching

topic: kgbench Benchmarking Harness — Grader and Matcher Logic
summary:
## Purpose
Implements deterministic pre-judge scoring matchers for kgbench cells. Matchers apply string, regex, and structural checks against agent answers before (or instead of) invoking the LLM judge, reducing judge cost and eliminating rubric ambiguity for mechanically verifiable criteria.

## Architecture
**Matcher rules (current enforced state):**
- **Separator folding**: applied only to literal needle matching — never applied to regex haystacks; applying it to regex patterns corrupts the pattern and produces false matches
- **A1 whitespace tolerance**: matcher accepts normalized whitespace variants of the expected answer string
- **F1 criteria**: requires both a store signal AND a failure signal to be present; a single signal alone does not satisfy the criterion
- **Matcher leniency diagnostic**: when checklist scores high and judge scores low in a unidirectional pattern, the matcher is accepting answers that do not satisfy the rubric; the directional pattern (checklist high / judge low) is the canonical diagnostic signal — tighten the matcher to require all necessary discriminating signals

**Judge configurability:**
- Judge is fully configurable via `KGBENCH_JUDGE_PROVIDER` and `KGBENCH_JUDGE_MODEL` env vars
- Default judge model: `claude-opus-4.8`
- Empirical analysis of disagreement cases has consistently traced errors to rubric/key bugs, not judge capability — do not switch judge models as a first response to disagreements

**Blind validation protocol:**
- Before committing any answer key rewrite, validate the new key against stored agent answers to catch false ground-truth changes before they corrupt scored cells
- A bad A2 key rewrite can corrupt up to 24 answers; blind validation catches this pre-commit

**Disagreement reduction (current baseline):**
- Total disagreements reduced to 13; A1 disagreements reduced to 3 via separator folding fix, A1 whitespace tolerance, and f1 signal strengthening
- Further reduction requires per-question rubric tightening guided by judge disagreement case analysis

## Key Files
- `lib/kgbench/graders.mjs` — all matcher implementations; separator folding, whitespace tolerance, and multi-signal criteria enforced here
- `config/kgbench/questions/coding-v1.json` — answer keys; wrong key fields cause silent measurement failure across all arms for the affected question

## Usage
Matchers run automatically during cell scoring in the kgbench harness. Judge is invoked for cells where matchers do not produce a definitive result. Disagreement counts between matcher and judge outputs are the primary signal for rubric health.

## Troubleshooting
- **Unidirectional disagreements (checklist high, judge low)**: matcher is too lenient; identify the discriminating signal the judge is using that the matcher misses and add it as a required criterion
- **Unidirectional disagreements (judge high, checklist low)**: matcher is too strict or answer key is wrong; validate key against stored answers before changing the matcher
- **Separator folding applied to regex**: produces false matches silently; confirm folding logic gates on `isLiteral` before applying
- **High disagreement count after answer key edit**: run blind validation against stored answers before committing; compare matcher and judge scores on the same stored answer set to confirm the key change does not flip correct answers to incorrect
- **Judge producing unexpected scores**: check `KGBENCH_JUDGE_PROVIDER` and `KGBENCH_JUDGE_MODEL` env vars; confirm rubric text in `coding-v1.json` is unambiguous before attributing errors to judge capability

topic: ETM Artifact Aggregation and Async Backfill
summary:
## Purpose
Applies two complementary guards between ETM fire paths and the database: turn-scoped semantic dedup prevents observations from distinct user turns from suppressing each other's content, and snapshot promotion upgrades mid-turn progress checkpoints to finals when a matching final arrives. A third guard explicitly exempts `kind:'progress'` observations from dedup entirely, preventing in-progress snapshots from being collapsed into final turn observations.

## Architecture
**Turn-scoped deduplication:**
- `_turnKeyForSet(promptSet)` generates a stable, immutable identifier derived from the prompt-set's first-exchange ID; survives ETM restarts; consistent for the full lifetime of a turn.
- `turnKey` is injected as metadata into both `_firePromptSetObservation` and `_fireBatchObservation` at the ETM fire path.
- `_isSemanticallyDuplicate` restricts duplicate checks to observations sharing the same `turnKey`; cross-turn observations with identical content are not suppressed.

**`kind:'progress'` dedup exemption:**
- Observations tagged `kind:'progress'` are excluded from the 4-hour semantic dedup filter in both directions: they are not checked against existing records, and existing records are not checked against them.
- This is a prerequisite for the token-delta progress emitter — without this exemption, progress snapshots would be silently collapsed into final turn observations (or vice versa) by the similarity filter.

**Snapshot promotion:**
- `_promoteProgressSnapshot` detects existing `kind:'progress'` records whose content hash matches an incoming final observation.
- Upgrades the progress record to a final in-place rather than inserting a duplicate; no hard deletes, preserving store integrity.

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — contains `_isSemanticallyDuplicate`, `_turnKeyForSet`, `_promoteProgressSnapshot`, and the `kind:'progress'` exemption logic

## Usage
Called transparently by all ETM fire paths. `turnKey` and `kind` metadata must be present in the observation payload for correct behavior; callers are responsible for injecting them before the write call.

## Troubleshooting

metadata.topic: ETM Artifact Aggregation and Async Backfill
metadata.summary:
## Purpose
Applies two complementary guards between ETM fire paths and the database: turn-scoped semantic dedup prevents observations from distinct user turns from suppressing each other's content, and snapshot promotion upgrades mid-turn progress checkpoints to finals when a matching final arrives. A third guard explicitly exempts `kind:'progress'` observations from dedup entirely, preventing in-progress snapshots from being collapsed into final turn observations.

## Architecture
**Turn-scoped deduplication:**
- `_turnKeyForSet(promptSet)` generates a stable, immutable identifier derived from the prompt-set's first-exchange ID; survives ETM restarts; consistent for the full lifetime of a turn.
- `turnKey` is injected as metadata into both `_firePromptSetObservation` and `_fireBatchObservation` at the ETM fire path.
- `_isSemanticallyDuplicate` restricts duplicate checks to observations sharing the same `turnKey`; cross-turn observations with identical content are not suppressed.

**`kind:'progress'` dedup exemption:**
- Observations tagged `kind:'progress'` are excluded from the 4-hour semantic dedup filter in both directions: they are not checked against existing records, and existing records are not checked against them.
- This is a prerequisite for the token-delta progress emitter — without this exemption, progress snapshots would be silently collapsed into final turn observations (or vice versa) by the similarity filter.

**Snapshot promotion:**
- `_promoteProgressSnapshot` detects existing `kind:'progress'` records whose content hash matches an incoming final observation.
- Upgrades the progress record to a final in-place rather than inserting a duplicate; no hard deletes, preserving store integrity.

topic: LLM CLI Proxy — VPN/Corporate Network Detection
summary:
## Purpose
`detectNetworkMode()` determines the active network environment (corporate/VPN/public) at request time so `proxy-bridge/server.mjs` can select the appropriate provider routing strategy. A prior misclassification caused transient coordinator outages to incorrectly degrade the provider chain to "corporate" mode; the function now fails open to `"public"`.

## Architecture
**`detectNetworkMode()` behavior (`proxy-bridge/server.mjs`):**
- <USER_ID_REDACTED> the health coordinator for authoritative network mode when the coordinator is reachable
- **Fail-open**: if the coordinator is transiently unreachable, returns `"public"` — never falls back to a "corporate" heuristic; the coordinator is authoritative **only when it responds**
- Previous behavior (fixed): fell back to a weak "corporate" heuristic on coordinator timeout, unnecessarily restricting the provider chain

**Four network scenarios (traffic-flow diagrams in `coding-history` GHE repo):**
- **Inside CN**: Corporate LAN; PAC → local proxy → central proxy chain; Kerberos/NTLM/OAuth; STRICT POLICY firewall
- **VPN (AnyConnect)**: Corporate proxy routing enforced; `api.anthropic.com` blocked at proxy (HTTP 000); `api.github.com` passes; STRICT POLICY applies
- **No VPN**: Direct internet or Proxydetox fallback; PAC fetch may fail; corporate-only resources inaccessible
- **Mobile Hotspot**: Direct internet; Proxydetox fallback via `127.0.0.1:3128` when direct calls fail

**Proxydetox role:**
- Runs locally at `127.0.0.1:3128`; handles PAC file resolution and proxy chain selection
- Transient offline events emit `ECONNREFUSED`; the retry layer in `server.mjs` absorbs single-occurrence outages before they affect mode detection (see: Provider Architecture insight)

## Key Files
- `proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — `detectNetworkMode()` implementation; fail-open logic
- Traffic-flow diagrams: `coding-history` GHE repo (4 PNG/diagram files for the four scenarios)

## Usage
- Called at request time; result governs which providers are attempted and whether direct-internet paths are considered safe
- Fail-open default (`"public"`) means the system errs toward full provider availability rather than unnecessary corporate-mode restriction

## Troubleshooting
- **Provider chain unexpectedly restricted to corporate mode**: verify coordinator is reachable; if unreachable, mode should now be `"public"` (fail-open) — persistent "corporate" mode while coordinator is down indicates the fix has not applied
- **VPN-mode provider failures for `api.anthropic.com`**: expected behavior — Anthropic's API is blocked at the corporate proxy on VPN per the traffic-flow diagram; this is not a proxy-bridge bug
- **Mode mismatch vs. actual network**: confirm coordinator response; if coordinator is stale or unreachable, mode defaults to `"public"` regardless of actual environment

topic: Knowledge Graph Viewers — VOKB and VKB
summary:
## Purpose
Browser-based interactive visualizations of the operational knowledge graph for exploring entities, relations, and graph topology. Three implementations exist with distinct tech stacks and ontology scopes.

## Architecture
**VOKB:**
- Root: `rapid-automations/integrations/operational-knowledge-management/`
- Stack: React 18 + D3.js + Vite + Tailwind CSS; served on port 3002 via Docker/supervisord

**VKB (sigma.js, legacy):**
- Stack: sigma.js; served on port 8080
- Port 8080 may conflict with `coding-services` health check endpoint — verify before starting

**Unified Viewer (`integrations/unified-viewer/src/`):**
- Stack: React + D3 force-simulation canvas; Zustand for filter state; serves VOKB, VKB, and OKB scopes through a single app
- `D3GraphCanvas.tsx`: `hiddenRelationTypes`/`hiddenNodeTypes` filter memos enforce layer separation; per-edge color lookup via `EDGE_STYLES` (keys must be lowercase/camelCase)
- `relation-types.ts`: viewer-side canonicalizer collapses space/underscore variant pairs before render to prevent duplicate edges
- Filter infrastructure: `viewer-store.ts` (Zustand) + `FilterRail.tsx`, `GraphToggles.tsx`, `TrendingPanel.tsx`, `LegendPanel.tsx`
- `integrations/unified-viewer` is a **regular tracked subdirectory** — not a git submodule

## Key Files
- `rapid-automations/integrations/operational-knowledge-management/` — VOKB application root
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/D3GraphCanvas.tsx` — D3 canvas; layer separation; per-edge color lookup
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/relation-types.ts` — relation-type canonicalizer
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/vokb-palette.ts` — `EDGE_STYLES` palette definitions
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/store/viewer-store.ts` — Zustand filter store
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/api/ApiClient.ts` — API client for graph entity and relation data

## Usage
- VOKB: Docker/supervisord on port 3002; React+D3 stack
- VKB (sigma.js): port 8080; start only after confirming no port conflict with `coding-services`
- Unified Viewer: active ontology scope determines which filter controls are visible (e.g., Layer filter is suppressed for coding-system graphs); all three scopes share the same React app and Zustand store

## Troubleshooting
- **`integrations/unified-viewer` shows unexpected git submodule state**: it is a regular tracked subdirectory — use standard git staging, not submodule commands
- **VOKB port 3002 unreachable**: check Docker and supervisord; restart via `supervisorctl restart vokb`
- **VKB port 8080 conflict**: stop `coding-services` health check before starting the sigma.js VKB server
- **Edge rendering or duplicate-edge issues in Unified Viewer**: see the "VKB Graph Viewer — Ontology Bleed and Entity Integrity" insight for detailed diagnostics on palette key format and canonicalizer coverage

topic: D3GraphCanvas — Bidirectional Graph Selection Component
summary:
## Purpose
Prevents timeline tick clicks from dispatching graph node IDs that are not rendered in the D3 canvas (phantom IDs). When a clicked entity ID has no corresponding rendered node, the system walks the entity's ancestry via BFS to return the nearest visible ancestor. The primary LLS-domination bug — an inverted `capturedBy` edge walk direction in `ancestry.ts` — has been corrected; Option B2 suppression provides defense for residual data-defect cases.

## Architecture
**Root cause of phantom IDs:**
- `LslTimelineStrip.onTickClick` sources the raw entity ID from `entities[0]`, which is a Detail-level Observation entity
- The D3 render pipeline explicitly excludes Observation/Digest/Detail-layer nodes and materializes only structural nodes (Project/Component/SubComponent)
- The sidebar renders phantom entities correctly because it reads directly from the store; `applySelectionStyling` and edge rendering fail silently

**BFS traversal (corrected):**
- `ancestry.ts` previously walked `capturedBy` edges in the inverted direction, causing BFS to terminate at `LiveLoggingSystem` in ~49/75 non-empty buckets
- The corrected walk direction resolves the majority of LLS-fallback misresolutions

**Residual data defect:**
- All Observation nodes carry only a single outgoing relation (`capturedBy → LiveLoggingSystem`); semantic-content edges (`discusses`, `mentions`, `references`) linking Observations to Insights/Components are absent from the ingest pipeline
- For buckets where the data defect applies, even the corrected BFS terminates at LLS; Option B2 (`noiseAncestors`) suppression handles these cases

**Resolution layer:**
- `resolveToVisibleAncestor(entityId, visibleIds)` — entry point in `ancestry.ts`; delegates to `pickFirstResolvable`
- `pickFirstResolvable` — BFS deepest-first traversal with corrected edge direction; returns deepest entity in the ancestry chain present in the visible set
- `pickAllResolvable` — BFS diamond-hierarchy-safe traversal returning all visible ancestors; used for Phase 56.1 many-to-many paths
- `visibility-predicate.ts` — encapsulates the "is this entity rendered?" test
- `useVisibleEntityIds.ts` — React hook exposing the currently-rendered node ID set
- Wiring: `D3GraphCanvas.tsx` and `LslTimelineStrip.tsx` invoke resolution before dispatching to `viewer-store.ts`
- 6th design contract locked in `56-PATTERNS.md` as a permanent architectural constraint

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/ancestry.ts` — `resolveToVisibleAncestor`, `pickFirstResolvable`, `pickAllResolvable`; corrected `capturedBy` BFS walk; `noiseAncestors` Option B2 suppression
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/visibility-predicate.ts` — visibility predicate layer
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/useVisibleEntityIds.ts` — React hook; currently-rendered node ID set
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/graph/ancestry.test.ts` — unit tests for BFS direction, suppression, and `useNodeToBucketsIndex`
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/D3GraphCanvas.tsx` — click handler wired to resolution
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/panels/coding/LslTimelineStrip.tsx` — `entities[0]` raw Detail-level entity source; zero net-new setState calls
- `.planning/phases/56-.../56-PATTERNS.md` — 6th design contract documentation

## Usage
Invoked automatically at click time within `D3GraphCanvas.tsx` and `LslTimelineStrip.tsx` before writing to `viewer-store.ts`. No direct external API — resolution is an internal click-handling step. The corrected BFS direction handles the majority of cases; Option B2 suppression handles residual LLS-fallback. Resolved IDs propagate through selection state to `SidePanel` and the D3 ring/trace renderer.

## Troubleshooting
- **LLS still dominates bucket resolution after BFS direction fix**: verify `ancestry.ts` has the corrected `capturedBy` walk direction; if correct but LLS still appears, Option B2 suppression is not filtering or the data defect applies (no alternate path in stored data)
- **Ring/edge rendering fails silently despite sidebar showing entity correctly**: phantom ID reached the store unresolved; verify `resolveToVisibleAncestor` is called before store dispatch
- **Phantom node IDs reaching the store**: click handler not calling resolution upstream of `setState` dispatch; raw ID from `entities[0]` is Detail-level and will never match a rendered D3 node
- **Visibility predicate returns false for all entities**: `useVisibleEntityIds` returning empty set — verify graph has completed its first render cycle before the hook is consulted
- **Traversal returns shallow (root-side) ancestor**: `pickFirstResolvable` not iterating deepest-first; verify BFS iteration order in `ancestry.ts`
- **Sidebar shows only `LiveLoggingSystem` with no per-tick differentiation**: ring/sidebar decoupling enhancement (show original bucket entity in sidebar while ring anchors to resolved ancestor) is not yet implemented

topic: Mermaid Diagram Rendering Pipeline (MkDocs Material Theme)
summary:
## Purpose
Documents how Mermaid diagrams embedded in MkDocs documentation (e.g. the graphify integration page) are built, rendered, and published, and clarifies why naive DOM-based headless checks for `<svg>` elements incorrectly report rendering failures.

## Architecture
- **Source**: Mermaid diagrams are authored as fenced code blocks (` ```mermaid `) directly inside Markdown source files under `docs-content/` (e.g. `docs-content/integrations/graphify.md`).
- **Build**: MkDocs compiles the Markdown into static HTML under `site/` (e.g. `site/integrations/graphify/index.html`), preserving the diagram as a `<pre class="mermaid">` element wrapped in a `<div class="mermaid">` container.
- **Client-side rendering**: the Material theme renders Mermaid diagrams client-side via `mermaid.min.js`, currently loaded from a CDN pinned to a major version tag. Rendering happens **inside a closed shadow root** — this means external DOM queries for `<svg>` elements are invalid probes and will always report zero rendered SVGs even when rendering succeeded correctly.
- **Verification method**: instead of querying for `<svg>`, confirm rendering by checking that the `<pre class="mermaid">` element was consumed/replaced and that the wrapper `<div class="mermaid">` has non-zero rendered dimensions (e.g. observed 602×768px).
- **CDN dependency risk**: 24 diagrams across 12 pages silently degrade to raw, unrendered code blocks if the CDN-hosted `mermaid.min.js` (~3.4 MB) is unreachable at page load — currently unmitigated. A proposed fix is vendoring `mermaid.min.js` locally via `extra_javascript` in `mkdocs.yml` to remove the CDN dependency and pin the exact version, but this has not yet been implemented.

## Key Files
- `docs-content/integrations/graphify.md` — example page containing Mermaid diagram source.
- `site/integrations/graphify/index.html` — built output containing the rendered diagram markup.
- `mkdocs.yml` — would host the `extra_javascript` entry if `mermaid.min.js` is vendored locally.

## Usage
Relevant when writing or debugging any Markdown page containing Mermaid diagrams under `docs-content/`, and when headless/automated checks are used to verify diagram rendering as part of a documentation build or health check.

## Troubleshooting
- If a headless check reports `renderedSVG=0` for a Mermaid diagram, do not treat this as a rendering failure by default — confirm whether the check is querying past a closed shadow root (invalid) rather than checking `<pre class="mermaid">` consumption / wrapper `<div>` dimensions (valid).
- If diagrams visibly render as raw code blocks (unprocessed fences) on the live site, suspect CDN unavailability for `mermaid.min.js`; check network access to the CDN, and consider vendoring the script locally via `extra_javascript` to eliminate the dependency.
- When auditing diagram health across the site, remember the current scope is 24 diagrams across 12 pages all sharing the same CDN dependency risk.

topic: Code Graph Viewer Feature
summary:
## Purpose
Visualizes LLM provider/model routing decisions as a directed graph within the Token Usage dashboard, giving users an at-a-glance view of which routes are actively used in the foreground versus collapsed background traffic, and the relative volume flowing through each.

## Architecture
- New component `token-usage-flow-tab.tsx` renders routing decisions as a directed graph:
  - 4 foreground routes are shown individually (distinct nodes/edges per route)
  - 31 background routes are collapsed into 3 aggregate targets, avoiding graph clutter
  - Edge thickness is proportional to token volume routed along that edge
  - Fallback routes are rendered as dashed edges to visually distinguish them from primary routes
  - Hover tooltips provide per-edge detail on demand
- Supporting edits made in `providers.ts`, `token-usage.tsx`, and `token-usage-settings-dialog.tsx` to feed routing/provider data into the new tab and integrate it into the existing dashboard page.
- Verified visually in gsd-browser under both light and dark themes; new files pass typecheck cleanly.

## Key Files
- `token-usage-flow-tab.tsx` — the new flow graph component
- `providers.ts` — provider data feeding the graph
- `src/pages/token-usage.tsx` — main dashboard page integrating the new tab (see also "Token Usage Dashboard — Provider and Model Label Normalization" insight for pre-existing normalization logic in this file)
- `token-usage-settings-dialog.tsx` — settings dialog updated to support the new visualization

## Usage
Consumed by dashboard users wanting to understand LLM routing behavior at a glance — which providers/models are actively serving foreground requests, how background traffic is distributed, and where fallback routing is occurring, without parsing raw routing config or logs.

## Troubleshooting
- If the graph appears empty or missing routes, check that `providers.ts` is correctly feeding current routing data (in sync with `proxy-bridge/routing-config.mjs`) into the component.
- If dashed (fallback) edges are missing where fallback routing is known to be active, verify the routing data distinguishes primary vs. fallback edges upstream.
- Verify rendering in both light and dark themes after any styling change, as this was explicitly validated at introduction.

topic: KB-Derived Task Sampler — A/B Experiment Discrimination Rate
summary:
## Purpose
Generates and audits the discrimination rate signal for the KB injection A/B experiment. The audit script validates facts from the ledger dataset via sandbox-based iterative grep, confirming that sampled facts are structurally absent from the sandbox and retrievable from the KB.

## Architecture
- Operates within the `kb-ab` experiment infrastructure; ledger data stored under `.data/kb-ab` (tracked in git)
- **Audit execution**: sandbox-based fact validation via iterative grepping per fact entry; I/O-intensive; no artifacts are modified during an audit pass
- **Discrimination report generation**: executed via Node.js utilities against ledger data; output feeds directly into the measurement report
- **3-fact minimum gate**: tasks producing fewer than 3 derived facts are excluded from discrimination scoring
- **`kb-redundant` outcome**: a distinct result class (neither arm fails) requiring prominent treatment — not collapsed into generic non-discrimination
- **"Neither-solves" pattern**: kb-on passing 1/3 and kb-off passing 0/3 indicates mining reduces but does not eliminate failures
- Proxy service dependency: `localhost:12435/health` must be live before derivation runs; stale availability warnings must be cleared before invoking the sampler
- Built modules: sampler, fact sets, CLI, and discrimination report; validated via 47 passing unit tests with clean eslint output

## Key Files
- `.data/kb-ab` — ledger data directory (tracked in git)
- `lib/experiments/kb-ab-facts.mjs` — fact set definitions
- CLI entry point (discrimination report generator) — Node.js utility invoked to produce structured metrics

## Usage
Run the discrimination report CLI against `.data/kb-ab` ledger to produce metrics for integration into `docs-content/measurement/knowledge-injection-ab.md`. Audit pass confirms fact provenance before reporting.

## Troubleshooting
- Confirm `.data/kb-ab` is git-tracked before committing (`git status .data/kb-ab`)
- If proxy is unreachable, check PID binding at `localhost:12435` before running sampler
- Gate count vs. topic count in output directory is the primary post-run health signal; shortfall indicates upstream mining failure
- Full test suite (577 pass expected) must be green before committing `classify()` contract changes; grep codebase for all referencing tests before finalizing

topic: kgbench Benchmark — Measurement Reliability and Report Integrity
summary:
## Purpose
Documents known threats to benchmark measurement validity in the kgbench coding performance project: system-load noise, ambiguous `"no_result"` cell classifications, baseline isolation constraints, concurrent session corruption, and tally discrepancies that affect report integrity.

## Architecture
- **Result buckets**: `report.mjs` (lines 125–131, 155–160) computes all metrics exclusively over the `"ok"` bucket; `"no_result"` cells are excluded from aggregate scores but still affect token median figures when they represent a large fraction of the underlying sample.
- **Token median skew**: ambiguous `"no_result"` cells can dominate the token sample for a given arm, making the token median unreliable until those cells are resolved.
- **Concurrent session corruption (confirmed)**: two concurrent opencode session sets corrupt attribution bidirectionally. Opencode combos must be scheduled **sequentially** to prevent overlapping time windows from cross-contaminating token count columns.
- **Progress monitoring race condition**: `tail -f` invoked on a log file before that file exists will fail silently or error. Pre-create the log file with `touch <scratchpad-log-path>` before starting the tail operation to ensure reliable progress tracking.

## Key Files
- `report.mjs` — result bucket logic (lines 125–131, 155–160); aggregate metric computation
- `lib/experiments/token-aggregate.mjs` — session-based aggregation; guards against window-overlap corruption

## Usage
Consulted when interpreting benchmark results, diagnosing anomalous token counts, or setting up a new benchmark run. Sequential scheduling and log pre-creation are required operational steps before starting any opencode combo re-run.

## Troubleshooting
- **Corrupted token columns after parallel run**: re-run opencode combos sequentially; inspect `token-aggregate.mjs` output for session overlap.
- **`tail -f` fails on missing log**: run `touch <log-path>` before invoking `tail -f`; do not start the tail after the process has already written and rotated the file.
- **Unreliable token median for opencode**: check fraction of `"no_result"` cells in the sample — if dominant, defer median comparison until cells are resolved.
- **`"no_result"` classification ambiguity**: cells must be manually reviewed to determine whether they represent genuine agent failure or infrastructure/containment faults before being included in comparative analysis.

topic: kgbench Token Attribution Pipeline
summary:
## Purpose
Attributes LLM token usage to individual benchmark cells (arm × question × replicate) within the kgbench harness. The pipeline groups tokens by originating session identifier to prevent cross-cell bleed when a session outlives its process boundary.

## Architecture
- **Attribution model**: tokens are grouped by session identifier (not temporal windows). The previous `byWindow` implementation in `lib/kgb` used time-based windows, which caused false positives in foreign-traffic detection and silent under-counts when a session spanned a cell boundary.
- **Aggregation**: `token-aggregate.mjs` aggregates token rows by session ID; `tokens.mjs` handles per-run token collection within the kgbench pipeline.
- **Reporting**: `report.mjs` source ranking consumes session-attributed token totals; the session model is used consistently across the entire pipeline including tests.
- **Concurrent run isolation**: opencode combos must run **sequentially**, not in parallel. Overlapping time windows across concurrent opencode session sets corrupt token attribution bidirectionally — each session contaminates the other's token count columns. Sequential execution is the required configuration for valid measurement.

## Key Files
- `lib/experiments/token-aggregate.mjs` — session-based aggregation logic (replaces `byWindow`)
- `lib/kgb/tokens.mjs` — per-run token collection
- `report.mjs` — consumes session-attributed totals for source ranking

## Usage
Runs as part of the kgbench benchmark pipeline when closing a measurement span. Token totals feed into per-cell result rows and aggregate report statistics. Sequential scheduling of opencode combo runs is enforced at the harness configuration level before starting a benchmark session.

## Troubleshooting
- **Cross-contamination in token columns**: caused by running opencode combos in parallel; reconfigure to sequential execution and re-run affected cells.
- **Silent under-counts**: symptom of the deprecated `byWindow` path; confirm `token-aggregate.mjs` is using session-ID grouping.
- **Persistent background session during benchmarking**: a background opencode session active during a benchmark run will corrupt attribution bidirectionally; terminate all background sessions before starting a run.

topic: kgbench Skill — Dashboard vs CLI Front-End Capabilities
summary:
## Purpose
Documents which kgbench operations are available from the dashboard front-end versus the CLI, and the operational guardrails that differ between the two entry points.

## Architecture
- **Two front-ends**: Dashboard (browser UI) and CLI (`kgbench-run.mjs`); both operate against the same benchmark matrix and results store
- **CLI-only operations**: `regrade`, `rejudge`, `publish`; `doctor` is partial in dashboard
- **Concurrency guards differ**:
  - Dashboard: one-sided concurrency guard — prevents launching a second run while one is active
  - CLI: run-id-only guard — does not protect against matrix corruption if multiple CLI invocations target the same matrix
- **Cancelled status recipe**: manually writing a `cancelled` status to a cell must follow a documented recipe (CLI-side); dashboard does not expose this operation

## Key Files
- `kgbench.md` — canonical skill documentation; capability comparison table and guardrail descriptions live here
- `CLAUDE.md`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md` — auto-generated from `kgbench.md` via `generate-agent-instructions.sh`; must be regenerated after skill doc changes

## Usage
Consulted when deciding whether to initiate a benchmark operation from the dashboard or CLI. Pre-launch verification (git cleanliness, daemon export currency, question/evidence integrity) should be completed before any run is initiated from either front-end.

## Troubleshooting
- **Matrix corruption risk**: running multiple CLI invocations concurrently against the same matrix is not protected by the CLI guard — use run-id isolation or serialize manually
- **Cancelled cells**: use the CLI recipe to write `cancelled` status; dashboard cannot perform this operation
- **Agent instruction drift**: if `kgbench.md` is updated, re-run `generate-agent-instructions.sh` to propagate changes to `CLAUDE.md` and `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

topic: ETM — Observation Artifacts Field Accuracy
summary:
## Purpose
The ETM daemon consumes active session LSL/JSONL transcript files and writes structured observation records used by health monitoring, the System Health Dashboard, and project tracking surfaces. It runs as a persistent background process; agent work continues independently of ETM liveness, meaning ETM failures silently create gaps in the observation record without interrupting the session.

## Architecture
- **Input**: Active session LSL/JSONL transcript files written independently by the Claude runtime; transcripts accumulate even when ETM is down, preserving a full recovery source
- **Output**: Structured observation records committed to the observation store; consumed by the Health Dashboard observations page
- **Liveness signal**: `lastBeat` (assigned at `health-coordinator.js` line 405) reflects the ETM daemon heartbeat — used by the health coordinator to detect daemon status
- **Critical distinction**: `lastBeat` freshness is **not** a user-activity signal; ETM daemon liveness must not be conflated with user presence in the session

## Key Files
- `scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — ETM daemon process
- `health-coordinator.js` line 405 — `lastBeat` assignment
- `health-coordinator.js` line ~410 — heartbeat payload containing `transcriptPath` (correct user-activity signal source)

## Usage
ETM runs continuously as a background daemon. The health coordinator polls `lastBeat` to surface ETM status on the health dashboard. Recovery after ETM downtime: restart ETM; it reprocesses accumulated transcript files to backfill the observation gap automatically.

## Troubleshooting
- **Observation gaps with no session interruption**: ETM was down; restart it and allow reprocessing from accumulated LSL/JSONL transcripts
- **`userActiveNow()` regression**: If `health-coordinator.js` reads `lastBeat` (line ~405) as the activity signal instead of `transcriptPath` last-modified time (line ~410), probes fire unconditionally whenever ETM is alive — fix by switching the signal source to transcript mtime
- **`lastBeat` stale but ETM process appears running**: ETM is likely stalled; check for STALL-DET events in ETM logs and restart if stall is confirmed

- **Input**: Active session LSL/JSONL transcript files written independently by the Claude runtime; transcripts accumulate even when ETM is down, preserving a full recovery source
- **Output**: Structured observation records committed to the observation store; consumed by the Health Dashboard observations page
- **Liveness signal**: `lastBeat` (assigned at `health-coordinator.js` line 405) reflects the ETM daemon heartbeat — used by the health coordinator to detect daemon status
- **Critical distinction**: `lastBeat` freshness is **not** a user-activity signal; ETM daemon liveness must not be conflated with user presence in the session

## Key Files
- `scripts/enhanced-transcript-monitor.js` — ETM daemon process
- `health-coordinator.js` line 405 — `lastBeat` assignment
- `health-coordinator.js` line ~410 — heartbeat payload containing `transcriptPath` (correct user-activity signal source)

## Usage
ETM runs continuously as a background daemon. The health coordinator polls `lastBeat` to surface ETM status on the health dashboard. Recovery after ETM downtime: restart ETM; it reprocesses accumulated transcript files to backfill the observation gap automatically.

## Troubleshooting
- **Observation gaps with no session interruption**: ETM was down; restart it and allow reprocessing from accumulated LSL/JSONL transcripts
- **`userActiveNow()` regression**: If `health-coordinator.js` reads `lastBeat` (line ~405) as the activity signal instead of `transcriptPath` last-modified time (line ~410), probes fire unconditionally whenever ETM is alive — fix by switching the signal source to transcript mtime
- **`lastBeat` stale but ETM process appears running**: ETM is likely stalled; check for STALL-DET events in ETM logs and restart if stall is confirmed

topic: Experiment Store & Ontology Foundation
summary:
## Purpose
The `/api/experiments/runs` endpoint exposes run metadata for run-selection dropdowns and comparison panels. The human-readable goal sentence is derived during LLM judging and stored on the run entity as `e.description`, but only surfaces in API responses when explicitly included in the `query.mjs` entity projection.

## Architecture
- During LLM judging (`judge.mjs`), goal text is read from archived spans and written onto the run entity as `e.description`
- `query.mjs` controls which fields of the run entity are projected into the API response; without an explicit `e.description` projection, the endpoint returns only `task_hash`, `task_id`, `score`, and related numeric/identifier fields — no goal text
- The `goal_sentence` identifier exists exclusively inside `judge.mjs` archival and scoring logic; it does not propagate automatically to the query layer
- **Fix:** `e.description` must be explicitly added to the run entity projection in `query.mjs` to surface goal text in API responses
- The `goal_achieved` numeric score and the goal sentence are independent fields; the score can be present even when the sentence is absent

## Key Files
- `lib/experiments/judge.mjs` — LLM judging; reads goal text from archived spans, writes to run entity as `e.description`
- `lib/experiments/query.mjs` — run entity projection; controls all fields returned by `/api/experiments/runs`; `e.description` must be explicitly declared here

## Usage
- Consumed by run-selection dropdowns and comparison panels in the performance dashboard
- Goal sentence enables human-readable labeling of runs alongside the numeric `goal_achieved` score
- Called at dashboard load and when users navigate to run-selection or comparison views

## Troubleshooting
- **Goal text absent from UI but numeric score present:** `e.description` is missing from the entity projection in `query.mjs` — add it
- **No `goal` field in API response at all:** expected behavior before the projection fix; verify `query.mjs` includes `e.description`
- **502 on `/api/experiments/runs`:** upstream proxy/server issue; confirm `vkb-server` is running before diagnosing field projection logic
- **`goal_sentence` grep returns no query-layer results:** correct — the identifier is confined to `judge.mjs`; the projected field name in `query.mjs` and the API is `e.description` (or its mapped output key)

topic: Observations API Server — Host-API Pattern
summary:
## Purpose
A standalone host-side HTTP API server that wraps `observations.db`, replacing direct SQLite access from dashboard containers with HTTP forwarding. Follows the established host-API wrapper pattern used for OKB/VKB and LevelDB integrations. Embeds the consolidation runner and Qdrant-based semantic retrieval to avoid multi-process race conditions.

## Architecture
- **Pattern**: Host-API wrapper — server runs on the host, holds the only live connection to `observations.db`, exposes REST endpoints; dashboard handlers inside Docker forward requests via HTTP.
- **Endpoints**: Observation projects, digests, insights, write endpoints, and `/api/consolidation/status` (includes freshness timestamps so the coordinator can poll observation state without opening SQLite directly, avoiding read-write conflicts).
- **Stuck-worker detection**: `_bumpHeartbeat` refreshes `_lastStderrAt` when real stderr has been silent for >30 seconds, preventing false-positive stuck-worker detection during quiet processing periods.
- **Qdrant integration**: Semantic retrieval is co-located in the server process to keep Qdrant queries serialized with the SQLite writer, avoiding concurrent access conflicts.

## Key Files
- Observations API server source — host-side process; sole live connection to `observations.db`
- `observations.db` — SQLite database; must only be opened by the host API server
- `/api/consolidation/status` — freshness timestamp endpoint polled by the coordinator

## Usage
Dashboard containers call this server over HTTP rather than opening SQLite directly. The coordinator polls `/api/consolidation/status` for observation freshness. The consolidation runner executes within the server process to serialize all writes.

## Troubleshooting
- **Dashboard shows stale observations**: Verify HTTP forwarding from container to host API; confirm the server is running on the host.
- **SQLite lock conflicts**: Ensure no process other than the host API server opens `observations.db` directly.
- **Stuck consolidation worker**: Monitor `_lastStderrAt`; if heartbeat is not refreshed during active processing, inspect the 30s silence threshold in `_bumpHeartbeat`.
- **Coordinator shows unknown observation state**: Confirm `/api/consolidation/status` returns valid freshness timestamps.

topic: rapid-llm-proxy Standalone Package
summary:
## Purpose
`@rapid/llm-proxy` is a domain-agnostic LLM abstraction layer shared across OKB and coding projects. It normalizes multiple LLM providers behind a single interface, handles corporate proxy routing, VPN-aware provider selection, exposes a local HTTP proxy bridge for sandboxed Docker consumers, and tracks token usage. `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/` is the single canonical source; `integrations/llm-cli-proxy/` is dead code slated for deletion.

## Architecture
- **Providers** (`src/providers/`):
  - `copilot-provider.ts` — reads the OAuth refresh token from `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` and uses it directly as Bearer; **no token-exchange step**; enterprise vs public routing is selected by API base URL only
  - `claude-code-provider.ts` — CLI-based provider
  - API-key providers: OpenAI, Anthropic, Groq, Gemini, GitHub Models
- **Proxy bridge** (`proxy-bridge/server.mjs`): Local HTTP server for Docker consumers; supports **5 provider backends**: 1 CLI (Copilot) + 4 HTTP (Anthropic, OpenAI, Groq, Gemini).
- **Token tracking**: Aggregates usage counts across all provider calls for reporting.

## Key Files
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/src/providers/copilot-provider.ts` — Copilot OAuth Bearer provider
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/src/providers/claude-code-provider.ts` — CLI-based Claude provider
- `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/proxy-bridge/server.mjs` — local HTTP proxy bridge for Docker consumers
- `integrations/llm-cli-proxy/` — **dead code**, do not use

## Usage
Imported as `@rapid/llm-proxy` by OKB ingestion pipelines, coding agents, and any service requiring provider-agnostic LLM access. Docker-sandboxed consumers point at the proxy bridge's local HTTP endpoint rather than calling providers directly. VPN state determines which backends are reachable.

## Troubleshooting
- **Copilot auth failure**: Verify `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` exists and contains a valid OAuth refresh token; no token-exchange step is needed.
- **Docker consumer cannot reach LLM**: Ensure `proxy-bridge/server.mjs` is running on the host and the container's endpoint is pointed at the bridge.
- **Wrong provider routing on VPN**: Check API base URL configuration — enterprise vs public Copilot distinction is URL-only.
- **Dead code confusion**: All work must target `_work/rapid-llm-proxy/`; ignore `integrations/llm-cli-proxy/`.

topic: Measurement Orchestrator
summary:
## Purpose
Orchestrates the full measurement-stop close pipeline: token aggregation, six flat deterministic heuristics, freeform goal sentence derivation, idempotent route node writes, and LLM judge scoring. Materializes per-run routing decisions, outcome metrics, and scores into the experiment store on `/gsd close`. Exposes two idempotent recompute CLIs for retroactive correction without touching live data. All stop/close requests route exclusively through `vkb-server`'s `/api/experiments/*` endpoints.

## Architecture
Four integrated subsystems wired through `measurement-stop.mjs`:

**Route node writes (idempotent):**
- `/gsd close` writes exactly one Route node per run with a `tookRoute` edge
- Idempotency guard checks for an existing Route node before writing — re-running close never produces a duplicate

**Six flat heuristics** (deterministic, zero-LLM, stored on the `Run` entity):
- `loopCount` — number of repeated execution loops
- Five additional heuristics derived from run telemetry

**Date sorting (defensive):**
- Numeric date comparisons in run ordering use **NaN-last handling** — malformed or unparseable date values sort after all valid dates; prevents undefined ordering or front-of-list pollution from bad inputs

**LLM judge scoring:**
- Freeform goal sentence is derived before the LLM scoring step
- Scores stored on the experiment entity alongside all heuristic fields

## Key Files
- `scripts/measurement-stop.mjs` — full close pipeline: token aggregation, heuristics, NaN-last date sort, route writes, LLM scoring
- `vkb-server/routes/experiments.js` — HTTP endpoints `/api/experiments/*` receiving all close/stop requests

## Usage
Triggered by `/gsd close` during an active experiment run. Two idempotent recompute CLIs allow retroactive correction of stored metrics without altering live run data. All requests must route through `vkb-server`; direct DB writes bypass idempotency guards.

## Troubleshooting
- **Duplicate Route nodes**: idempotency guard was bypassed (e.g., direct DB write); use the recompute CLI to reconcile
- **Run ordering anomalies**: NaN-last guard in date sort prevents malformed values from corrupting order; if ordering appears wrong, inspect run store for non-ISO or unparseable date strings
- **Partial runs (heuristics written, no score)**: LLM scoring is the final stage; an LLM call failure after heuristic materialization leaves this state; recompute CLI can rerun scoring only

topic: ObservationConsolidator — Two-Tier Memory Aggregation
summary:
## Purpose
Generates per-entity structured insight documents for the knowledge base by running LLM analysis over knowledge graph entities. Observations accumulate incrementally across two storage-backend pipelines; insight documents are fully regenerated each consolidation cycle.

## Architecture
**Three distinct data types (not interchangeable):**
- **Observations** — atomic typed facts; appended with deduplication via `persistence-agent.ts` (lines 928–944); never overwritten
- **Insight documents** — per-entity LLM-generated markdown files written to `knowledge-management/insights/`; fully overwritten each run via `fs.writeFileSync`
- **Insight generation results** — intermediate pattern catalogs filtered by significance score; not independently persisted

**Git-log scope — HEAD only:**
- Git reference scanning is restricted to HEAD; scanning all refs is explicitly avoided
- Scanning all refs causes spurious "purple" over-flagging of valid observations (incorrectly marks them as anomalous cross-ref matches)
- HEAD-only scoping is enforced in `ObservationConsolidator.js`

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationConsolidator.js` — consolidation orchestration, git-log scoping, insight document generation
- `persistence-agent.ts` (lines 928–944) — deduplication logic for observation appends
- `knowledge-management/insights/` — output directory for generated insight markdown files

## Usage
Invoked as part of the observation pipeline after entity facts are accumulated. Produces insight documents consumed by the Coverage dashboard and knowledge queries. Runs in full-regeneration mode — prior insight content is overwritten, not merged.

## Troubleshooting
- **Spurious "purple" over-flagging**: caused by git-log scanning all refs instead of HEAD only; verify `ObservationConsolidator.js` restricts log scope to `HEAD`
- **Stale insight content**: insight documents are only as fresh as the last consolidation run; the Coverage dashboard "Refresh" button does not re-run consolidation — trigger a new consolidation pass manually
- **Observation deduplication failures**: check `persistence-agent.ts` lines 928–944; observations are appended, never overwritten — duplicate root causes should be addressed at the ingestion layer

topic: LSL Resolver — resolve-observations-from-lsl.mjs
summary:
## Purpose
Digest entities produced by `ObservationConsolidator.js` were orphaned at the knowledge graph level: inserted via `kmStore.putEntity()` with no subsequent `kmStore.addRelation()` calls, leaving them as disconnected nodes with zero graph edges. Phase 59 ("digest-insight-writer-edge-repair") is the 5-plan, 3-wave repair track that materializes embedded metadata as typed graph relations, backfills 34 historical orphans, and provides a 24-hour soak harness for ongoing orphan-floor monitoring.

## Architecture
- **Write site**: `ObservationConsolidator.js` — `kmStore.putEntity(legacyDigestToEntity(...))` is the primary insertion call; `kmStore.addRelation()` was absent pre-repair, leaving all digest entities with zero edges
- **Pre-repair storage gap**: `observation_ids` and similar fields were stored as scalar metadata rather than typed graph relations
- **`writeInsight` return signature** (Plan 59-01): refactored from scalar `row.id` to `{ legacyId, mintedId }` object; both fields are required for Wave 2 consumer wiring that establishes typed graph edges
- **Phase 59 wave structure:**
  - Wave 1 — Writer/Consolidator edge metadata; includes `writeInsight` signature change and JSDoc update
  - Wave 2 — Consumer wiring and orphan repair; backfills 34 historical orphaned entities; depends on dual-ID return from Wave 1
  - Wave 3 — 24-hour soak harness and runbook
- **Orphan baseline**: `orphanCount=7` measured pre-phase via `GET :3848/api/v1/graph/orphans`; backfill target resolves 34 additional historical orphans

## Key Files
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.js` — `writeInsight` implementation; return value changed from scalar `row.id` to `{ legacyId, mintedId }` in Plan 59-01
- `src/live-logging/ObservationWriter.test.js` — test assertions updated for object return; 12/12 passing post-Wave 1
- `ObservationConsolidator.js` — primary write site; calls `kmStore.putEntity(legacyDigestToEntity(...))`; `addRelation()` calls added in Wave 2
- `.planning/phases/59-digest-insight-writer-edge-repair/59-01-SUMMARY.md` — Plan 59-01 execution summary
- `.planning/phases/59-digest-insight-writer-edge-repair/59-02-PLAN.md` — full phase plan artifact (5 plans across 3 waves)

## Usage
- `ObservationConsolidator.js` is invoked during daily digest consolidation to persist observation entities to the knowledge graph via km-core on `:3848`
- `writeInsight` is called by the consolidator; its `{ legacyId, mintedId }` dual-ID return feeds Wave 2 consumer wiring, which issues the previously-missing `addRelation()` calls to connect entities into the graph
- Ongoing orphan-floor check: `GET http://localhost:3848/api/v1/graph/orphans`; orphan count rising above pre-phase baseline signals new unrepaired insertions

## Troubleshooting
- **Orphan count rising post-repair**: new consolidation runs may be calling `putEntity()` without a matching `addRelation()`; audit `ObservationConsolidator.js` for any `putEntity` call not followed by edge materialization
- **Callers broken by `writeInsight` signature change**: any consumer expecting a scalar ID must destructure the new object; locate affected callers with `grep -r "writeInsight" src/`
- **Test failures in `ObservationWriter.test.js`**: ensure assertions reference `result.legacyId` / `result.mintedId`, not the deprecated `row.id` scalar form
- **Backfill verification**: after Wave 2 lands, re-query `:3848/api/v1/graph/orphans` and confirm the count dropped by approximately 34 from the pre-phase baseline

metadata.scope: Phase 59 repair of knowledge-graph edge materialization in `ObservationWriter.js` / `ObservationConsolidator.js`

topic: obs-api Ontology Registry Sourcing Architecture
summary:
## Purpose
Documents the obs-api ontology class sourcing architecture: a curated host-side directory (`.data/ontologies/obs-api/`) is wired into `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs` with fallback to the bundled `lib/km-core/ontology/` registry. The API serves 50 classes including L1 and L2 types needed by the unified viewer filter and writer-side validation.

## Architecture
- **Active load path**: `GraphKMStore` reads ontology class definitions from `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` at startup, with automatic fallback to the bundled `lib/km-core/ontology/` directory if the host directory is unavailable
- **Host directory contents**: merged `upper.json` (host classes + `LearningArtifact`) plus writer L1/L2 files and viewer L1/L2 files; validated by standalone pre-flight load before wiring
- **Class count**: API serves 50 classes — L1 (`Component`, `SubComponent`, `Detail`), L2 (10 Phase-57 classes), upper-level classes, and writer/viewer domain classes
- **Bundled-only classes**: `Digest`, `Insight`, `Observation` exist in the bundled registry but are absent from the host `upper.json`; writer-side validation for these classes depends on the bundled fallback path remaining active. `LearningArtifact` has been added to the host `upper.json` and is no longer bundled-only.
- **L0 synthesis**: the km-core API handler at port 12436 synthesizes `System` and `Project` L0 anchor classes via `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` + `extends` fallback; this path is independent of the ontology directory sourcing
- **Configuration point**: `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs` line 1336 — `ontologyDir` parameter for `GraphKMStore`

## Key Files
- `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs` — line 1336: `ontologyDir` configuration; currently set to `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` with fallback to bundled
- `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` — active curated ontology directory; contains merged `upper.json` and writer/viewer L1/L2 files
- `.data/ontologies/obs-api/upper.json` — merged L0/L1/L2 hierarchy including host classes and `LearningArtifact`
- `lib/km-core/ontology/` — bundled fallback registry; contains `Digest`, `Insight`, `Observation`; activated when host directory is unavailable

## Usage
obs-api reads ontology classes from `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` at startup; the bundled fallback activates if the host directory is missing. The merged `upper.json` must contain all classes needed for writer-side validation that are not covered by the bundled fallback. When adding new ontology classes, add them to `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` and confirm the class count increases in the API response. Do not remove the bundled fallback path — `Digest`, `Insight`, and `Observation` depend on it.

## Troubleshooting
- **L1/L2 group headers absent from viewer filter**: verify `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` exists and contains the expected L1/L2 files; if the directory is missing, obs-api falls back to the bundled registry which contains no viewer-specific L1/L2 classes
- **L0 group headers (`System`/`Project`) absent**: km-core API handler at port 12436 not running or `HIERARCHY_ROOTS` registry not compiled; this path is independent of the host ontology directory
- **`Digest`/`Insight`/`Observation` writer validation breaks**: these are absent from the host `upper.json`; they depend on the bundled fallback; do not disable or remove the fallback path
- **API serves fewer than 50 classes**: host directory missing, incomplete, or pre-flight load failed; check obs-api startup logs for directory load errors
- **Confirming which ontology path is active**: inspect line 1336 of `scripts/observations-api-server.mjs`; `.data/ontologies/obs-api/` = host (current default), `lib/km-core/ontology/` = bundled fallback

topic: D3GraphCanvas — Unified Viewer Graph Interaction Component
summary:
## Purpose
Provides the D3-based interactive graph canvas in the unified viewer. Responsible for atomic node selection, background-click deselection, bidirectional hover with pulse effect, history-row-driven pan-zoom centering, multi-ring halo rendering, selection-history stacking, and layer fit-to-bounds transitions. Serves as the graph endpoint of the bidirectional selection and hover synchronization loop across all viewer panels.

## Architecture
- **Atomic node-click handling**: all selection state fields updated in a single `setState` call; mirrors the same pattern used in `LslTimelineStrip.tsx`
- **Sibling-clear invariant R2**: node-click must clear `selectedSessionId` and `selectedSessionStartAt` together in the same atomic `setState`; clearing one without the other violates CR-02
- **Bidirectional hover with pulse**: store-driven hover signals propagate in both directions — graph node hover → store → sidebar highlight; sidebar item hover → store → D3 pulse effect on corresponding node; entities filtered out of the current view receive a visual indicator when hovered from the sidebar
- **Background-click (`clearSelection`) routing**: dispatches through `viewer-store.ts`, clearing active selection across all panels
- **History-row-to-graph pan-zoom centering**: reactive effect monitors history-row selection state and pans/zooms the D3 canvas to center the corresponding node
- **Multi-ring halo rendering**: rings rendered on all graph nodes touching the selected tick(s) via `selectedBucketEntityIds` and `selectedNodeTickKeys`; `nodeToBuckets` reverse index stored in `useRef`, read at click time to eliminate stale closures
- **Selection-history stacking**: node selection history maintained in the store; back-navigation across selection states is supported
- **Layer fit-to-bounds transitions**: on layer switch, D3 canvas animates to fit the bounds of the new layer's visible nodes
- **Phase 45 invariant (critical)**: `selectedNodeId` MUST NOT appear in the main render-effect dependency list — causes render loops if violated
- **Zero console.log policy**: `D3GraphCanvas.tsx` contains no `console.log` statements (enforced)
- **Audit contract**: 0 improper `useViewerStore.setState` calls confirmed across all unified viewer components
- **Test coverage**: unit tests (including dedicated hover tests) + 4 Playwright E2E tests; E2E tests drive the store directly and bypass real D3 paint — visual rendering correctness requires human smoke testing

## Key Files
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/D3GraphCanvas.tsx` — D3 graph canvas; atomic node-click; bidirectional hover + pulse; `clearSelection`; history-row pan-zoom; multi-ring halo; selection-history stack; layer fit-to-bounds; Phase 45 invariant enforced; zero console.log
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/components/D3GraphCanvas.hover.test.tsx` — hover behavior unit tests; graph→sidebar and sidebar→D3 signal paths
- `integrations/unified-viewer/src/store/viewer-store.ts` — selection slice including `selectedBucketEntityIds`, `selectedNodeTickKeys`, `selectedBucketKeys`; hover signal fields; `clearSelection` action; `selectedSessionId`/`selectedSessionStartAt` sibling fields
- `tests/e2e/unified-viewer/` — E2E test suite (4+ tests, store-driven, bypass D3 paint)
- `.planning/phases/56-unified-viewer-bidirectional-selection-timeline-scale/56-PATTERNS.md` — 6 state-model contracts; Phase 45 render-effect invariant

## Usage
Rendered within the unified viewer at `localhost:5173/viewer/coding`. Node clicks trigger atomic selection; canvas background clicks clear selection; graph node hover emits a store hover signal consumed by the sidebar; sidebar item hover emits a store hover signal consumed by the D3 pulse renderer; history-row selections trigger pan-zoom centering; tick selection triggers multi-ring halo rendering; layer transitions trigger fit-to-bounds animation. Visual rendering must be verified via human smoke test — E2E tests bypass D3 paint. Use port 5174 when 5173 is occupied.

## Troubleshooting
- **`selectedSessionStartAt` persists after node-click cleared `selectedSessionId`**: sibling-clear R2 violated; both must be cleared in the same atomic `setState`
- **Hover pulse not appearing on graph node when sidebar item hovered**: sidebar→store hover signal not emitted, or D3 pulse effect not subscribed to the store hover field; verify the hover action and the D3 effect dependency
- **Sidebar item not highlighted when graph node hovered**: graph→store hover signal not emitted or sidebar not reading the store hover field
- **Multi-ring halos not rendering on tick selection**: `selectedBucketEntityIds` not populated, or `nodeToBuckets` index stale — verify `useRef` read pattern at click time
- **Layer fit-to-bounds not animating on layer switch**: reactive effect for fit-to-bounds not triggered; inspect its dependency on the layer-switch event
- **Selection-history not enabling back-navigation**: history stack not pushed on node selection — verify push logic in the atomic `setState` block
- **Selection-history or fit-to-bounds absent unexpectedly**: these features were previously reverted by a phantom agent session; confirm commits are present in git history before diagnosing at the code level
- **Render loops after selection changes**: Phase 45 invariant violated — `selectedNodeId` added to render-effect dependency list; remove immediately
- **Background click does not clear selection**: click handler not distinguishing D3 canvas background from nodes; verify `clearSelection` dispatch path
- **E2E tests pass but visual behavior is wrong**: E2E tests bypass D3 paint; only a human smoke test surfaces visual rendering defects
- **Console logs in `D3GraphCanvas.tsx`**: violates zero-log policy; remove before merging
